beans.desc: A Kenyan from a highland washing station on Mount Kenya's slopes, where small growers farm at 1,600-1,800 metres. Cool temperatures and volcanic soil slow ripening, building intricate, mature fruit flavours.

beans.name: Shoondhisa
beans.desc: Thirty-five small farmers from Shoondhisa supplied this lot, processed by Sookoo Coffee in Shakiso. Plots average about 2.5 hectares, often shared with food crops, and communal drying stations help growers without their own facilities earn fair prices.

beans.name: Mayra Solis
beans.producer: Tarrazu, Santa Maria de Dota; Alto El Vapor micromill (Mayra Solis); Catuai
beans.desc: Mayra Solís and her three children run the Alto El Vapor micromill on one of Tarrazú's highest farms, growing produce too, with much land protected. Bean Voyage, a women-focused programme, provides training, seed funding and market access.

beans.name: Las Lajas
beans.producer: Las Lajas micromill (Oscar and Francisca Chacon); Caturra, Catuai
beans.desc: Oscar and Francisca Chacón run a Costa Rican farm from their grandparents. After a 2008 earthquake they borrowed African-style raised beds and helped pioneer honey processing there. This black honey lot dries for weeks in greenhouse piles.

beans.name: Pedro Pastor
beans.producer: Curaren, Francisco Morazan; IHCAFE 90, Lempira, Parainema
beans.desc: Second-generation farmer Pedro Pastor grows this coffee in Curarén, Honduras, at 1,350-1,600 metres in a region of long dry spells. Growers protect water and soil by planting with native and shade trees.

beans.name: Magarciy
beans.producer: Santiago Atitlan, Lake Atitlan; Jose Ramirez and family; mixed varieties
beans.desc: Grown near Santiago Atitlán on Lake Atitlán by a family business named for José Ramirez's father, supporting small Tzutujil farmers under shade. It runs a roastery led by José's son and a café staffed by young local women.

beans.name: Kii
beans.producer: Gichugu, Kirinyaga; Kii Factory, Rungeto FCS; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: From small farmers in Gichugu, Kirinyaga, at 1,600-1,900 metres, where local cultivation dates to 1953 and a typical grower tends 400 trees on a third of a hectare. Processed at Kii Factory by the Rungeto Farmers Cooperative Society.

beans.name: Karogoto
beans.producer: Nyeri, Mathira; Karogoto Factory near Karatina; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: Grown by small farmers in Nyeri's Mathira area at 1,650 metres. About 1,250 members of Karogoto Factory near Karatina contribute, many of them women, each tending about 250 trees alongside maize and bananas.

beans.name: Gihere
beans.desc: Smallholders in Burundi's Ngozi region grow this at high altitude, hand-picking cherries for central processing at Gihere Washing Station, which gives growers access to investment, education and better infrastructure.

beans.name: Gakenke
beans.desc: Smallholders in Kayanza, Burundi farm plots of 1,650-1,950 metres, usually under half a hectare, with bananas, beans and root crops. Ripe cherries go to Gakenke washing station, which helps with funding, training and infrastructure.

beans.name: Elisabete Martins
beans.desc: Run by Elisabete Martins and family, who left 23 years in supermarkets in 2000 to move into coffee. Cherries are laid thinly to dry naturally in the sun, with regular turning for even drying and few flaws.
beans.priceBasis: Listing price, size not shown (likely 250g); unconfirmed

beans.name: Misspent Youth
beans.producer: Elisabete Martins, Fazenda Cachoeira (Brazil, Catuai); Mensur Abahika Jemal, Jimma (Ethiopia, 74110, 74112)
beans.desc: A blend of two naturals: Brazilian Catuaí from Elisabete Martins's family at Fazenda Cachoeira, and Ethiopian 74110 and 74112 from Mensur Jemal, whose 18-hectare Jimma farm joins the Tokuma farmer group.

beans.name: Legoman (Decaf)
beans.producer: Popayan; 65 growers via Cofinet; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A decaf from 65 growers in the Popayán region supplying a programme run by Cofinet, which has worked long-term with these farmers to prioritise quality.

beans.name: Latitude Espresso
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso of Ethiopian Sidama and a Guatemalan lot from Finca Santa Isabel. Crisp, tangy floral first, then juicy berry-like sweetness as it cools, finishing on caramel-toffee.

beans.name: Solitude Espresso
beans.producer: Finca San Lorenzo, San Cristobal Verapaz, Coban (Valdes family); Caturra, Catuai, Sarchimor; 1,550m
beans.desc: An espresso currently from one Guatemalan coffee with gentle acidity and deep sweetness: blackberry, plum and praline. From Finca San Lorenzo, a high-altitude farm near Cobán.

beans.name: Lakes Espresso
beans.producer: Ecoagricola (Flanzer family), Serra do Cabral, Minas Gerais; Yellow Catucai; 1,100m
beans.desc: An espresso currently featuring one Brazilian coffee from the Flanzer family in Serra do Cabral. Chocolate, dried fruit and nuts with a traditional roast profile.

beans.name: Lakes Filter
beans.producer: Ecoagricola (Flanzer family), Serra do Cabral, Minas Gerais; Yellow Catucai; 1,100m
beans.desc: A filter blend of a single Brazilian from the Flanzer family farm in Serra do Cabral. Same beans as Lakes Espresso but roasted more deeply, with chocolate, dried fruit and nut.

beans.name: Decaf
beans.producer: Pergamino blend of four lots, Huila, Cauca and Antioquia
beans.desc: A decaf of four Colombian lots from small farms in three regions, decaffeinated by the sugarcane method. Orange brightness, then cocoa and a toffee close; sweet with chocolate and caramel in milk.

beans.name: El Carmen
beans.desc: An anaerobic natural from a generational family estate at 1,300 metres in El Salvador's Apaneca-Llamatepec range. Juicy lychee, candy-like tropical sweetness and blood orange as it cools, with a long, refreshing finish.

beans.name: Santa Isabel
beans.desc: From a 300-hectare Guatemalan estate, washed and sun-dried. Starts like black tea, then hazelnut bitterness with juicy sweetness, finishing with apricot and bergamot as it cools.

beans.name: Brazil Cerrado
beans.producer: Cerrado and Alta Mogiana; Mundo Novo, Catuai
beans.desc: Grown in Brazil's Cerrado and Alta Mogiana areas at 800 to 1,200 metres, this naturally processed coffee has a smooth, weighty mouthfeel and little tartness. Flavours lean toward chocolate, caramel and nuts, suiting espresso and milk drinks.

beans.name: Colombia Tatacoa
beans.desc: Named after Colombia's Tatacoa Desert, this Huila blend reflects the region's resilience and vibrancy. Its beans grow in fertile soil under strong equatorial sun, sourced through the roaster's own Carcafe operation. Tasting notes lean toward chocolate, stone fruit and caramel.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia Popayan Reserve
beans.desc: Sourced from selected farms around Popayan, milled there, then decaffeinated in Caldas using a sugarcane-derived byproduct and water, avoiding high heat to preserve sweetness. Expect honey, vanilla and chocolate-milk notes with a full body.

beans.name: Union Espresso Blend
beans.desc: An espresso blend with a well-rounded profile and thick, velvety texture. Dark chocolate and caramel sit alongside bright, stone-fruit-like acidity. An even mix of a Brazilian natural and a Colombian washed coffee.

beans.name: Charlestown Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Cerrado (Brazil); Goroka, Eastern Highlands (PNG); Typica, Bourbon
beans.desc: The roaster's most popular espresso blend, named for the neighbourhood where it's roasted. Traditional and full-bodied, it stands up to milk. Cocoa, toffee and shortbread notes lead to a velvety, smooth finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Lalesa
beans.desc: A standout Ethiopian lot from Gedeb, grown under shade at high altitude and hand-picked in the dry season. Cherries ferment nine days in sealed containers before sun-drying. Produced by Ephtah, supporting local families, a childcare centre and women farmers.

beans.name: Colombia Guava Banana
beans.producer: Tolima; El Vergel Estate (Elias and Shady Bayter); Red and Yellow Caturra; 1,350m
beans.desc: Grown by Elías and Shady Bayter at El Vergel Estate in Colombia. Selected cherries ferment in an airtight, oxygen-free setting before sun-drying, giving a full-bodied, layered cup with hints of banana, kiwi and raw cane sugar.

beans.name: Colombia El Indio
beans.desc: A pure Caturra microlot supplied by Cofinet. Only fully ripe fruit was harvested, hand-sorted and sun-dried on raised beds in controlled conditions. Look for blackberry, cherry and a wine-like edge.

beans.name: Edinson Argote SL28
beans.producer: Oporapa, Huila; La Quebraditas (Edinson Argote); SL28; 1,850m
beans.processFull: Double anaerobic washed, yeast inoculated, thermal shock
beans.desc: From La Quebraditas in Huila, where Edinson Argote uses a two-stage fermentation with temperature shocks and added yeast. This SL28 is his third batch with the roaster, with bright herbal, minty flavours evoking a cooling mojito.

beans.name: Jefferson Motta Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: Acevedo, Huila; Jefferson Adrian Motta; Pink Bourbon; 1,700m
beans.desc: Jefferson Adrián Motta of Acevedo, Huila, mixes classic and experimental methods. A natural process on his Pink Bourbon adds sweetness and layered character, giving a lively, wine-like cup best enjoyed black as filter.

beans.name: Fabric Filter Blend
beans.desc: A new seasonal filter blend of two washed African peaberries, one Kenyan and one Rwandan. Vivid blackcurrant and tangerine with a black tea finish; suits pour-over, AeroPress and batch brew.

beans.name: Catanduva
beans.producer: Patos de Minas, Minas Gerais; Marie Nakao; Catuai, Vermelho; 1,080m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Brazilian coffee grown at 1,080 metres in Minas Gerais, rich, sweet and low in acidity. Third-generation producer Marie Nakao emphasises sustainability and regenerative methods. Medium-dark roasted, for espresso fans and newcomers to specialty filter.

beans.name: Finca La Colombia
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; Finca La Colombia via Cafe Lumbus; Caturra; 1,800-2,050m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A full-bodied Colombian from an Antioquia farm, sourced directly from the grower. Raspberry, brown sugar and hazelnut notes, medium roasted for filter and espresso, with moderate brightness and smooth sweetness that works black or with milk.

beans.name: Eden Seasonal Espresso Blend
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A sweet, fruity espresso blend with toffee, honey and woodland fruit flavours. Roasted slightly darker than the single-origin espressos to keep sweetness and depth with little bitterness. The blend's makeup shifts through the year.

beans.name: Cumbres Decaf
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; Cafe Cumbres; Caturra, Castillo; 1,500-1,700m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A naturally decaffeinated Colombian from Café Cumbres, a Cast Iron supplier for three years. Lively, sweet and well rounded rather than diminished, with brownie-like dark chocolate, biscuit and plum; good as espresso or filter.

beans.name: Unity Espresso Blend
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: The house espresso: rich and smooth with mellow acidity, built to taste consistent all year and holding up well in milk for a sweet drink. Roasted only for espresso, suiting black coffee and milk drinks.

beans.name: La Secreta
beans.producer: Antioquia; Finca La Secreta; Caturra Chiroso; 1,980m
beans.processFull: Anaerobic washed (meta text says lactic honey)
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From Finca La Secreta in Antioquia, the roaster's third annual purchase from the farm; this year a washed Chiroso lot. Buttery body and floral character, with zesty tangerine aroma and tropical mango, passion fruit and lychee.

beans.name: La Reserva
beans.producer: Ciudad Bolivar, Antioquia; La Reserva (Carlos Pineda); Geisha; 1,800-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A Colombian Geisha from La Reserva, grown high so the land's character shows. A 96-hour anaerobic fermentation and careful honey process yield a graceful, layered cup with lively sweetness and floral, tropical fruit.

beans.name: Andy Llanos Geisha
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Colasay, Cajamarca; Pluma Dorada (Andy Llanos Delgado); Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Elderflower, Chardonnay, Green apple, Blood orange
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Geisha from Peruvian grower Andy Llanos, whose highland farm in northern Peru's Colasay region shows its potential. Submerged fermentation shapes a complex profile with lively acidity, tea-like body and floral notes.

beans.name: Marcelo Perez
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; Marcelo Perez Pablo (ASDEFLOR); Catuai, Pache, Typica; 1,700m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Smallholder Marcelo Pérez grows this washed Guatemalan in Huehuetenango's high mountains, fermented in open clay tanks without water, then dried on beds and patios. Nectarine and plum with milk chocolate and hazelnut.

beans.name: Gicherori AA
beans.producer: Kibugu, Embu County; Gicherori Factory; SL28, SL34; 1,600-1,800m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From Gicherori Factory, a community-led site in Kibugu taking cherries from about 1,200 smallholders on Mount Kenya's high slopes. Only the ripest are selected, washed and sun-dried, giving a bright, silky cup with a sweet, lingering finish.

beans.name: Pedro Moreno
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: The roaster's debut lot from Pedro Moreno, a pioneer of Santa Bárbara's specialty scene who built his farm from under a hectare and earned several Cup of Excellence podiums. A washed SL28 with lively fruit and crisp acidity.

beans.name: Cumaccha
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Colasay, Cajamarca; Chacra Coffee smallholders; Typica, Caturra, Catimor; 1,700-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Grown by smallholders in Cajamarca, opening with tropical mango and pineapple, then blueberry sweetness and a zesty rhubarb note as it cools. Bright but balanced acidity, soft rounded body and lingering fruity sweetness.

beans.name: Samusure
beans.producer: Nyamasheke, Lake Kivu; family farm; Red Bourbon; 1,800-2,000m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from Nyamasheke, Rwanda, grown at about 1,800-2,000 metres and dried on raised beds. Orange, nectarine and blackberry sweetness with a tea-like, smoky finish. Light-medium roast for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Halo Beriti
beans.producer: Gedeb, Yirgacheffe; Halo Beriti washing station; Typica, Heirloom; 1,900-2,300m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: From smallholders in Gedeb's Ethiopian highlands, fermented without oxygen then dried on raised beds. A juicy cup of strawberry, kiwi and tinned pineapple, with smooth texture and a lingering tropical aftertaste.

beans.name: Gaturiri AA
beans.producer: Kibugu, Embu / Nyeri; Barichu Farmers Cooperative; SL28, SL34; 1,600-1,800m
beans.source: Cast Iron Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Grown by about 1,500 smallholders in Nyeri's cool volcanic highlands, washed and sun-dried. Juicy berry, floral elderflower and zesty citrus, with lively acidity and a tidy, sweet finish.

beans.name: Aftermath
beans.producer: Alfenas, Minas Gerais; Huila; Red and Yellow Catuai, Caturra, Castillo, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Maple syrup, Sugarcane, Florentine
beans.desc: A lively blend of a natural-process Brazil and a washed Colombia: chocolate-coated nuts, bright citrus peel and rich sweetness with a lingering, juicy complexity.

beans.name: Lucid Trance (Decaf)
beans.producer: Popayan (Colombia); Huehuetenango (Guatemala); Gesha, Caturra, Typica, Bourbon, Castillo
beans.listedNotes: Caramel fudge, Praline, Quince, Creme brulee
beans.desc: A decaf blend pitched as nothing like old decaf: a washed Colombian with caramel and praline and a high-altitude Guatemalan with quince and creme brulee, both sugarcane-decaffeinated.

beans.name: Maverick
beans.producer: Oaxaca (Mazatec families); Huila; Typica, Bourbon, Castillo, Tabi
beans.desc: The roaster's 'killer espresso blend': shade-grown Oaxaca coffee from Mazatec families with hand-picked coffee from small high-altitude Huila plots worked by women; dark chocolate, cherry and demerara sugar.

beans.name: Utopia
beans.producer: Nogales Farm (decaf lot); Las Planadas, Huila (Castillo)
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry milkshake, White peach, Acacia honey
beans.desc: A smooth blend pairing Nogales Farm's mosto-fermentation decaf with a washed Castillo from Las Planadas, Huila; strawberry milkshake and white peach with a lingering acacia-honey sweetness.

beans.name: One Piece
beans.desc: Boundary-pushing processing with effortless balance: Jairo Arcila's dragonfruit co-fermented Castillo with a syrupy Las Planadas Castillo; dragonfruit, bubblegum and celeste fig, expressive and clean.

beans.name: Ipanema
beans.producer: Two Brazilian lots; Yellow Bourbon, Red Catuai
beans.desc: Classic Brazilian sweetness with modern specialty character, blending a chocolate, hazelnut and caramel Brazil with a brighter citrus and red-fruit one; layered and approachable.

beans.name: Peach Black
beans.processFull: Peach and wine yeast co-ferment; natural
beans.desc: Two ideas of fruit in coffee: a peach co-fermented Colombian Castillo with a natural Ugandan lot from the Rwenzori Mountains; stone fruit, dark cherry and chocolate that start bright and turn richer.

beans.name: Third Rail
beans.producer: Bekele Kachara, Sidama; Gregorio Espinosa, San Antonio de Chinizo
beans.listedNotes: Ube ice cream, Forest honey, Pecan pie
beans.desc: Ethiopian fruit and floral intensity meets Latin American experimentation: a natural Sidama with a criomacerated Peruvian Catuai; ube ice cream, forest honey and pecan pie.

beans.name: Limited Release #04
beans.desc: A small boxed release of a natural Starmaya, a rare hybrid from El Salvador, chosen by longtime partner Tomas. Floral aromas, a nutty, creamy character and a sweet, lasting chocolatey finish.

beans.name: Revival Classic Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Sertao and Mantiqueira (Brazil); Gaitania, Tolima (Colombia); Los Andes (El Salvador)
beans.desc: A velvety, cocoa-toned blend with deep character and lingering aftertaste, drawing on classic Italian espresso tradition. Works in domestic espresso machines and moka pots, pairing ethical, open sourcing with nostalgic café feel.

beans.name: Ranmore Signature Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Sertao and Mantiqueira (Brazil); Gaitania, Tolima (Colombia); Los Andes (El Salvador)
beans.desc: The flagship blend: dark chocolate, caramel and walnut in a silky, rich cup. Roasted medium-dark as an everyday coffee for espresso, filter or cafetière.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Sertao
beans.desc: A dependable, hearty Brazilian single origin with sweet, cocoa-like, nutty flavour. Praline, hazelnut and chocolate bar notes, balanced and mellow black, with sweetness becoming more pronounced in milk.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca Medina
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan tasting sweet like dark chocolate, with bright orange hints. Smooth and even, making it flexible whether brewed as filter or pulled as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Las Cruces
beans.producer: Quinchia, Risaralda; Finca Las Cruces (Esnayder Cuartas)
beans.desc: A medium-roast Colombian from the Cuartas-Alvarez family's Finca Las Cruces: sweet and lively, with chocolate, toffee and bright grape. Well suited to filter.

beans.name: Indonesia Mandheling
beans.producer: North Sumatra, Lake Toba highlands; smallholders
beans.desc: A deeply roasted Indonesian with flavours of rooibos, cosy spices and gentle tobacco. Strong, heavy body and soil-like character give way to a silky, easy finish.

beans.name: Uganda Bukonzo Dream
beans.desc: Grown at high elevation by small-scale Ugandan farmers and naturally processed. A lively, even cup with bright, juicy acidity, sweet berry-like flavours and a silky, tidy aftertaste.

beans.name: El Salvador El Cipres
beans.producer: Ilamatepec / Santa Ana volcano; Don Tomas; Bourbon; 1,600-1,700m
beans.desc: From El Salvador, with gentle tropical fruit, berry sweetness and a touch of cola. Sweet, even and well rounded, a versatile pick for filter and espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji Shakiso
beans.desc: A light-roast Ethiopian with subtle bergamot-like tea flavours and lively citrus brightness. Sweet, smooth texture, graceful and fragrant; suits drip filters and manual pour-over.

beans.name: Kenya Ngoe AB
beans.producer: Ngoe Farm, Murang'a / Nyeri (Dr Helen Gichohi); SL28, Ruiru 11, Batian
beans.desc: Dr Helen Gichohi grows this washed Kenyan at Ngoe Farm. A lively, juicy cup with red berry and citrus flavours, layered acidity and a silky, wine-like finish that lingers.

beans.name: Natural Decaf
beans.producer: Popayan, Cauca; producer group of ~75 growers; 1,700m
beans.desc: A Colombian decaf with mellow chocolate and malt, a sweet, even profile and crisp aftertaste. Decaffeinated by a sugarcane-based method, well suited to espresso or French press.

beans.name: Half Caf
beans.producer: Decaf component from Cauca producer group
beans.desc: Chocolate and caramel sweetness with a smooth, even finish. Equal parts Ranmore Signature Blend and naturally decaffeinated coffee, giving rich flavour with about half the caffeine of a standard cup.

beans.name: Odds & Ends Blend
beans.desc: A waste-cutting blend using coffee that would otherwise be discarded. Not freshly roasted, but still flavourful and good with any brew method; a mix of the roastery's specialty beans, roasted and combined.

beans.name: Donut Jam - Kenya
beans.producer: Muthuthi-ini factory, Kirinyaga; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11; 1,560-1,650m
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan peaberry, the rounder single-seed bean, from farmers supplying the Muthigi-ini factory. Light roasted for a lively, juicy cup of raspberry jam, wafer biscuit and sweet pastry.

beans.name: Go Go Juice - Burundi
beans.desc: A light-roast natural red bourbon from many small Kayanza farmers in Burundi. Cherries are floated, sorted and dried slowly for weeks; the washing station supplies growers with seedlings and compost. Strawberry yogurt, iced sweets and chamomile.

beans.name: Static Cherry - Ethiopia
beans.producer: Megadu, Guji; Bette Buna; 74112, 74110, Wild Guji Megadu
beans.listedNotes: Cherry syrup, Orange wine, Um Bongo
beans.desc: An Ethiopian natural from Bette Buna's Megadu site in Guji. Cherries dry a day on covered beds, then ferment four days in sealed, oxygen-free containers, giving a deep, rich cup of cherry syrup and orange wine.

beans.name: Juicy Pants - Colombia
beans.producer: El Portal, Palestina, Huila; Yoiner Mosquera; Geisha; 1,700m
beans.desc: A light-roast natural Geisha from Yoiner Mosquera's farm in Palestina, Huila, settled by his grandfather in 1949. Yoiner left banking to run the estate after his father died. Mango, jelly beans and hibiscus.

beans.name: Fizzy Drop - Ethiopia
beans.desc: From the Worka Wuri washing station near Gedeb, grown high from heirloom varieties and sun-dried about two weeks. A juicy, floral cup with jasmine, lemonade and parma violet notes.

beans.name: Liquid Amber - Guatemala
beans.desc: A fully specialty-grade Guatemalan from producer Elmer Meléndez. Anaerobic natural processing gives a rich, indulgent profile layered with blackberry, port wine and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Waffle Wizard - Honduras COMSA
beans.producer: COMSA collective; Parainema, Lempira, Typica, Ihcafe 90; 1,250-1,700m
beans.desc: A washed Honduran from COMSA, a producer group founded in 2001 with over 1,500 farmers. Members focus on organic farming, hand-pick ripe cherries, then ferment, wash and dry them on raised beds.

beans.name: Highwire Coffee Blend
beans.desc: The roaster's flagship blend, built to work as espresso and as a smooth, satisfying filter. It pairs a Brazilian coffee with a Ugandan one, each roasted to bring out its best.

beans.name: Temple Arches Dark Roast Blend
beans.desc: A dark-roast blend giving the deep, full-bodied richness dark roasts are known for, without the usual harshness. It reflects the roaster's own distinctive take on dark roasting.

beans.name: CaraNut Swirl - Brazil
beans.producer: Fazenda Mio, Monte Santo de Minas (Freitas family); Bourbon, Catuai; 900-1,000m
beans.desc: From Fazenda Mió in Monte Santo de Minas, a high-altitude, women-led Brazilian estate focused on sustainability. Satellite imagery traces each lot, and a third of the land is preserved forest.

beans.name: Cola Comforts - Colombia
beans.producer: Northern Tolima; CDNT collective; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: Organically grown cherries are hand-sorted, pulped, fermented, washed and dried 10-18 days in curved greenhouses. The result is a tidy cup that reflects the strength of small farming families in Planadas.

beans.name: Mellow Moon - Colombia Decaf
beans.producer: Huila, Tolima; smallholders; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia; 1,500-1,700m
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced decaf from small farms in Huila and Tolima, decaffeinated with ethyl acetate, a compound found in ripe fruit. Beans are steamed and soaked to remove about 97% of caffeine; residue is below banana levels.

beans.name: Value Blend - Everyday Coffee
beans.producer: Lucky dip of lots incl. natural gesha, natural Maragogype, washed typica
beans.desc: A budget-friendly, zero-waste blend of leftover coffee from past roasts, some up to eight weeks old, including natural gesha, natural Maragogype and washed typica. An everyday coffee that still tastes good.

beans.name: Old Chapel Signature
beans.producer: Not shown (meta text says Uganda and Colombia)
beans.desc: The 2024 charity coffee, with profits going to Old Chapel Music CIC, a Leeds rehearsal studio that has helped launch bands and offers music education to disadvantaged people. Praline, chocolate and nougat.

beans.name: The Baron (Bruno's Pick): Fazenda Inhame
beans.producer: Cerrado Mineiro, Campos Altos, Minas Gerais; Fazenda Inhame (Marco Aurelio Fiorita Franco and son Bruno, family farm since 1910)
beans.desc: A smooth, dependable espresso with chocolate and nut notes and clean sweetness; works with milk or black.

beans.name: The Estate: Fero
beans.producer: Sidamo; Fero Washing Station (Ranger Coffee, 700+ growers)
beans.desc: The roaster's signature espresso: bright, balanced and complex; smooth black, creamy like a jaffa cake in milk.

beans.name: Broadway Blend: El Salvador & Guatemala
beans.producer: 50/50: Las Ranas, Santa Ana, El Salvador; El Durazno, Jalapa, Guatemala (Ventura family)
beans.desc: Seasonal espresso blend, balanced and sweet; the roaster's go-to for flat whites.

beans.name: The Fields: Santa Cruz
beans.processFull: Natural, 72h sealed-tank ferment, about 25 days drying
beans.brew: Espresso, filter and other grinds offered
beans.desc: Part of the adventurous range, named after London Fields; 250ha farm with 95ha in coffee and the rest forest reserve.

beans.name: The Decaf: La Plata
beans.producer: La Plata, Huila; Crecert women-led cooperative
beans.processFull: Washed; sugar-cane EA decaffeination in Colombia
beans.brew: Espresso, filter and other grinds offered
beans.desc: A decaf chosen for flavour and lower-impact processing; caffeine removed in-country.

beans.name: Finca Grevillea
beans.producer: Marcala, La Paz; Melvin Mauricio Calix and mother Victorina, Finca Grevillea
beans.processFull: Natural, whole cherries sun dried 15-25 days
beans.brew: Espresso, filter and other grinds offered
beans.desc: A natural microlot from a third-generation farmer; hand-picked cherries dried whole in the sun. Fruit-forward with a molasses sweetness.

beans.name: Uraga
beans.producer: Guji; Uraga Raro washing station (400+ smallholders)
beans.desc: Bright, fruity washed coffee; the roaster's favourite for filter and cold brew.

beans.name: El Witano
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; Marvin Soliz, El Coyegual, San Antonio Huista
beans.brew: Espresso, filter and other grinds offered
beans.desc: Bright, fruity coffee from a family farm sourced since 2016; cool conditions build sweetness.

beans.name: Suspension Espresso
beans.producer: Fazenda Pinhal, San Antonio do Amparo, Sul de Minas (Gabarra family)
beans.listedNotes: Malted milk biscuits, peanut butter, 80% dark chocolate
beans.desc: A well-balanced, easy-drinking espresso named after Bristol's Clifton Suspension Bridge, full of depth and flavour.

beans.name: Village Organic
beans.producer: La Paz; COMUCAP cooperative of about 200 women farmers
beans.desc: An organic house espresso from the COMUCAP women-farmers cooperative in La Paz, Honduras.

beans.name: E1 Project Espresso
beans.producer: Finca Buena Vista, Ahuachapan (Ricardo Lima family)
beans.desc: From Clifton's first direct-trade partnership (2015) with the Lima family in El Salvador; one of their most popular coffees.

beans.name: Cadence Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Black cherry, baker's chocolate, Earl Grey
beans.desc: A seasonal natural espresso (changes every 3-6 months) with black cherry sweetness and a light Earl Grey character.

beans.name: Sundown
beans.producer: Decaf from Finca San Luis and Finca Santa Martha; caffeinated from Cafetos de Segovia
beans.desc: A half-caffeine blend of a decaf and a full-caffeine Nicaraguan lot, for slow mornings, afternoons and espresso martinis.

beans.name: Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Finca San Luis and Finca Santa Martha, San Ramon and La Corona
beans.desc: A sweet, comforting, balanced sugarcane decaf from two family-run Nicaraguan farms.

beans.name: House Filter
beans.desc: A house filter from the revitalised 780-hectare Mount Sunzu estate in northern Zambia, solar-irrigated beside reforested Miombo forest.

beans.name: Colombia - Las Flores Caturra Chiroso
beans.producer: Finca Las Flores, Acevedo, Huila (Vergara family)
beans.desc: An elegant, floral, fruit-driven Caturra Chiroso from Finca Las Flores, fermented in five stages.

beans.name: Ethiopia - West Arsi
beans.producer: Bishan Guracha washing station, Worka (Nensebo), West Arsi, Oromia; about 250 smallholders
beans.desc: A bright, refined washed Ethiopian from around 250 smallholders, slow-dried on raised beds.

beans.name: Honduras - Finca La Valentina
beans.producer: Finca La Valentina, Montecillos, La Paz (Carlos Ernesto Mejia)
beans.desc: A honey-processed lot from the 25-hectare Finca La Valentina, shaded by citrus and Japanese plum trees.

beans.name: Nicaragua - El Diablo
beans.producer: Cerro Datanli-El Diablo Natural Reserve, Jinotega; smallholders (farms average 20 ha)
beans.listedNotes: Orange peel, dandelion and burdock, maple syrup
beans.desc: Grown on steep slopes under cloud forest in the Cerro Datanli-El Diablo Natural Reserve; hand-picked, fermented 36-48 hours in tiled tanks and dried on raised beds for 30-45 days.

beans.name: Mexico - Sierra Mazateca
beans.producer: Sierra Mazateca, northern Oaxaca (Huautla de Jimenez); small family farms
beans.desc: Grown on small family farms of 1-5 hectares under cloud-cover shade in the Sierra Mazateca.

beans.name: Brazil | Cafe Delas, COOPFAM
beans.producer: Poco Fundo, Sul de Minas; Cafe Delas female smallholders; Catuai, Mundo Novo, Topazio
beans.desc: A bold South American coffee from near Poço Fundo with full body, dark chocolate and caramelised sugar. Suits filter and single-origin espresso; part of each sale's profit funds gender-equality programmes for women farmers.

beans.name: Colombia | Planadas
beans.producer: Planadas, South Tolima; 1,042 growers in 23 groups; Colombia, Castillo, Caturra
beans.desc: A Planadas lot from Tolima in Colombia's Central Andes, a region the roaster has sourced from for five years. Local growers use time-honoured methods; past conflict left some areas underserved, and specialty markets are now opening doors.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia
beans.producer: Huila and Tolima; Castillo, Caturra, Colombia
beans.desc: A popular decaf that keeps plenty of flavour despite gentle, chemical-light decaffeination. Grown in Huila and Tolima, with chocolate, redcurrant and lime, and about 97-99% caffeine free.

beans.name: Guatemala | Magdalena Camaja Cafe Delas
beans.producer: Cubulco, Baja Verapaz; Magdalena Camaja Cafe Delas; Catimor, Caturra, Marsellesa, Parainema, Sarchimor
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from Magdalena Camaja with caramel-glazed apple, malt and cocoa. Part of a scheme sourcing only from female growers, with profits reinvested in gender-equality work and childcare and schooling during harvest.

beans.name: Guatemala | Blue Ayarza - Natural
beans.producer: Lake Ayarza, Santa Rosa; smallholders; Bourbon, Catuai, Pache, Anacafe14, San Ramon
beans.desc: A natural from growers around the Ayarza mill in Santa Rosa. The mill buys ripe cherries and processes them centrally, drying on a sunny hillside then in a mechanical dryer, improving acidity and avoiding rain damage.

beans.name: Indonesia | Cahayani Gayo
beans.producer: Gayo Highland, Aceh; Ara Cahayani Gayo co-op (~500 smallholders); Gayo 1, 2, 3
beans.desc: A wet-hulled Sumatran from a cooperative in Aceh's Gayo Highlands, with chocolate, lemonade and nut notes. Cherries are hand-picked, pulped, fermented overnight, sun-dried, hulled, dried further and hand-sorted.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea | Kongo B
beans.desc: From Kongo Coffee, a locally owned exporter in Simbu, Papua New Guinea, supporting small farmers since before 2000. Its Simbu Project pays 20% above market plus quality bonuses and funds local schools and roads.

beans.name: Peru | San Ignacio
beans.producer: San Ignacio; COOPAFSI; Bourbon, Catimor, Catucai, Caturra, Pache, Typica, Mundo Novo
beans.desc: From COOPAFSI, a cooperative founded in 1968 uniting sixteen committees of small growers across several districts. It helps them reach buyers and provides social and microfinance support, aiming for sustainable, internationally recognised farming.

beans.name: Rwanda | Huye Mountain
beans.producer: Huye District; David and Family Mill; Bourbon
beans.desc: Founded in 2012 by David Rubanzangabo, Huye Mountain supports over 1,300 growers with training and small loans for equipment and inputs. Cherries are hand-sorted, density-separated in water, then sun-dried on raised beds for three to four weeks.

beans.name: Rwanda | Sholi Single Mothers lot
beans.producer: Muhanga, Cyeza; Aba Sholi Women's Co-op; Bourbon; 1,800-2,000m
beans.desc: From an all-female collective within a co-operative started in 2008 by thirty women in Muhanga; it now has 721 members and supports local schools and healthcare. A high-grown washed Bourbon reflecting that community focus.

beans.name: Uganda | Rwenzori Mountains
beans.producer: Kalingwe, Rwenzori; Agri Evolve (350+ farms), Kisinga station; SL14, SL28, Catimor; 1,500-1,800m
beans.desc: Uganda has built a strong specialty reputation. The roasters visited the Rwenzori Mountains and have sourced here for five seasons; small growers on the southern slopes sell to a local station and are paid fairly.

beans.name: East Gate | Light Roast Blend
beans.desc: A light-roast blend of Brazilian, Colombian and Ugandan coffees with caramel, milk chocolate and stone fruit. Retains brightness and sweetness, suiting milky drinks while shining in cafetière or AeroPress.

beans.name: Jacob's Well | Medium Roast Blend
beans.producer: Ara Cahayani Gayo (Bener Meriah); Finca Buena Vista, La Entrada; Marsellesa
beans.processFull: Indonesia wet hulled; Nicaragua anaerobic natural
beans.desc: A medium-roast blend of two specialty coffees with bold body that holds up in milk. Walnut, caramelised toffee and dark cocoa, with a fuller, longer finish tempering the sweetness of the lighter blends.

beans.name: Solomon's Porch | Fairtrade Blend
beans.producer: Aba Sholi Kundwa women's co-op; San Ignacio; Planadas
beans.desc: Named for a temple gathering place open to everyone, a dependable daily blend of Fair Trade beans from Rwanda, Peru and Colombia, showing chocolate, nut and plum.

beans.name: Fireside | Dark Roast Blend
beans.desc: A blend for black coffee drinkers, built to shine alone since dark roasts can hide poor beans. 100% arabica from Brazil, Peru and Colombia, tasting of milk chocolate, almond and butterscotch.

beans.name: Brazil
beans.desc: A Brazilian that's a roastery favourite: moderate in strength and richness with a nicely harmonised flavour. Versatile across brew methods and pleasant at any time of day.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.desc: A Colombian showing the well-rounded, rich profile the origin is known for, with typical chocolatey, nutty notes. Easygoing and hard to brew badly, so use whichever method you like.

beans.name: El Salvador
beans.desc: An El Salvador with rich body, plenty of flavour and gentle acidity, capturing the origin's mellow sweetness. Recommended as a strong choice for flat whites.

beans.name: Honduras Abeja Honey
beans.desc: A honey-processed lot from the Capucas collective in Honduras, grown at one of the country's highest elevations among local beekeepers and their hives. Only 100 bags were produced, so it sells out quickly.

beans.name: India
beans.desc: A single origin packed with spice, smoke and dark chocolate, a roastery favourite. India was among the first origins shipped to the UK. Suited to a leisurely weekend brew in a French press.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.roastNote: "Rainbow roast" mix of light, medium, dark
beans.desc: A decaf for those going caffeine-free, made with the Swiss Water method from South American beans. Roast levels range light to dark, so it suits any brewing approach. Honey, walnut and dark chocolate flavours.

beans.name: The Every Day Blend
beans.desc: A robust blend of the roaster's favourite coffees from South America, India and East Africa. Versatile enough for a bold morning brew or an after-dinner espresso.

beans.name: The Morning After Blend
beans.desc: Equal parts East African and Indonesian beans for a sharp, citrusy jolt aimed at groggy mornings. Good for recovering from a late night and makes a strong Americano.

beans.name: The Weekend Blend
beans.desc: A blend of quality beans from South America, India and East Africa for unwinding after a busy week or a relaxed weekend brunch. Chocolate, smoke and hazelnut flavours.

beans.name: Yorkshire Blend
beans.desc: Blended from South American, Indian and central African beans, with bold cocoa, smoke and hazelnut flavours for any time of day. Each sale also supports Herriot Hospice Homecare, which provides free end-of-life care at home.

beans.name: Fairtrade Italian Espresso
beans.desc: An espresso blend of 100% Fairtrade arabica from Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia and Sumatra. Brazil and Colombia give generous crema and even flavour, Ethiopia a citrus lift, Sumatra body. Small-batch roasted, with almond, malt and cocoa notes.

beans.name: Fairtrade Peruvian
beans.producer: Puno, Tambopata and Inambari valleys; CECOVASA; Tipica, Caturra, Catimor; 800-2,000m
beans.desc: A Fairtrade single-origin arabica from Peru made for slow mornings. Gentle nut and toffee notes finish with a sugary, milky cocoa sweetness; smooth yet full-bodied and comforting.

beans.name: Fairtrade Brazilian Super Crema
beans.desc: An everyday blend of Fairtrade arabica and robusta from a Brazilian cooperative in Minas Gerais. Small-batch roasted, with nutty, caramel and dark chocolate notes, smooth body and lively acidity, suited to many brew methods.

beans.name: Fairtrade Honduran
beans.desc: A Fairtrade single-origin 100% Arabica from a Honduran cooperative with over 700 members who gain fair pay and community support. Balanced and smooth, with hints of nuts and caramel, especially in milk.

beans.name: Fairtrade South American House Blend
beans.desc: A house blend of Fairtrade Brazilian and Honduran beans, roasted in small batches. Brazil brings a zesty edge, Honduras robust nuttiness and a velvety finish. Nut, toast and spicy liquorice notes.

beans.name: Fairtrade Colombian
beans.processFull: Handpicked, fermented, dried on beds and patios
beans.desc: A classic dark-roast Colombian, sweet and fruity in the Medellín style. 100% Arabica, low in acidity, from smallholder farms through local cooperatives and sourced with ethics and sustainability in mind.

beans.name: Fairtrade Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.desc: A Fair Trade Ethiopian from high-altitude Sidamo, where farmers intercrop with shade trees. A bright, fruity medium roast with citrus hints, small-batch roasted for freshness.

beans.name: Fairtrade Organic Swiss Water Peruvian Decaf
beans.desc: A Fairtrade organic decaf with nutty peanut and chocolate notes and subtle citrus, decaffeinated by the chemical-free Swiss Water method. From the Cenfrocafe co-op in northern Peru, where Fairtrade helped growers build processing facilities and go organic.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Pinhal
beans.desc: A mixed-harvest Brazilian dried with the cherry around the bean, giving the sweetness Brazil is known for. Bright fruit over creamy cocoa, ending in toasted nuts. Medium roast makes it smooth and balanced, especially as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia ACC - Attia Castillo
beans.producer: Piendamo, Cauca; ACC co-op community lot
beans.desc: A distinctive honey-processed Colombian with zesty lime and tart green apple, dark chocolate notes and a crisp, bittersweet finish reminiscent of tonic water. Light roast suits pour-over; medium suits espresso and cafetière.

beans.name: Colombia Atunkaa Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Piendamo, Cauca; ACC; sourced by Siruma
beans.desc: A naturally processed sugarcane decaf from a small association in Piendamó, Cauca. Caffeine is gently removed with ethyl acetate at Descafecol, preserving sweetness. Balanced and easy-drinking with apple, lemon and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Costa Rica Los Cipreses Geisha
beans.producer: Los Cipreses, West Valley (Max Salazar and family)
beans.desc: A bright, juicy, fruit-forward washed Geisha, clean and lively.

beans.name: Guatemala La Bolsa
beans.producer: La Libertad, Huehuetenango; Finca La Bolsa; Caturra, Bourbon
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from La Bolsa farm at 1,800 metres, grown from Caturra and Bourbon. Juicy blackberry and bright apple lead into mellow caramel and milk chocolate, with black tea adding structure and a sweet finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji G1 Fruit Jam
beans.desc: A lively natural from Megadu in Guji with cherry, blueberry and ripe mango, crisp acidity, thick sweetness and a dark chocolate finish. A 120-hour low-oxygen fermentation intensifies the fruit. Medium suits espresso, lighter suits pour-over.

beans.name: Kenya Gatomboya
beans.producer: Gatomboya washing station; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan of SL28, SL34 and Ruiru 11: bright, citrusy and sweet, with pink grapefruit, baked apple and smooth toffee. Medium roast suggested for espresso, lighter for fruity pour-over.

beans.name: Black Gold No.3
beans.producer: Fazenda do Salto, Sul de Minas (Catuai); Finca Serbia, Ilamatepec (Bourbon)
beans.desc: The roaster's first blend and the heart of the business: an award-winning seasonal espresso designed for wide appeal and served daily in their café. Roasted past first crack for a lively, chocolatey, biscuity taste.

beans.name: Candle Light No.1
beans.desc: A house espresso whose bean origins rotate through the seasons to keep its character consistent. Deep dark chocolate with a faint hint of toffee, for those who prize richness.

beans.name: Anthracite No.2
beans.producer: Rwenzori Mountains; SL14, SL28; Agri Evolve
beans.desc: A natural-process espresso with juicy, fruit-forward character, aiming for flavours you wouldn't normally link with coffee. Lively and layered, with fruit, blossom and wine-like notes; a three-star Great Taste Award winner.

beans.name: The Union No.4
beans.desc: The roaster's first blend designed for filter, refined over months of tasting at its Ammanford roastery. Sourced from Uganda's Mount Elgon, with gentle sweetness, mid-weight body and notes of blackcurrant, orange and cocoa.

beans.name: Drifft No.6 Half Caff
beans.producer: Muungano, South Kivu (decaf); Fazenda do Salto (natural)
beans.desc: A half-caff blend of beans from two farms: smooth and balanced with about half the caffeine, for a calm, steady day without jittery peaks or crashes. The name mixes Welsh heritage with a nod to a drift mine entrance.

beans.name: Jenkin Jones Decaf No.5
beans.producer: Simbu / Eastern Highlands; smallholders; Typica, Bourbon
beans.desc: A decaf named for a Welsh coal figure, blending beans from Simbu and the Eastern Highlands of Papua New Guinea. Water-based decaffeination; limestone soils add structure and volcanic earth richness. A mellow, polished cup.

beans.name: Catanduva
beans.producer: Fazenda Catanduva, Cerrado Mineiro (Marie Nakao); Catuai, Bourbon; 1,000m
beans.desc: A natural from a third-generation Brazilian family farm in the high Cerrado at about 1,000 metres, whose grandparents emigrated from Japan. Orange, molasses and cashew chocolate notes.

beans.name: Nguguini PB
beans.producer: Kirinyaga; Nguguini factory, Kibirigwa; SL28, SL34, Ruiru 11, Batian; 1,600m+
beans.desc: A lively Kenyan peaberry washed lot from a cooperative-linked factory in Kirinyaga above 1,600 metres. Sweet blackcurrant, gentle chamomile and zesty tamarillo, with bright acidity and a long, tidy aftertaste.

beans.name: El Oso
beans.desc: A Peruvian grown high in San Ignacio by an organic cooperative that helps protect spectacled bear forest. Blackberry, cacao nibs and agave; sweet and lively as filter, thick and fruity as espresso.

beans.name: Unearthed Vol 3 - Orange Bourbon
beans.processFull: Washed, yeast inoculation and thermal shock
beans.desc: The third Unearthed release, a single origin from Edinson Argote's Quebraditas farm in Huila, Colombia. Positioned as a homage to scarce coffees, blending story, terroir and craft for adventurous newcomers and experts alike.

beans.name: Matazano
beans.producer: Finca El Matazano (Elvin Castillo); Lempira, Ihcafe 90; 1,400-1,450m
beans.desc: From a 5-hectare Honduran farm at about 1,450 metres, shaded by timber and fruit trees, produced by national cupper Elvin Castillo. Cherries rest a day and a half, then dry ten days on raised beds, giving a sweet, clear, layered cup.

beans.name: Finca Serbia
beans.producer: El Congo near Lake Coatepeque (Fernando Lima); Bourbon; 1,000m
beans.desc: From a farm founded in 1930 near El Salvador's Santa Ana volcano, on nutrient-rich volcanic soil. Cedar, oak and balsam shade help against intense sun, and rust-resistant varieties spared the estate the 2012 outbreak.

beans.name: Deep Winter
beans.producer: Cerro San Juan, Nayarit; Grupo Terruno Nayarita; Bourbon, Catuai
beans.desc: A warming seasonal coffee with chocolate, caramel and brown sugar notes, grown by cooperative farms on volcanic slopes near Cerro San Juan in Nayarit, Mexico. A smooth, sweet option for chilly days.

beans.name: Candy Cane
beans.desc: A festive seasonal coffee, lively and cheerful, with juicy citrus, mellow sweet pear and cosy wine-like warmth. Zesty brightness meets tender fruit and soothing spice for a joyful holiday cup.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.origin: Brazil and others (Cerrado Mineiro, Bahia, Santa Rosa)
beans.desc: A modern take on a traditional house-style blend whose recipe shifts with the seasons while staying silky, chocolatey and indulgent. Cocoa, sweet citrus peel and toffee; works with or without milk.

beans.name: Brazil
beans.listedNotes: 65% cocoa milk chocolate, Tropical fruit, Shortbread
beans.desc: Bahia's high-elevation growers have ideal conditions but wet harvest weather makes drying hard, so many truck their cherries about 50 km to the drier Caatinga. The fruit ferments briefly in the enclosed truck, giving a fruity, sweet cup.

beans.name: Colombia El Buho EA Decaf
beans.producer: Caparaó, Minas Gerais; Geographic Indication project (15 municipalities)
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate (65% cocoa), ripe cherry, toffee
beans.desc: A Great Taste 2025 award-winning sugarcane EA decaf from the Caparaó mountains.

beans.name: Guatemala
beans.producer: Santa Rosa, Ayarza mill; Catuai, Pache, Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Ripe citrus, Toffee, 65% cocoa milk chocolate
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from a central cherry mill in Ayarza that pays extra for ripe fruit from many local growers, easing the consistency problems of small-farm processing. Producer Francisco Nájera, 30, with under a hectare, is one of them.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea Arufa AX
beans.desc: Grown in Jiwaka Province, this natural starts as cherries from the Kindeng mill. Monpi selects the best and sun-dries them for a month before hulling. Bright acidity and full body with dark berries, honey, stone fruit and caramel.

beans.name: Ethiopia Worka Sakaro
beans.producer: Worka Gedeb; Worka Sakaro washing station; Heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Wild blueberry, Red grape, 65% cocoa milk chocolate
beans.desc: A top-tier small-batch Ethiopian from the Worka Sakaro processing site in the Worka community, Gedeb. Its natural-process cherries underwent an extended three-day fermentation sealed in vacuum bags.

beans.name: Ethiopia Tigst Boru Kochere
beans.listedNotes: Peach crumble, 65% cocoa milk chocolate, Dried apricot
beans.desc: A premium fully washed Kochere lot from the Worka Gedeb region, made from heirloom varietals and ranked among the roaster's top lots.

beans.name: The Battersea Blend
beans.producer: Typica, Bourbon, Batian, SL28, Catuai, Ruiru 11, Pache
beans.desc: An award-winning blend of Malawi, Guatemala and Papua New Guinea for a lively, harmonious brew. Juicy citrus, mango and blueberry, softened by deep chocolatey richness and a buttery biscuit finish.

beans.name: Ethiopia Supernatural
beans.desc: An Ethiopian with lush, jam-like stone fruit alongside floral and chocolate hints and a rich, smooth mouthfeel. Cherries dehydrate slowly in deep beds within partially permeable enclosures, deepening fermentation for a sweeter, more layered cup.

beans.name: Tanzania Ibero PB
beans.desc: From Tanzania's Jipemoyo district, washed using traditional methods and a Great Taste winner. A berry-led tang of blackcurrant and gooseberry settles into a creamy toffee finish.

beans.name: Heritage Blend
beans.producer: Sumatra Lintong; Monsoon Malabar; Santos Mantiqueira
beans.desc: Blended by roasters Jason and Eric to mark founder John Green's retirement after 45 years in the trade. Three origins give earthy depth, gentle spice and natural sweetness; medium-dark, warm and smooth with walnut and biscuit.

beans.name: Cafe Creme
beans.desc: The company's signature espresso, based on a recipe founder John Green found about forty years ago. Versatile and easy to pull, giving a robust shot that suits milk. The best seller, always roasted fresh.

beans.name: Brazilian & Costa Rica 80/20
beans.desc: A smooth yet sophisticated blend of Brazilian Daterra beans from Petit Soleil with all-Arabica Costa Rican. Deep cocoa and treacle with a lively sparkle; an Italian-style espresso for cafés and home machines.

beans.name: Hamburg Roast
beans.desc: Roasted a little darker than medium, blending Brazil, India and Ethiopia. Balanced acidity, chocolate and caramel, and a smooth, full body make it good for espresso and an excellent flat white.

beans.name: Mocha Italian
beans.desc: A popular café-style espresso without robusta, for a distinctly Italian character. 100% Arabica from Colombia, Mysore and Ethiopia: full body, low acidity, clean finish, chocolate and caramel; good with milk.

beans.name: Italia Creme
beans.desc: An espresso blend of nine parts Arabica to one part Indian cherry Robusta, giving a rich, aromatic cup with full body, creamy texture and golden crema. Balances intensity, aroma and bitterness.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea
beans.producer: Aiyura Valley, Eastern Highlands; Sero Dan Bebes, Besser farm
beans.desc: From Sero Dan Bebes' 40-hectare Eastern Highlands farm, where cool air, volcanic soil and slow ripening add complexity. Blue Mountain and Typica trees grow under native Casuarina shade. Suits many brew methods, best as espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: Grown chemical-free by Yohanes Ageze and family on their 4-hectare farm in Idido. Only ripe red cherries are hand-picked and hand-sorted, then dried on raised beds for two weeks.

beans.name: Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Floral, Full body, Low acidity
beans.desc: A washed Sidamo from southern Ethiopia, grown high with ample rain and fertile soil. Full body, sweet layered flavours, gentle acidity and a flowery scent; versatile for filter, espresso or milk, and the boss's favourite.

beans.name: Guatemala (Black Honey)
beans.desc: A Guatemalan processed by the Black Honey method, leaving fruit residue on the beans as they dry. Sweeter and richer, with berry, citrus and caramel, full silky body and bright acidity.

beans.name: Rwanda
beans.producer: Rebero lot, Kinini washing station (633 farmers); Bourbon; 1,973-2,250m
beans.desc: A Rebero lot from 633 farmers supplying the Kinini washing station on north-facing slopes above 1,973 metres. Cherries arrive the day they're picked and are repeatedly fermented and soaked before drying, giving a crisp cup.

beans.name: Andean Sisters - Peru
beans.desc: Grown on small farms in Peru's Cajamarca highlands. Smooth and balanced with chocolate and nutty notes and gentle brightness; good as espresso, in milk drinks or as filter.

beans.name: Decaf (Colombia)
beans.desc: One of the roaster's favourite decafs, equally good as espresso or filter, with low acidity and full, rich body. Caffeine is removed with steam and a solvent, then re-steamed and roasted, leaving no chemical trace.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf (Peru)
beans.desc: A decaf using the organic, chemical-free method first developed in Switzerland in the 1930s. A concentrated green-coffee liquid draws out only the caffeine, so the beans keep their original taste.

beans.name: Liberatrix - Gran Colombia
beans.desc: The long-standing flagship blend that launched the roaster's coffee journey. Large, high-grown Colombian beans with Brazilian give a round, full-bodied cup with caramel, a zesty citrus finish and suitability for nearly any brew method.

beans.name: Regina - Santos
beans.desc: A blend of two Brazilian varieties: Oberon for creamy, nutty chocolate and Yellow Bourbon for sweet, fruity character. A smooth, low-acid cup with a pleasing finish, suited to press or filter.

beans.name: Hotfoot
beans.listedNotes: Orange peel, berry jam, rich chocolate, cocoa finish
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, stovetop, V60, AeroPress, Chemex, French press
beans.desc: A punchy, balanced, vibrant medium-roast blend.

beans.name: Mellow Mare - Mexico Mountain Water Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa, Praline, Brown sugar, Orange marmalade
beans.desc: A decaf from Veracruz processed at Descamex with Pico de Orizaba mountain water, removing caffeine without chemicals. Gentle, rounded body with sweet cocoa, light caramel and juicy fruit.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Yirgacheffe G2
beans.listedNotes: Forest fruits, Brown sugar, Citrus, Floral
beans.desc: A washed Yirgacheffe medium roast and team favourite: forest fruit, brown sugar and citrus, floral aroma and bright, juicy acidity. Suits filter and makes a distinctive espresso.

beans.name: Mexico - El Jaguar
beans.desc: A lush, silky Mexican with bittersweet cocoa and caramelised sugar flavours and a zesty citrus finish. Works as filter or strong espresso.

beans.name: Guatemala - Huehuetenango SCA 83+
beans.desc: A sweet, even-keeled Guatemalan with hints of ripe strawberry, rich chocolate and bright tropical fruit. Grown in frost-sheltered, clay-rich highlands; brews cleanly through filter or as espresso.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Guji
beans.desc: A wild, complex Guji with jammy blueberry, bright honey and zesty bergamot. Juicy and tea-like as filter, richly layered as espresso. Whole sun-dried cherries from high-altitude smallholders add intense fruitiness.

beans.name: Kenya - Gachika SCA 87
beans.producer: Gachika factory, Kimaratia FCS, Kiambu; SL28, SL34, Batian, Ruiru 11; 1,600-1,800m
beans.desc: A lively, layered Kenyan and roasters' favourite with juicy cherry, sweet aroma and crisp acidity. Works as pour-over and espresso.

beans.name: Colombian Bucaramanga
beans.desc: A Colombian from Bucaramanga, known for a rich, smooth character and layered flavour. A balanced, easygoing cup with cocoa-like warmth and subtle nutty sweetness that lingers.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: A Yirgacheffe hand-harvested from small local farms, then washed and dried with care. Its fruity character suits all brew methods; the roaster recommends a morning filter to show its natural purity.

beans.name: Peruvian Tunki
beans.desc: An organic coffee from Peru's high Tambopata Valley, farmed by hand without chemicals by Quechua and Aymara families. Smooth and rich with chocolate, berry and nutty tones.

beans.name: Breakfast Favourite
beans.desc: A smooth, well-balanced blend with a long finish, moderate body and little spice. A bestseller roasted in large daily batches, good in milky drinks or black via paper filter, cafetière or drip.

beans.name: Guatemala El Fogon
beans.desc: A Guatemalan arabica with an easygoing, widely appealing cup: gentle spice, silky cocoa and faint berry scents. Softer body suits many methods, and the roastery uses it in three of its five blends.

beans.name: Costa Rican Tarrazu Valley
beans.desc: A Tarrazú coffee that's sweet, clean and beautifully balanced, especially for filter and AeroPress. The roaster credits strict national standards and supervised exports for its quality.

beans.name: Monsoon Malabar
beans.desc: An Indian coffee named for a slow drying process: beans rest in airy west-coast barns where damp monsoon sea winds swell them. Small-batch roasted, with espresso recommended.

beans.name: Everyday Espresso
beans.desc: An espresso blend for café-style taste without the harshness of robusta. 100% arabica from Brazil, Guatemala and Colombia, suited to espresso machines, filter or AeroPress, and to lattes and cappuccinos.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: Indonesian beans that once served as ship ballast. Aged green for at least two years, they deepen in flavour and lose acidity. A polarising, earthy, spicy cup with a long finish.

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.desc: A Sumatran with blue-tinted, glossy beans grown on volcanic soil. A deep, intense cup with robust character and complexity, leaning toward cocoa, earth and warm spice.

beans.name: Italian Stallion Blend
beans.desc: An Italian-style blend of deeply roasted beans with robusta for those craving strength. Thick, velvety crema and deep cocoa character, holding up in lattes and cappuccinos with an extra caffeine lift.

beans.name: Nepalese Mount Everest - Nuwakot (Washed)
beans.desc: A single-estate Nepalese lot from Lekali Coffee Estate in Nuwakot, grown under shade and harvested mid-season. Washed with glacial meltwater, dry fermented, double-soaked and shade-dried for a layered, smooth, balanced cup.

beans.name: Roaster's Choice - Seasonal Crop
beans.desc: A rotating selection chosen by the roastery team: a mix of exceptional coffees that its roasters themselves drink most, each with its own character.

beans.name: Colombian Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Colombian decaf from the Bucaramanga region: smooth and clean with rich chocolate, gentle nutty sweetness and a well-rounded finish. Swiss Water decaffeination keeps the flavour intact.

beans.name: Mexico Siltepec El Jaguar
beans.producer: Chiapas; small producers; Catuai, Bourbon, Caturra; 1,250-1,350m
beans.desc: A long-time bestseller from a cooperative of small farmers growing at high elevation in Siltepec, Mexico. Roasted for a smooth, chocolate-forward cup without bitterness.

beans.name: Galapagos San Cristobal Hacienda El Cafetal
beans.desc: Grown in the Galápagos Islands, about 1,000 km off South America. Output is small, about half from volcanic San Cristóbal. A fragrant cup with caramel, chocolate, tobacco and spice.

beans.name: Peru Mountain Water Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Nutty, caramel, chocolate; soft citrus acidity
beans.desc: A smooth, naturally sweet decaf with chocolate depth and caramel notes.

beans.name: Nicaragua Blueberry & Pineapple Candy
beans.producer: Hacienda Santa Luz, La Bastilla; H3
beans.desc: A lively, experimental Nicaraguan with bold, fruit-led character: confectionery-like sweetness, a crisp, refined tang and layered berry and tropical notes from inventive processing.

beans.name: Kenya Kisii Estate Peaberry
beans.producer: South West Kenya near Lake Victoria; peaberry
beans.desc: A Kenyan peaberry from the south-west near Lake Victoria, an area of well-organised cooperatives. Washed and sun-dried, with blackcurrant and stone fruit, lively acidity and richness without harsh notes.

beans.name: Nicaraguan Jinotega - Community Project
beans.desc: A silky, lively Nicaraguan from Jinotega with milk chocolate and nutty flavours, brightened by gentle apricot sweetness, from small-scale growers favouring eco-minded methods.

beans.name: Ecuador Loja Co-operative
beans.desc: A freshly harvested Ecuadorian from a farmers' co-operative of small producers in Puyango, Loja. Zesty brightness, juicy body and notes of stone fruit and chocolate.

beans.name: Indonesia Kalossi Toraja Grade 1
beans.desc: A rare coffee grown on volcanic soil near Mount Sesean in Sulawesi, raised by ten Toraja families in small home gardens and processed by hand. Distinctive aroma, rich creamy body and subtle spice.

beans.name: Decaf Roaster's Choice - Seasonal Crop
beans.desc: A rotating decaf selected by the roastery team, who drink their favourites from the range themselves, with each month's crop bringing its own character.

beans.name: Sumatra Wahana Estate Rusana Natural
beans.desc: Dried inside the cherry, this Sumatran has a sweet brown-sugar character with rich spiced molasses notes, a lingering aftertaste and substantial mouthfeel.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Sofia Screen 19
beans.producer: Belen de Umbria, Risaralda; 30 small producers
beans.desc: Back in stock: a large, rich bean with heavy body, sweet banana toffee pie flavours and a silky finish, supplied by thirty small farmers in Colombia's western Andes.

beans.name: Zambia Keteshi Estate Mbuni Natural
beans.desc: A Zambian with a lively citrus-like tang that gives way to rich, liquor-tinged fruit as the brightness mellows. Full-bodied, typical of premium African beans, and a current house favourite.

beans.name: Peru Queromarca Community
beans.producer: Queromarca, Callayuc, Cajamarca; Aromas del Valle co-op (22 farmers)
beans.desc: A versatile cup with crisp profile and mild brightness: milk chocolate, gentle candied citrus and toffee. Good as filter and as espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Finca Las Mercedes La Isla
beans.producer: Southwest Antioquia; Finca Las Mercedes (Guerra family)
beans.processFull: Washed; double fermentation (25h anaerobic, 25h aerobic); African beds
beans.desc: A Finca Las Mercedes Caturra from high-altitude western Colombia, hand-picked and double-fermented before drying. Lively and sweet with plum and lemon, silky texture and clean finish.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca El Borbollon Red Bourbon
beans.producer: Santa Ana; Alvarez family; El Borbollon mill; Red Bourbon
beans.desc: Bright, lively acidity with full body and deep, rich flavour: milk chocolate and a hint of stone fruit. In milky espresso drinks it stays layered yet smooth, with caramel sweetness leading.

beans.name: Brazil Nossa Senhora da Aparecida Natural
beans.producer: Poços de Caldas, Minas Gerais; Nossa Senhora da Aparecida family farm
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, cherry liqueur, soft acidity
beans.desc: A smooth, easy-drinking single-origin from a family farm with 50+ years in coffee.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca El Platanillo Gesha Natural
beans.desc: A Gesha prized for quality, with berry and tropical fruit flavours and a sweet finish. Silky and lively; best as filter or cafetière, though a short ristretto also works.

beans.name: Mystery Coffee Mark 18
beans.desc: The roaster praises this coffee's estate and quality but keeps its origin, identity and flavour secret. The low price is subsidised, mimicking blind tasting and protecting farms from having produce sold cheaply under their names.

beans.name: Sweet Bourbon Espresso Blend
beans.origin: Not shown (Bourbon base with Asian coffees)
beans.desc: An espresso built to enhance crema and sweetness, using Bourbon beans as the base with unusual Asian coffees. Toffee, chocolate and almond with a sweet finish; the roastmaster often prefers it for lattes and cappuccinos.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Malabar Hit
beans.producer: Monsoon Malabar base; Java Lingtong; Sidamo; Ipanema
beans.desc: Related to the Jampit Hit but darker and different in personality. Indian Monsoon Malabar gives full body and dark chocolate, malty, slightly spicy notes, mixed with three other origins. A dark roast for espresso or milk.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Jampit Hit
beans.desc: A darker blend centred on full-bodied Java Jampit. Ethiopian Yirgacheffe adds blackcurrant fruit and acidity, Brazilian pulped natural a creamy texture. The deep roast stays mellow, with chocolate and citrus-tinged spice.

beans.name: Brighton Lanes Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Created for a Brighton café wanting less sharpness: deep, full flavour for espresso, filter, AeroPress and cafetière. 100% arabica from Brazil, Peru, India and Kenya, with smooth chocolate notes and mild acidity.

beans.name: Hill and Valley Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Created by a longtime friend of the Roastmaster, Charlie the Coffeeman, who favours bold Sumatran character. A quick, forceful roast draws out caramel and treacle that hold up in milk. The shop's top-selling dark espresso.

beans.name: Mediterranean Mocha Espresso
beans.desc: A distinctive, smooth, full-bodied espresso with subtle chocolate notes and rich crema, good straight or in milk drinks and long popular with cafés and home brewers.

beans.name: Mahogany Roast Sucker Punch Hit Decaf Blend
beans.desc: A darker, fuller decaf for drinkers wanting intensity: Swiss Water Sumatra with CO2-decaffeinated Ethiopian Sidamo. Sweet chocolate notes and a smoky, bold finish from its mahogany roast.

beans.name: Colombia Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Colombian decaffeinated by Swiss Water: beans soak in water with dissolved coffee compounds for about twelve hours, removing nearly all caffeine while preserving flavour. Nutty and sweet.

beans.name: Sumatra Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Sumatran decaffeinated by the chemical-free Swiss Water method, soaking about twelve hours to remove almost all caffeine. It copes well with the process, keeping its bold, earthy richness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: An Ethiopian Swiss Water decaf: premium beans steeped in caffeine-free liquid so the stimulant leaves and taste remains. Lively, zesty and flowery with traces of green tea and a light close.

beans.name: Costa Rica Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Costa Rican Swiss Water decaf, soaked about twelve hours in coffee-enriched water to remove nearly all caffeine. A crisp, tidy cup with full body, chocolatey hints and a lasting aftertaste.

beans.name: Guatemala El Hato CO2 Decaf
beans.producer: Finca El Hato, Santa Rosa (Verena de Rasch); 1,200-1,450m
beans.desc: Restocked decaf the roastery considers a match for its caffeinated coffees: a fully washed lot from El Hato in Santa Rosa. Candied citrus and mango, ending on caramel; smooth and very drinkable.

beans.name: Guatemala Swiss Water Decaf
beans.desc: A Guatemalan decaf made by soaking top beans in pure water about twelve hours, removing about 99% of the caffeine. Typical Guatemalan character: well rounded, lively acidity and delicate floral notes.

beans.name: 1984 Espresso Blend
beans.desc: The first product Coffee World released, dating from 1984 and still popular. Modelled on traditional Italian espresso, bold and sweet, like a cocoa drink with roasted nuts.

beans.name: Supremo Blend
beans.desc: Named for the Colombian Supremo bean at its core: gentle, silky and rich, with moderate, coating tartness giving way to chocolate biscuit and brown sugar. Versatile across brew styles.

beans.name: Fairtrade Artisan Blend
beans.desc: The best-selling espresso blend, 100% Fairtrade. Rich and soothing, with sweetness like smooth dark chocolate and caramel-dusted hazelnuts, for drinkers wanting a robust cup with gentle acidity.

beans.name: Blue Mountain Blend
beans.desc: Inspired by Jamaica's celebrated Blue Mountain coffee, offering similar appeal: rich, full body with thick caramel, bitter cocoa, subtle herbal undertones and cooked red fruit. Tasting it beside the real thing is suggested.

beans.name: Continental Blend
beans.desc: The deepest-roasted, sturdiest blend in the range, 100% Arabica from lower-elevation Brazil and Guatemala. Mellow sweetness and low acidity with bold, bittersweet dark cocoa and treacle, heavy-bodied with a punchy finish.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.desc: A signature everyday blend and longtime favourite, recommended as a silky, rich filter brew with cocoa, sweetness and gentle citrusy brightness evoking a fruit-and-nut chocolate.

beans.name: Brazil Brigadeiro
beans.producer: Mantiqueira de Minas; Santa Caterina (Marco Valerio Inacio Silva)
beans.desc: A single Brazilian farm's Arara coffee from a producer who keeps reinvesting in his land. Full and sweet, with cocoa, toasted nut and dried fruit balanced by fruit and acidity; suits espresso and filter.

beans.name: Brazil Minas Gerais
beans.desc: A Minas Gerais coffee; the region, whose name means 'General Mines', produces more than half of Brazil's coffee, and many farms have turned to modern irrigation to boost yield and quality.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.desc: From mountainous Bolívar, Colombia, grown at 1,200-2,600 metres in volcanic soil with heavy rain and a warm climate. Washed, medium roasted, with milk chocolate, caramel and green apple.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: An Ethiopian, from the country often seen as coffee's original home. Growers farm much as they did centuries ago, with some plants wild among forest trees and others cultivated in gardens.

beans.name: Mengesha Derso
beans.desc: A natural lot from Gedeo farmer Mengesha Derso on volcanic soil, one of the traceable single-farmer lots made possible by direct cooperative ties. Jasmine, lemon candy and apricot.

beans.name: Mexico Decaf
beans.desc: Small-scale growers in northern Chiapas, Mexico, deliver harvests to buying stations in San Cristóbal de las Casas and Yajalón. Farms sit at 900-1,100 metres, mostly planted with varieties that yield sizeable, smooth-textured beans.

beans.name: Guatemala
beans.desc: A Huehuetenango coffee: hot, dry Oaxacan air meets cool mountain breezes, creating microclimates that shield cherries from frost as they ripen slowly, adding sweetness and the region's chocolatey flavour.

beans.name: Honduras
beans.desc: From San Andrés in Lempira, a lesser-known Honduran area with volcanic soil and high farms. Growers process beans on their own land, so each lot reflects their choices. Spiced berry and rich dark chocolate.

beans.name: Uganda Masaba
beans.desc: A Ugandan from Masaba, contributing to the Friends of Mothers Initiative, which works to reduce gender-based pay inequality in Uganda's coffee trade with over 200 women across seven villages.

beans.name: Kenya Ruiru AA Mills Estate
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from Sasini's 65-hectare Kiambu farm; the largely Kenyan-owned company provides housing, education and fair wages. Tangy blackcurrant, creamy butterscotch and a lively morello cherry finish.

beans.name: Burundi Shikankoni
beans.desc: Burundi has been a notable specialty producer since 1962. This year the roastery chose two favourite Bourbon lots from Shikankoni Hill, grown by smallholders and processed at partner mills.

beans.name: La Chumeca
beans.producer: San Pablo de Leon Cortes, Tarrazu; Beneficio La Chumeca
beans.desc: A light-roast Costa Rican from a family-run operation in Tarrazú founded in 2014 by Martín Ureña. Four farms supply it, with experienced pickers and regenerative methods. Honeydew, papaya and floral notes.

beans.name: Block Party
beans.desc: A blend that's sweet, tart and well balanced for filter, espresso or flat whites. Its sweetness comes from Paraná, Brazil, where volcanic soil, small family farms and cool seasons slow ripening, giving a rich, creamy cup.

beans.name: Amatillo Bioreactor
beans.producer: Pueblo Nuevo Vinas, Santa Rosa; Finca Amatillo
beans.desc: From a family farm between two Guatemalan volcanoes, fermented in a controlled bioreactor to encourage microbial activity. A lively, complex cup with rich tropical fruit and ripe banana, softened by orange-like sweetness.

beans.name: Jamaica Blue Mountain
beans.desc: A rare coffee from high in Jamaica's Blue Mountains, above 2,000 feet, with its own trademark. A regulator oversees every batch with strict quality checks.

beans.name: Y Fenai Rum Infused Coffee
beans.desc: A collaboration with Anglesey Rum Co: smooth, full-bodied speciality coffee with warm Anglesey rum character, named for the Menai Strait and roasted fresh in north Wales. For gifts, after-dinner sipping or everyday enjoyment.

beans.name: Porth yr Aur
beans.desc: An award-winning Huila single origin from careful farmers using fresh cultivation and processing methods. Medium-dark roasted: smooth and rich, balancing sweetness with depth.

beans.name: Castell Bach
beans.desc: A festive blend roasted medium in North Wales, with hints of dark fruit, zesty citrus and cocoa. Beans are grown at 1,500-2,000 metres, and it's sold only over Christmas while supplies last.

beans.name: Dros'r Aber
beans.producer: Kamwangi wet mill, Kirinyaga (New Ngariama FCS); Batian, Ruiru 11, SL28, SL34; 1,750m
beans.desc: A Kenyan Arabica from a cooperative of about 1,500 growers in the Kirinyaga highlands, carefully sorted, washed and dried. Roasted for filter to give a lively, fruity cup, though it also suits espresso.

beans.name: Segontiwm Decaf
beans.desc: The roaster's award-winning decaf from Mexican beans, decaffeinated by a chemical-free mountain water method that preserves flavour. Medium-dark roasted, good for espresso and cafetière.

beans.name: Twthill
beans.desc: A smooth, medium-roast Indian blend designed for espresso. Sweet and balanced, holding up black or with milk.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Medium
beans.desc: A smooth, evenly balanced medium roast of 100% Arabica from high-altitude Colombia, hand-picked and roasted in Britain to highlight natural sweetness. Caramel and milk chocolate with a light citrus lift.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Medium-Dark
beans.desc: For lovers of intensity, roasted a little longer to draw out more chocolate and caramel. A fuller, layered cup with a subtle smoky edge that stays mellow and easygoing.

beans.name: Don Jose Colombian Supremo - Dark
beans.desc: A dark-roast Colombian Arabica with a bold, smoky punch and hearty mouthfeel. Cocoa richness, sweet treacle and toasted nuts finish smooth and lingering; strong but velvety.

beans.name: Dona Ester Sugar Cane Decaf
beans.desc: A single-origin Colombian decaf, chosen and roasted to bring out its aroma and decaffeinated by the natural sugar cane process, keeping the full, rich body of a premium coffee.

beans.name: Cafe Colco Premium Signature Blend
beans.origin: Colombia / Honduras / Brazil (plus Ethiopian per description)
beans.desc: A premium blend, hand-roasted in Britain from top-quality beans. Gentle and mellow, hearty and full-bodied, aimed at drinkers wanting a smoother, less acidic cup.

beans.name: Cafe La Vida Premium House Blend
beans.desc: A UK-roasted blend with a gentle, rounded taste for those preferring a softer cup. Beans are carefully chosen and hand-roasted to bring out aroma, giving a full-bodied coffee for connoisseurs and everyday drinkers.

beans.name: Espresso Comercio Premium Signature Blend
beans.desc: A house roast for espresso drinks, combining top-grade robusta with Colombian Supremo Arabica: robusta adds boldness and body, Arabica smoothness and sweetness. Developed for trade clients and valued for its crema and punchy balance.

beans.name: Los Mejores
beans.desc: A mix of two Colombian grades: one adds lively, lighter sweetness, the other deep chocolatey richness. Blending medium-dark and dark roasts for a sturdy, easygoing coffee from family-owned, eco-conscious farms.

beans.name: Santico - Ethiopian
beans.desc: A single-origin Ethiopian Arabica from fertile highlands where climate and soil shape flavour. Hand-picked and grown with traditional, eco-friendly methods.

beans.name: Tio Lucas - Brazilian
beans.desc: A Brazilian single origin of 100% Arabica Bourbon from high elevations: a sweet, aromatic, smooth and balanced cup suited to pour over, French press and cold brew.

beans.name: Paola - Vietnamese
beans.desc: A single-origin Vietnamese robusta roasted to highlight earthy, woody, peppery character. Potent and hearty with chocolatey, nutty fragrance and slight bitterness at the end; darker roasts hit harder, lighter ones are softer.

beans.name: Catracho - Honduras
beans.desc: A Honduran Bourbon from mountain slopes with mineral-rich volcanic soil: layered but gentle and balanced, with dark cocoa, roasted nuts and fruit. For seasoned drinkers and newcomers.

beans.name: Cafe Excelso - Colombian
beans.desc: A Colombian with smooth chocolate, gentle caramel sweetness and cosy toasted nut undertones. Balanced acidity and a long, rich finish.

beans.name: All Day Blend (Half Caff)
beans.desc: Equal parts arabica and Swiss Water decaf, for a morning boost without overdoing it. Pleasantly sweet for any hour, with reduced caffeine to help avoid disrupted sleep.

beans.name: Ambush Forest
beans.desc: Grown on forest farms in Ethiopia's Oromia mountains at 1,900-2,300 metres with minimal human involvement. Presented as an energy boost for celebrations and a reminder of gratitude; its flavour is unlike other origins.

beans.name: Aurora Blend (Limited Edition)
beans.desc: A blend created to celebrate women around the world, pairing a gentle Peruvian coffee with a rich Indonesian one, as a tribute to female farmers and a gift or treat.

beans.name: Luna Blend (Limited Edition)
beans.desc: A seasonal take on Aurora: Indonesian Gayo and Peruvian Café Femenino from women producers plus Ethiopian Yirgacheffe for floral aromas and fruity notes. Medium-light roasted, balanced and clean, celebrating spring.

beans.name: Bolivia Finca Los Rodriguez
beans.producer: Samaipata, Santa Cruz; Fincas Los Rodriguez
beans.listedNotes: Dulce de leche, Green apple, White grape
beans.desc: The Rodriguez family's story began about 35 years ago when former banker Pedro Rodriguez followed his passion for coffee and became a leading figure in Bolivian specialty coffee. His family now runs an export firm and twelve farms.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Miaki - Yellow Bourbon
beans.desc: Brazil is a major grower that also keeps much of its crop at home, ranking second in consumption after the US. This Fazenda Miaki offers peach and spicy hot chocolate flavours.

beans.name: Brazil Peaberry
