beans.desc: A peaberry from neighbouring farms near Cabo Verde, Minas Gerais, at 950 metres with distinct seasons. In peaberries the seed fails to split in two, thought to channel extra nutrients and boost flavour.

beans.name: Brazil Serra Negra
beans.desc: From Fazenda da Lagoa, where coffee is a way of life across generations. A few selected arabica types are grown sustainably, blending a two-century heritage with modern on-site research.

beans.name: Coffeelink Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A classic everyday espresso from three continents. The roaster partners with honest growers and roasts meticulously for crema, bold taste and a caffeine lift.

beans.name: Colombia Caturra de Altura
beans.desc: A Caturra, a natural Bourbon hybrid developed in São Paulo State, grown in Huila, Colombia. Mineral-rich soils and Andean microclimates give a juicy, fruity, complex character.

beans.name: Colombia Huila
beans.desc: Huila combines high altitude, varied soils and dedicated growers; its farmers often win Cup of Excellence recognition, and it is becoming Colombia's largest producing region. A chocolatey cup worth trying.

beans.name: Colombia Supremo Noble (Oro de Suarez)
beans.desc: A Colombian Supremo, the top size grade, bigger than Excelso. Western and northern harvests run October-November, southern main crop April-June, and smallholders usually wash and dry on their farms.

beans.name: Colombian Geisha
beans.desc: A blend pooling tiny harvests of rare varietals such as Gesha from growers partnering with Osito Coffee. Lots were too small to sell alone, so they were combined as Divino Niño after grading and cupping.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca Castelgazzo
beans.producer: Montecristo / Trifinio; Castelgazzo; Kenya, Bourbon, Pacamara, Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Red berries, Stone fruit, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: From a farm set up in 1995 by Mario and La Geña Cristiani on the edge of Montecristo National Park in cloud forest. Now run by their daughters, combining coffee, forestry, conservation and community growth.

beans.name: Costa Rica Tarrazu
beans.desc: A Costa Rican Strictly Hard Bean lot roasted until it takes a dark chocolate tint and its oils rise, giving a bolder, heavier brew ideal for espresso.

beans.name: Coffeelink Espresso Blend Dark Roast
beans.desc: A classic dark roast espresso blending coffees from three continents. The roaster picks trustworthy growers and roasts carefully for espresso at any hour.

beans.name: Decaf Cinnamon Blend
beans.desc: A caffeine-free version of the roaster's Christmas blend, offered year-round: a spiced decaf with warm cinnamon to share with people you care about.

beans.name: Decaf Ginger Blend
beans.desc: A decaf from the Christmas line blending ginger with nutty notes. A toasty, spiced fragrance for festive gatherings, caffeine-free, to share with family and friends.

beans.name: Decaf Nutmeg Blend
beans.desc: A Christmas-themed decaf blend with ginger and nutty notes and a warm, spicy aroma that makes December mornings feel festive, caffeine-free for everyone to share.

beans.name: Decaf Pumpkin Blend
beans.desc: Originally a Halloween favourite, now sold year-round as a decaf so people can enjoy its warm, pleasing character without caffeine.

beans.name: Dominican Republic Barahona
beans.desc: Grown on the Dominican Republic's southwestern Caribbean coast. Alternating rain and sun cause repeated flowering, so pickers revisit each tree several times. Organic methods, with producers investing in healthcare, schools and water.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca San Antonio
beans.producer: Los Ausoles; Malacara B and Las Mercedes farms
beans.desc: From the Chantuc company, founded in 1979 by Emma Alvarez and now run by her children. Workers get meals, housing and steady employment. Beans come from two old plantations under shade trees, fed with compost-based products.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Grade 2
beans.desc: A top seller and the base of the All Day blend, from Yirgacheffe in Sidamo. Lively, sparkling brightness with floral and citrus notes, and an aroma worth buying for alone.

beans.name: Ethiopian Guji Grade 1
beans.desc: A Guji lot bought direct from the grower. Honey, jasmine and bright citrus, with cardamom and nutmeg notes; its lively acidity may not suit everyone but may appeal to Kenyan coffee fans.

beans.name: Ethiopian Illubabor Forest Anaerobic Grade 1
beans.desc: From forest farms in Ethiopia's Illubabor Zone, anaerobically fermented in a sealed, vented tank. The roaster suggests a long pour rather than espresso or moka.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe Grade 1 (Hand Picked & Washed)
beans.desc: An Ethiopian Yirgacheffe sourced directly via a long-time charity partner and a bestseller seen as a good all-day coffee. Wet processing gives lively sparkle, with bright floral and citrus notes.

beans.name: Finca La Verona
beans.producer: El Arenal, Matagalpa; Finca La Verona
beans.desc: A Nicaraguan farm that grows many varieties and keeps them separate after harvest. Pulped coffee ferments anaerobically in airtight tanks; hand-picked cherries dry at a separate facility, then are sorted as regional or microlot.

beans.name: Guatemala Los Volcanos
beans.desc: From Antigua, a Guatemalan valley ringed by mountains, with nutrient-rich volcanic soil and cool climate. Bourbon cherries are washed and sun-dried at a mill owned by the Zelaya family.

beans.name: Christmas Blend (Guji Grade 1 with Cinnamon)
beans.desc: A cinnamon-infused blend added after the Christmas Blend's success, using beans bought direct through an Ethiopian charity partner. This Guji is fragrant and mellow, milder than Yirgacheffe.

beans.name: Orange Blossom Blend
beans.desc: A bright, fruit-forward summer blend, excellent for cold brew and iced Americanos. Gentle, tea-like mouthfeel leaves lingering sweetness.

beans.name: Honduras Honey Process (Microlot)
beans.desc: Honduras is emerging as a specialty leader, with growers experimenting with processing, some offering several methods from one farm. Coffee is central to its economy alongside minerals, tropical fruit and sugar cane.

beans.name: Indian Mysore Nuggets AAA
beans.desc: India has exported fine coffee for over 150 years and ranks fifth worldwide for Arabica. Karnataka grows about four-fifths of the crop, and its large, top-quality Mysore Nuggets are compared to gold.

beans.name: Indonesia Queen Gayo Grade 1
beans.desc: Chocolate, nut and fruit flavours from an all-female cooperative in Aceh. Ketaira belongs to Café Femenino, a programme supporting women growers, using foundation grants for leadership training and a community hub.

beans.name: Italiano Vero Blend
beans.desc: A blend suited to classic Italian-style espresso served straight, also good in milk. Robust yet bold with smooth flavour notes, a tribute to Italy's role in coffee culture.

beans.name: Rocket Fuel Blend
beans.desc: Made for groggy mornings, mostly Tanzanian robusta with Ethiopian arabica adding smooth, cocoa-like sweetness. Works with any method and especially in milky drinks.

beans.name: Jamaican Blue Mountain
beans.desc: A Cup of Excellence-winning Jamaican, a sliver of the island's crop and one of the world's costliest. Grown in cool, misty, rainy highlands with free-draining soil; also the base of Tia Maria liqueur.

beans.name: Jamaican Blue Mountain Peaberry
beans.desc: A scarce Jamaican peaberry honoured with Cup of Excellence, grown on the misty Blue Mountains slopes. Highly sought worldwide and the flavour base of Tia Maria liqueur.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.desc: Acidic soil suits Arabica here. Most production is from small and mid-sized farms that wash beans on-site and sun-dry on raised beds. Beans are size-sorted and auctioned weekly, with two harvests a year.

beans.name: Kongo Papua New Guinea
beans.desc: Grown in Simbu, Papua New Guinea's third-largest coffee province, via Kong Coffee. Y grade covers about 65% of national exports from small village farmers, traditionally with a rich, fruity body that suits blends.

beans.name: Maragogype
beans.desc: Oscar Jimenez runs Nuevo Pacto in Jinotega, Nicaragua, where forest shade protects soil and creates a microclimate. Mostly hardy Catimor with a smaller share of large-bean Maragogype, all washed.

beans.name: Mexican Terruno Nayarita Reserve
beans.desc: Opening the bag releases berry sweetness and nutty butter. A medium-bodied cup finishing smoothly with baker's chocolate, candy-like sweetness and bright berry and orange acidity. Grown by about 260 cooperative farmers around Cerro San Juan; fully traceable.

beans.name: Mexico El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve Premium
beans.desc: The El Triunfo reserve sits where two ecological zones meet, supporting abundant wildlife and about 12,000 residents. A 663-member cooperative grows shade coffee under layered native trees and replanted with resistant varieties after the 2012 rust outbreak.

beans.name: Noss Noss Blend
beans.desc: A tribute to cultural traditions and coffee's Arabic roots, best as espresso. Arabica and Robusta, with its concept from a Moroccan drink, roasted several times a week to stay fresh.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: From Java, where coffee once matured on long sea voyages as ballast on spice ships to Europe. Exposure to wood and brine gave a sturdy, earthy flavour, best slowly savoured.

beans.name: Peru 121 Project
beans.desc: Part of importer DR Wakefield's 1-2-1 scheme pairing individual growers with roasters. An organic, Fairtrade-certified Peruvian grown under shade and washed traditionally, mostly picked in August at peak ripeness.

beans.name: Peru Cafe Femenino
beans.desc: The Café Femenino Foundation awards grants to women in coffee regions worldwide. Peru's small farms, often under three hectares, are organised into carefully run cooperatives.

beans.name: Premium Espresso Blend
beans.origin: Ethiopia / Colombia / Peru / Honduras / El Salvador
beans.desc: A premium blend of five high-grade coffees from Ethiopia, Colombia, Peru, Honduras and El Salvador. The roaster extends roasting time and samples each batch to hit the intended profile.

beans.name: Pumpkin Spice Blend
beans.desc: A Halloween-themed coffee mixing pumpkin spice with a seasonal dark roast and mellow, cocoa-tinged single origins. Medium-dark, works with any brew method and suits lattes.

beans.name: Rwanda Kinini AA Microlot
beans.desc: A microlot from trees above 2,000 metres, processed at Kinini washing station where 633 farmers deliver. Ferments five to twenty hours after pulping, then sun-dries about two weeks. Smooth dark chocolate, lemon and fudge.

beans.name: Rwanda Lake Kivu
beans.listedNotes: Toffee caramel, Red berry, Citrus, Clove
beans.desc: A Rwandan from Lake Kivu grown high in volcanic soil: rich, creamy toffee and caramel with bright berries and citrus, clove and cinnamon warmth, and a full body that lingers.

beans.name: Sidamo Dara Grade 1 (Washed)
beans.desc: Ethiopians treat coffee as a cherished ritual. Sidamo's fertile soil, steady rain and ideal temperatures yield outstanding beans; wet processing gives this one bright apricot, jasmine and caramel.

beans.name: Signature Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A tailored classic espresso of Colombian, Brazilian, Ethiopian and Indian beans: sweet, rich and harmonised in taste, acidity and scent, holding up in milky drinks with chocolatey notes.

beans.name: Spiced Ginger Blend
beans.desc: A holiday blend of premium Ethiopian coffee with ginger, meant to bring people together. Nutty ginger flavour and a warm, spicy aroma for festive mornings.

beans.name: Spiced Nutmeg Blend
beans.desc: A Christmas blend of the newest single origin with a sprinkle of nutmeg, for sharing. Ginger and nutty flavours and a warm, spicy aroma.

beans.name: Sumatra Lintong Grade 1
beans.desc: A Sumatran with distinctive taste, mild sourness, heavy mouthfeel and rustic, soil-like notes. Traditional wet-hulled, grown in full sun without chemical inputs mostly by small-scale farmers.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Colombian Excelso
beans.producer: Suarez; Cafe Granja La Esperanza; Caturra, Typica; 1,700m
beans.desc: Swiss Water decaf using water, heat and timing to strip caffeine while preserving the bean's character. This Excelso grade is smaller than Supremo but tastes sweeter, with smooth, rounded body and subtle caramel.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Brazil Cerrado
beans.desc: Brazil has pushed sustainability through stronger forest-protection laws, with many estates setting aside conservation land. Standard lots taste nutty and caramelly, creamy, while newer methods reveal sweetness, citrus and brightness.

beans.name: Winter Espresso
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Telila Washing Station, 8 women smallholders in the Kecho Anderacha kebele. Guatemala: El Anonal, Huehuetenango (Orlando Antulio Martinez Samayoa and Gesler Gudemny Martinez Lopez)
beans.desc: A festive, espresso-only blend of honey-processed Ethiopian coffee (JARC 74110 and 74112, from Telila Washing Station) and a washed Guatemalan field blend of Bourbon, Typica, San Ramon and Caturra from El Anonal. The roaster likens the Ethiopian half to fruit-flavoured Turkish delight and describes the cup as sweet and richly textured, made for Christmas drinks. The Guatemalan producers replanted with rust-resistant varieties after a leaf rust outbreak and trialled Gesha and Pacamara in 2015.

beans.name: Red Brick
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Telila and Atoma washing stations, Jimma, about 97 smallholders via Addis Exporter. Costa Rica: La Lia Micromill (Luis and Oscar Monge) and Don Oscar Micromill (Alejandro Jimenez), Tarrazu
beans.processFull: Ethiopia washed; Costa Rica white honey
beans.brew: Espresso. Roaster's recipe: 19g in a 20g VST basket, 94-94.5C, 28-32 seconds, 1:2 ratio (developed on a Victoria Arduino Black Eagle)
beans.desc: The roaster's seasonal espresso blend, built on the idea of good neighbours: 47% washed Ethiopian lots from Addis Exporter's Telila and Atoma stations (JARC 74110 and 74112) and 53% white-honey Costa Rican lots from two neighbouring Tarrazu micromills (Catuai and Caturra). The components change with each harvest, and the aim is to emphasise fruit and sweetness: yellow plum, smooth butterscotch and orange, with a silky, lightly floral Ethiopian edge.

beans.name: La Cidra
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Renato Sanchez and family; exported by Beneficio San Vicente. Region not shown
beans.desc: A washed Honduran espresso (Catuai and IHCAFE90, 2026 harvest) from Renato Sanchez and his family, with plum, caramel and praline plus stonefruit and dark chocolate. For 2026 Renato built raised drying beds for tighter quality control, his daughter Alejandra worked a season at exporter Beneficio San Vicente to learn its quality methods, and the family is working on soil quality and biodiversity.

beans.name: Sweetshop
beans.producer: Ethiopia: Dambi Uddo Drying Station, Guji, via Sookoo Coffee. Costa Rica: El Higueron, Mario Araya (Los Cuarteles micromill, Araya family), Tarrazu
beans.processFull: Ethiopia natural; Costa Rica red honey
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Creamy body, Florals, Bergamot (Bookkisa); Jammy, Candy-like (El Higueron)
beans.desc: A playful, fruit-driven espresso, 50% natural Ethiopian Bookkisa (Gibirinna 74110 and Serto 74112) and 50% red-honey Costa Rican El Higueron (Catuai). The roaster says it is aiming for as much fruit and fun as possible rather than balance or tradition. Bookkisa brings strawberry, a creamy mouthfeel, then florals and bergamot; El Higueron adds jammy, candy-like notes.

beans.name: Decaf Espresso
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Sanchez family, southwestern Lempira; exported by Beneficio San Vicente
beans.desc: A decaf version of La Cidra (Catuai and IHCAFE90, washed) roasted for espresso, with raisin, fudge and orange. The page describes southwestern Lempira as drier than Santa Barbara, with more remote, larger farms, and says Beneficio San Vicente's slow, careful drying improves shelf life and flavour; the roaster first bought La Cidra in 2022.

beans.name: Don Cayito
beans.producer: Don Cayito farm, Diego Calderon and family, Los Angeles Micromill, Dota, Tarrazu
beans.desc: A natural Typica from Dota, Tarrazu, in small 175g bags, with a blueberry-led profile of fresh and dried berries, cherry, peach and white flowers and a velvety mouthfeel. It comes from one of the roaster's foundational Costa Rican relationships: Diego Calderon's family mill at Los Angeles Micromill, from a farm the founding green buyer first visited about a decade ago.

beans.name: Shortcut
beans.desc: A no-decision filter option for people who love juicy, sweet specialty coffee but sometimes want to skip choosing: complex, sweet, high-grown washed lots picked by the roaster. The page gives no origin, producer, variety or roast and marks it coming soon.

beans.name: Shoondhisa
beans.producer: Guji; smallholders via Sookoo Coffee, processed at Suke Drying Station
beans.desc: A natural Guji lot (Gibirinna 74110 and Serto 74112) bought by the roaster since 2023 from Sookoo Coffee, who grow, process and export it. The late 2026 harvest reached the station into February; cherries are dried whole in a thin layer for four to five days, then thickened for two more weeks, which develops the nectarine, honey and lychee character. Suggested for afternoons or brunch.

beans.name: El Trapiche Santa Rosa 1900
beans.producer: Santa Rosa 1900 micromill, Santa Rosa Arriba de Leon Cortes; Kevin and Efrain 'Macho' Naranjo; 1,700-1,900m
beans.desc: A washed Red and Yellow Catuai from father and son Macho and Kevin Naranjo at 1,700-1,900m, named after the traditional mill used to press sugarcane juice. Baked apple, honey and nougat with caramelised sweetness, bright acidity and a full, lush body; the roaster usually buys honey-process lots from this family, so a washed lot is new. Pitched as classic Costa Rica for breakfast or weekends.

beans.name: The Filter Blend
beans.producer: Guatemala: Paya', Huehuetenango (Nery Pablo Lopez; Cooperative El Sendero). Rwanda: Rebero, Kinini Washing Station, Rulindo
beans.desc: A seasonal, adaptable everyday filter blend using the same idea as Red Brick: 50% Guatemalan Paya' (Caturra and Bourbon) and 50% Rwandan Rebero (BM139, BM71, Bourbon Jackson), both washed. Sweet, balanced and medium-bodied, with red apple, praline and sultana; its components are subject to change.

beans.name: Half Caff
beans.producer: Honduras: La Cidra, Lempira (Renato Sanchez). Costa Rica: Santa Rosa 1900 micromill, Tarrazu (Naranjo family)
beans.processFull: Washed; Honduras component ethyl acetate decaf
beans.desc: A 50/50 filter blend of ethyl-acetate decaf La Cidra from Honduras and washed El Trapiche Santa Rosa 1900 from Costa Rica, bringing two family-run farms into one cup. Forest fruit, milk chocolate and almond, with crisp apple and a creamy mouthfeel from El Trapiche and persimmon-like acidity and syrupy depth from La Cidra. Pitched as a mid-afternoon pick-me-up.

beans.name: Decaf Filter
beans.producer: La Cidra farm, Sanchez family, southwestern Lempira; exported by Beneficio San Vicente
beans.brew: V60 or French press. Roaster suggests 70g coffee per litre of water; for V60 agitate the bloom, then use low agitation
beans.desc: A light-roast decaf La Cidra (Catuai and IHCAFE90, washed) with raisin, fudge and hazelnut, dried fruit and toffee and a dulce de leche-like sweetness. The ethyl acetate process softens the coffee's sharp pomegranate acidity. The page says the next decaf will be Union San Pedro from Oaxaca, Mexico.

beans.name: The Good Brew
beans.desc: A brighter, juicier blend, roasted lighter than the Espresso Blend: two Ethiopian Anderacha lots and a Brazil natural.

beans.name: Community Blend
beans.desc: Smooth, sweet and balanced: a 50/50 Colombia and Brazil blend made for Company of Cooks, designed for espresso and milk.

beans.name: Anderacha Ethiopia
beans.desc: A clean, bright washed Ethiopian espresso from the Anderacha estate, Limu: floral, citrus acidity and intense sweetness.

beans.name: Jesus Arbey Iquira Colombia
beans.desc: A natural Pink Bourbon from Finca El Placer, Acevedo, Huila; a staff favourite for V60 with rhubarb, papaya and cola.

beans.name: El Corozo El Salvador
beans.desc: A clean honey-processed Pacamara from Palo de Campana, Santa Ana, grown in Los Volcanes National Park; lime, melon and cocoa.

beans.name: Bisal Munti India
beans.desc: A fruit-forward carbonic maceration lot from Malavalli, Karnataka, shade-grown under areca and pepper; blueberry, lemon and forest honey.

beans.name: 01 Brazil + Guatemala
beans.listedNotes: Maple syrup, Bakewell tart, Plum, Hazelnut
beans.desc: A classic house blend with a citrusy body and maple sweetness, layered with fruit and a Bakewell-tart finish.

beans.name: 02 Brazil + Rwanda
beans.listedNotes: Orange zest, Stewed apple, Sweet almond
beans.desc: A full-bodied house blend, "a forest of flavour", with stewed apple, sweet candied almond and a blackberry finish.

beans.name: 03 Brazil / Colombia / Guatemala
beans.desc: A three-origin blend where tart pomegranate meets butterscotch, with a touch of salted cocoa.

beans.name: 04 Brazil
beans.desc: A single-origin Brazilian with juicy plum, creamy chocolate and sweet clementine.

beans.name: 05 Decaf Colombia
beans.desc: A sugarcane decaf from Tolima, naturally sweet and smooth with warm, citrusy, fruity notes.

beans.name: 06 Guatemala (filter)
beans.desc: Honey sweetness reminiscent of a Crunchie bar, with bright Pink Lady apple and a soft peach finish.

beans.name: 07 Kenya (filter)
beans.desc: A washed lot named after the Adumu Maasai jumping dance, from the slopes of Mount Kenya, with raspberry, cherry cola and redcurrant.

beans.name: 08 Colombia (filter)
beans.desc: A relaxing washed Colombian filter from Inza with sweet melon, rich raisin and juicy mango.

beans.name: 09 Costa Rica (filter)
beans.desc: A vibrant, sweet natural from San Lorenzo, part of the DRWakefield Projects premium scheme, with blueberry, caramel and pear sorbet.

beans.name: 10 Honduras (filter)
beans.desc: A Parainema lot from German Reyes at Beneficio San Vicente, anaerobic honey processed, with pecan pie, toffee and nectarine.

beans.name: 11 Peru (filter)
beans.desc: A refined, clean, well-balanced washed cup from small farmers in San Ignacio, Cajamarca, with tropical fruit, grape and floral notes.

beans.name: Article
beans.desc: Workshop's flagship house blend, dependable and steady in every cup, with familiar dark chocolate, maple syrup and raisin notes. Built to shine across all brew methods for a timeless, pleasing daily coffee.

beans.name: Legacy
beans.producer: Calca (Manuel Patilla Carrasco); Uraga, Guji (Raro Boda)
beans.desc: A blend of rotating harvests from the roaster's longest-standing growers, rich and layered, with spiced baked goods, caramel-like sweetness and dark berry fruit. Suits any preparation method.

beans.name: Pillar
beans.desc: A coffee with rich mouthfeel, layered sweetness and gentle acidity. Treacle, crushed cocoa bits, liquorice root, a hint of spice and sugared nuts; pairs especially well with dairy-based drinks.

beans.name: Slow Brew
beans.desc: A filter blend of Colombian coffee with brown sugar and gentle apple and Ugandan coffee bringing citrus, smooth sweetness and bright aromas. Lively, fruity and full of character, especially brewed slowly.

beans.name: Reset Half Caff
beans.listedNotes: Roasted almonds, Sweet raspberry, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A half-caff blend for late-day work, using roughly half decaf beans for afternoons and evenings when a full hit feels unnecessary. The Colombian beans are from Huila, with a La Plata lot chosen for decaffeination.

beans.name: Sipi Tangwen
beans.desc: A small batch of Sipi Tangwen from Mount Elgon, Uganda, designed for filter: crisp, sweet and citrusy. Smallholders grow it at high altitude in volcanic soil, supported by a co-op.

beans.name: Maidy Bocanegra Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: Bruselas, Pitalito, Huila; Finca Los Limones; Pink Bourbon
beans.desc: Maidy Bocanegra returns with a standout Pink Bourbon from her Huila farm. Cherries are hand-picked, rested, depulped, briefly fermented, washed and slowly dried on mesh for a fruity, richly sweet cup.

beans.name: Danche
beans.desc: A fresh new-season Ethiopian from Chelbesa, a long-standing team pick prized for its intensely floral and powerful character.

beans.name: Bulaago
beans.desc: An espresso from Bulaago, Uganda: smooth and silky with bright citrus-like fruit, quince and fresh pine, honey-like sweetness lingering through a clean finish. Grown by Mount Elgon smallholders and picked as a standout reserve lot.

beans.name: La Colorada Gesha
beans.producer: Villa Maria, Iquira, Huila; Eduardo Anacona; Gesha
beans.desc: A Gesha, one of two releases from Eduardo Anacona's Finca La Colorada in Colombia. Bright, fizzy pink lemonade quality, delicate flowers and juicy, mature berry flavours.

beans.name: Migoti
beans.desc: A fresh Burundi from a Rubanda lot where over a thousand small growers bring ripe cherries to the Migoti station. Layered fruit and rich cocoa with a tidy, defined finish from carefully handled Red Bourbon.

beans.name: Gakuyu-ini
beans.desc: A lively, striking Kenyan from the Gakuyu-ini washing station, chosen for composure, strength and crystal-clear character. Only a small number of bags were secured, as it was too good to pass up.

beans.name: Chakra
beans.desc: A year-round Peruvian. Workshop has bought from Peruvian growers for about a decade and has partnered with the Valle Inca association since 2018. Shaped by organic methods and attentive harvesting and processing.

beans.name: El Nevado
beans.producer: Huila; about 24 smallholders via Caravela; Caturra, Castillo
beans.desc: A lively yet smooth single-origin Colombian with toasted sugar, almond paste and warm fruit. Roasted to suit every brew method, a versatile home-brewing favourite.

beans.name: Madegi
beans.desc: Madegi, whose Amharic name means growth, celebrates Workshop's Ethiopian sourcing since 2011, mostly through Snap Coffees over the past eight years, and how that partnership has matured.

beans.name: La Plata Decaf
beans.producer: San Sebastian, La Plata, Huila; 7 farmers
beans.desc: A decaf given as much attention as the caffeinated coffees: a rich, well-rounded Colombian with currant- and prune-like fruity sweetness ending on bittersweet cocoa and toasted nuts. Roasted for any brew method.

beans.name: Evergreen
beans.desc: Grown high in Nueva Segovia, Nicaragua: a layered coffee with plum, fudge and chocolate-biscuit sweetness, roasted to work across every brewing style.

beans.name: BS1 Espresso
beans.desc: An easy, sweet espresso for flat whites and cappuccinos that also works straight: milk chocolate richness, sticky caramel and a bright red-fruit finish. Grown by smallholders near Buesaco with the Procaal cooperative handling drying.

beans.name: Cruise Control
beans.desc: A single-farm Brazilian from Daterra Estate in Cerrado Mineiro: dependable and sweet with a rich, cocoa-like body, honey and hazelnut. Works black or with dairy and plant milks.

beans.name: Jumpstart
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Nut praline, Maple syrup
beans.desc: Triple Co's first house blend, built to energise tougher mornings. Mellow and smooth, with rich silky body and little sharpness, and designed to taste great with milk.

beans.name: Mixtape
beans.desc: A 50/50 fruity espresso blend highlighting coffees the team especially enjoys. More adventurous than the everyday range, with a lively, liqueur-like character; components change with the seasons.

beans.name: Slow Burn
beans.desc: A half-caff blend for the calm after a lively fire: warm, steady and long-lasting. Suits flat whites, iced coffee, afternoon espresso or batch filter, giving energy without a crash.

beans.name: Colombia Sugarcane Decaf
beans.desc: A decaf from the same growers as BS1, aiming to taste much like regular coffee. Decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate to protect the bean's flavours, then steamed to remove leftover solvent.

beans.name: Shop Filter
beans.producer: Santa Ana Volcano, El Borbollon mill
beans.desc: A washed El Salvador from farms supplying the El Borbollon mill, run by the Alvares family, mostly on the Santa Ana volcano. Patio-dried and hand-sorted, with sweetness, plum flavours and a nutty close.

beans.name: Burundi Vyiza
beans.producer: Vyiza washing station, Ngozi; Red Bourbon 1800m
beans.desc: A returning favourite from Vyiza station in Ngozi, northern Burundi, at 1,800 metres, run as a shared community project (the name means 'good things' in Kirundi). Slow-dried over weeks for sweet, liquor-like richness.

beans.name: Birthday Party - Tanzania
beans.desc: An SL28 from Glenmalure on Ngila Estate in northern Tanzania, near a cloud forest where wildlife such as elephants roams. Hand-sorted, pulped, fermented 12 hours, then dried on raised beds over eight to thirteen days.

beans.name: Nicaragua La Picona
beans.producer: Finca La Picona, Nueva Segovia; Maracaturra 1250m
beans.desc: From a nine-hectare farm in Las Manos, Dipilto, Nicaragua, owned by Martha Lucía Albir Sotomayor and shaded by native trees. The rare Maracaturra variety gives a lively, layered cup with medium body and molasses-like sweetness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Buku Abel
beans.desc: A Buku Abel lot from a high-altitude Guji village. Smallholders' cherries are hand-picked, sorted and dried outdoors on raised platforms. Sourced via SNAP Specialty Coffee, a partner since 2022.

beans.name: Peru San Ignacio
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian from San Ignacio smallholders with caramel sweetness, citrusy pomelo and an herbal finish. Moist valleys and steady rain ripen cherries slowly and evenly for clean, sweet cups.

beans.name: Colombia Gaitania
beans.producer: Gaitania, Planadas, Tolima; Nasa Wesx community; Caturra
beans.desc: An organic microlot from the Nasa Wesx community in Tolima, Colombia. The Caturra ferments 50 hours in low oxygen, then dries on raised beds under temperature control, drawing out juicy red grape, a rum-like body and sweetness.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea - Elimbari
beans.producer: Chuave, Mount Wilhelm; smallholders via Kongo
beans.desc: A mellow-acidity coffee with earthy, black-tea-like notes from Chuave district in Papua New Guinea's central highlands, grown by smallholders on Mount Wilhelm's slopes. Pulped, fermented and tarp-dried before Kongo's mill sorts and exports it.

beans.name: Brazil Rancho Grande Estate
beans.producer: Sul de Minas; Rancho Grande farm, José Carlos Reis
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed for sweetness and balance'
beans.desc: A Brazilian from a family farm in Sul de Minas, made for easy, comforting drinking. Milk chocolate leads, with roasted nuts, a soft round body and little acidity. Suits espresso, milk drinks and filter.

beans.name: Dark Sugars
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed for body, sweetness and milk performance'
beans.listedNotes: Heavy dark chocolate, Subtle spice, Medium sweetness
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend built to hold up in milk while keeping sweetness and structure. Brazilian and Indonesian coffees combine for a heavy, chocolate-led cup with full body and a long finish.

beans.name: Bond Street Espresso Blend
beans.roastNote: Medium roast developed for body and sweetness
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Roasted nuts, Strawberry sweetness
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso of Brazilian and Ethiopian beans. The Brazilian brings chocolate, nuts and a silky body; the Ethiopian adds sweet, strawberry-like fruit. Balanced and rounded, made for espresso and milk drinks.

beans.name: Rwanda Musozi Washed Lot 4
beans.listedNotes: Blackberry, Black tea, Raspberry, Orange, Brown sugar, Bright fruit
beans.desc: A seasonal single origin from Rwamatamu Coffee in Nyamasheke, grown high in mineral-rich volcanic ground. Fully washed, with fruit-led brightness, natural sweetness, clean acidity and a smooth, balanced body for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Kenya Ngunguru AA
beans.listedNotes: Redcurrant, Lemon, Grapefruit, Bergamot, Dark chocolate
beans.desc: A seasonal Kenyan from the Ngunguru area, grown high on volcanic soil. Ripe cherries are hand-picked and washed at local stations. Juicy fruit brightness, citrus lift and a little dark chocolate with a medium, lively body.

beans.name: Funky Weekend Blend
beans.roastNote: Medium roast developed for chocolate, body and funk
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, Roasted nuts, Red fruit, Winey funk
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend pairing a creamy, chocolate-heavy Brazilian with a lively, wine-like fermented Colombian that adds red fruit and bold character. Sweet and chocolate-led with an edge, aimed at lattes and flat whites.

beans.name: Colombia ReForest Project
beans.producer: Northern Tolima / southern Caldas; Reforest Project cherry, processed at El Vergel Estate
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Chocolate, Sugar cane, Roasted almond, Light orange finish
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced, lively Colombian from a reforestation-led scheme in northern Tolima and southern Caldas, where farms prioritise environmental care and help neighbouring growers. Caramel, chocolate and almond with a light orange finish.

beans.name: Colombia El Silencio
beans.producer: Piendamó, Cauca; Robinson Rivera, El Silencio
beans.desc: A seasonal natural from Robinson Rivera's farm in Piendamó, Cauca. Robinson, a grower for over twenty years, picks very ripe cherries that are sorted, rested in silos, fermented and dried, giving a fruity, sweet, layered cup.

beans.name: Rwanda Musozi Natural Lot 3
beans.desc: A seasonal natural from Rwamatamu Coffee in Nyamasheke. Natural processing gives juicy, fruit-forward sweetness and a lively body, with blackberry, apricot and a floral hint. Expressive yet approachable, for espresso or filter.

beans.name: Ethiopia Guji Megadu Kickstart
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed to highlight sweetness, body and fruit clarity'
beans.listedNotes: Peach, Bergamot, Dark chocolate, Vanilla, Honey, Berries
beans.desc: A sweet, balanced coffee from Bette Buna's own Guji farm. A short oxygen-free stage before natural drying adds body and depth while keeping the classic Ethiopian natural character: familiar, but richer.

beans.name: Ethiopia Lalesa
beans.producer: Gedeb; Lalesa washing station (Ephtah Specialty Coffee); smallholder producers
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Blueberry, Peach, Black tea, Milk chocolate
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian from the Lalesa washing station in Gedeb, grown high. Ripe berries, soft peach and gentle black tea over a rounded milk chocolate sweetness; fruity without being tart. Filter brewing suits it best.

beans.name: Ethiopia Gotiti
beans.producer: Gedeo Zone, Gedeb; Gotiti washing station; smallholder producers
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Blueberry, Peach, Milk chocolate (headline); Strawberry laces, Blackberry, Apricot, Orange zest, Honey, Jasmine, Thyme, Floral tea (detail)
beans.desc: A single origin from the Gedeb district of southern Ethiopia, grown high and washed after harvest. Lively and fruit-led, with floral touches and natural sweetness; the roaster calls it clean, layered and elegant, for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Indonesia Team Pegasing CM
beans.producer: Pegasing, Sumatra; Hendra and family (farm and washing station)
beans.desc: From Hendra and his family's farm and washing station in Pegasing, Sumatra. Instead of standard wet-hulling they experiment with carbonic maceration, giving bright fruit sweetness and a smooth body for filter or espresso.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca Filadelfia
beans.producer: Antigua Valley; Dalton family, Finca Filadelfia
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated (roast profile listed as Filter)
beans.desc: A tidy, sweet, clean Guatemalan typical of the Antigua Valley. The Dalton family has grown coffee on the farm for more than 160 years, and the roaster praises their steady commitment to quality.

beans.name: Pour Star Martini
beans.producer: Huila; no producer or farm named
beans.processFull: Anaerobic fermentation with passionfruit, yeast and natural flavouring
beans.listedNotes: Passionfruit, Tropical fruit, Subtle sweetness, Smooth body, Bright juicy character
beans.desc: An experimental Colombian from Huila fermented with passionfruit, giving vivid, powerful tropical fruit with a silky mouthfeel and restrained sweetness. Suited to filter and espresso.

beans.name: Colombia Frozen Berries
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated; 'developed to highlight fruit intensity and sweetness'
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry, Raspberry, Blackberry, Plum, Red fruits, Strawberry
beans.brew: Filter (page says it can also be enjoyed as espresso)
beans.desc: An experimental Huila microlot from the Wild Collection, fermented alongside dried forest fruits for depth and sweetness. Bold and juicy with a syrupy body and long finish; best as filter.

beans.name: Colombia Simply Red
beans.producer: Huila; no producer or farm named
beans.desc: An experimental Huila lot made by co-fermentation, leaning into red berries: lively and fruity with tangy brightness, a smooth body and gentle sweetness. Suits filter and espresso.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Micro Lot 803 Honey
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Honeyed sweetness, Caramelised sugar, Sticky toffee pudding, Ripe stone fruit, Delicate florals
beans.desc: A limited-release honey-process Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate: syrupy and sweet with caramel and toffee-like notes, ripe stone fruit and delicate flowers, aimed at clarity and sweetness.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 1015
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Pink florals, Raspberry, Dried cherry, Syrupy dessert-like body, Long juicy finish
beans.desc: A limited-release natural Geisha from the Janson family estate: sweet with pink florals, raspberry and dried cherry over a syrupy, dessert-like body and a long, juicy finish.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 943
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
notes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating)
beans.listedNotes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating); description mentions clarity, sweetness, delicate floral and fruit notes
beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate, a producer known for expressive coffees. Each micro lot is grown and processed with care for clarity, natural sweetness and delicate floral and fruit character.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 1039
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
notes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating)

beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate, a producer known for expressive coffees. Each micro lot is grown and processed with care for clarity, natural sweetness and delicate floral and fruit character.

notes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating)

beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate, a producer known for expressive coffees. Each micro lot is grown and processed with care for clarity, natural sweetness and delicate floral and fruit character.

beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
notes: Not yet published (page says tasting notes are updating)

beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha from Panama's Janson family estate, a producer known for expressive coffees. Each micro lot is grown and processed with care for clarity, natural sweetness and delicate floral and fruit character.

beans.name: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 1045X
beans.producer: Janson Family Estate (Janson Coffee), 1,700 masl; Geisha
beans.listedNotes: Clarity, Florals, Sweetness (roast aim, not formal tasting notes)
beans.desc: A limited-release Geisha lot from Panama's Janson family estate, roasted to bring out clarity, florals and sweetness for an elegant, aromatic cup.

beans.name: CGLE Competition Series Laurina
beans.producer: Café Granja La Esperanza, Cerro Azul farm
beans.roastNote: Roast level not stated (roast profile listed as Filter)
beans.listedNotes: White peach, Orange blossom, Honey, Mandarin, Black tea, Cane sugar
beans.desc: A graceful, finely balanced Colombian Laurina offering bright citrus, gentle stone fruit and floral notes. Smooth sweetness carries into a neat, tea-like aftertaste that lingers.

beans.name: CGLE Competition Series XO Geisha
beans.producer: Café Granja La Esperanza, Cerro Azul farm; Geisha
beans.roastNote: Medium-light (per user; page lists roast profile as Filter)
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, Tropical fruits, Peach, Honey, Bergamot, Silky tea-like finish
beans.brew: Espresso (per user; page's brewing text is cut off and its roast profile says Filter)
beans.desc: An elegant, very expressive Colombian Geisha from Cerro Azul farm, XO-processed. Jasmine, ripe tropical and stone fruit and honey lead into a lingering tea-like finish. Made in tiny batches for competitors and enthusiasts.

beans.name: Milan
beans.producer: Ethiopian Mocha; Indian Monsoon Malabar; regions and producers not shown
beans.listedNotes: Smoky roasted almond, Caramelised demerara sugar, Chocolate, Nutty
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, flat white, latte, cafetiere, AeroPress
beans.desc: Hawkins' best-selling 100% Arabica blend of Brazil, Kenya, Colombia, Ethiopian Mocha and Indian Monsoon Malabar, pitched as the starting point in the range and the blend most cafe and home customers reorder. Smooth, sweet and clean-finishing with smoky roasted almond, caramelised demerara, chocolate and nut notes and no harshness or bitterness; works as espresso and holds up in flat whites and lattes.

beans.name: Cafe Selva
beans.listedNotes: Toffee, Butterscotch, Sweet acidity, Smoky, Spice, Full body
beans.brew: Filter, cafetiere, AeroPress; espresso (whole beans); milk drinks
beans.desc: The Fairtrade and Soil Association Organic blend, roasted medium-dark and rated 4/5 for strength. Full-bodied and smooth with toffee, butterscotch, sweet acidity and smoky spice; works as espresso and in milk drinks and is pitched at cafes serving it all day, with filter suggested for a smoother cup.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Dark chocolate, Orange, Hazelnut, Vanilla, Red apple
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, pour-over, cafetiere, AeroPress; milk
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from Huila, rated 3/5 for strength: sweet and dependable with caramel and dark chocolate up front, a soft orange note and a clean finish. Aimed at drinkers who want a single origin that is not sharp or bright; suits espresso, milk drinks and cafetiere.

beans.name: Colombian Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, Dark chocolate, Orange, Hazelnut, Vanilla, Red apple
beans.desc: Single-origin Huila decaf, decaffeinated with water only, pitched as decaf that tastes like real coffee: smooth and medium-bodied with chocolate and sweetness and none of the flatness common in decafs. Aimed at people cutting caffeine and served in the evening by its care home and hotel customers; works as espresso, filter, cafetiere or with milk.

beans.name: High Mountain Blend
beans.desc: Listing only (the product page would not load): chocolate and nut with a bright, fruity edge.

beans.name: Mocha Mysore
beans.producer: Mysore-Coorg (India); Ethiopian Mocha; producers not shown
beans.desc: A medium-roast blend of Ethiopian Mocha and beans from India's Mysore-Coorg region, rated 2/5 for strength: mellow and gentle with plenty of chocolate, some nuttiness and no sharp edges or strong acidity. Suggested for cafetiere and filter, for drinkers who find Milan too strong, or for a quieter afternoon cup.

beans.name: After Dinner Blend
beans.desc: Listing only (the product page would not load): chocolate, butterscotch, sweet acidity and a smoky note.

beans.name: Brazil Mogiana
beans.producer: Mogiana, on the Sao Paulo / Minas Gerais border; producer not shown
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from Mogiana, on the Sao Paulo / Minas Gerais border: mild with a soft body and gentle chocolate and nut flavours, subtle fruity hints and no sharp acidity. Described as an easy all-day coffee that many cafes keep alongside their main blend; works as espresso, cafetiere, with milk or on its own.

beans.name: Breakfast Blend
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Butterscotch, Sweet acidity, Smoky, Light body
beans.desc: The lighter morning coffee in the range: Colombian Huila with a little Kenyan, roasted medium and rated 3/5 for strength. Bright and clean with chocolate, butterscotch and enough acidity to wake you up without harshness, a light body and a smoky edge; works as filter or espresso and suits milk better than heavier blends. The page suggests 92-96C water.

beans.name: Continental Blend
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, Cocoa, Nutty, Molasses, Burnt caramel, Smooth
beans.brew: Espresso, cafetiere, filter, AeroPress; milk drinks
beans.desc: The darker option for drinkers who find Milan too mild, rated 4/5: South American Arabica roasted longer and darker for body, chocolate and cocoa, nuttiness, molasses and burnt caramel with a roasted finish. Popular with cafes wanting a stronger blend for milk drinks; suits espresso, cafetiere, filter and AeroPress, and Flying Scotsman is the darker step beyond it.

beans.name: Costa Rica
beans.listedNotes: Crisp acidity, Creamy body, Citrus, Sweet chocolate
beans.brew: Filter and pour-over; lighter espresso; milk drinks
beans.desc: A single-origin light roast from Tarrazu, rated 2/5 for strength: clean, bright and easy to drink, with crisp acidity, soft citrus, a touch of chocolate sweetness and a creamy body. Recommended as filter or pour-over to bring out the brightness; can be pulled as a lighter espresso and is also suggested for lattes and flat whites.

beans.name: Flying Scotsman
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Nutty, Cocoa, Molasses, Burnt caramel, Smooth
beans.brew: Espresso, moka pot, cafetiere, drip filter
beans.desc: The company's darkest, boldest coffee, rated 5/5: South American Arabica roasted longer and darker for body, plain chocolate, cocoa, molasses and burnt caramel with a roasted finish and no fruit or brightness. Cafe customers use it as a second blend for a stronger cup; suits espresso, moka pot and cafetiere, with well-textured milk.

beans.name: Java
beans.producer: Ijen Plateau, East Java; producer not shown
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Toasted nuts, Subtle herbal notes
beans.desc: A single-origin medium roast from the Ijen Plateau in East Java, at medium strength: dark chocolate, toasted nuts and subtle herbal notes, with the herbal side more noticeable in filter than espresso. One of the older single origins and a popular choice for customers who want something different from South American beans; the page suggests trying it black.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.producer: Murang'a; AA grade (hand-sorted); producer not shown
beans.desc: A single-origin Kenya AA from Murang'a (AA is the top bean-size grade, hand-sorted before leaving the farm): bright and citrusy with blackcurrant, berry, lemon and jasmine. Recommended as filter or pour-over; it also works as espresso, sharper and more vivid, for customers who want more character than a house blend.

beans.name: Kenya Peaberry
beans.listedNotes: Blackcurrant, Cherry, Chocolate, Plenty of acidity
beans.desc: A single-origin medium-roast Kenya Peaberry from Nyeri; peaberries are a single round bean rather than the usual pair, which the page says tends to give a more concentrated cup. Blackcurrant, cherry and chocolate with plenty of acidity at medium strength; best as filter or pour-over, or a sharper, fruitier espresso, for drinkers wanting more intense Kenyan character than the AA.

beans.name: Cerrado, Brazil (Decaf)
beans.producer: Cerrado, Minas Gerais; blend from hundreds of family farms, assessed by a five-person team at a Patrocinio lab; about 900m; Catuai, Mundo Novo
beans.processFull: Natural and pulped natural; sugarcane decaf
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A decaf from Cerrado in Minas Gerais, Brazil's main Arabica region and its first with an official designation of origin. Catuai and Mundo Novo cherries grown at about 900m are dried whole or partly pulped, then decaffeinated with sugarcane to keep body and sweetness. Described as rich and comforting: melted chocolate up front, fudge in the middle and a raisin-like sweetness on the finish. 43 reviews, about 88% five-star.

beans.name: El Indio, Colombia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; about 175 smallholder families; up to 2,150m; Caturra
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A natural-process Caturra from about 175 families in Planadas, southern Tolima, grown up to 2,150m in volcanic soil, then sugarcane decaffeinated to keep its sweetness. Sweet, fruity and full-bodied: dark chocolate first, then tart rhubarb and juicy pineapple. Partners have trained growers in natural processing since 2019, and most now process at least 80% of their harvest this way. 17 reviews.

beans.name: Grown Organic*, Peru (Water Decaf)
beans.producer: Various (smallholders selling to local co-ops, most farming under one hectare); 1,200-1,600m; Bourbon, Catimor, Caturra, Pache, Typica
beans.processFull: Washed; Mountain Water decaf (water from Pico de Orizaba, Mexico)
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: Peruvian smallholder coffee from steep Andean slopes at 1,200-1,600m, washed and sun-dried, then decaffeinated by the Mountain Water process (removes up to 99% of caffeine without chemicals). The page says it is Fairtrade certified and grown organically, though Craft Decaf is not organic certified. Toasty pecan, soft vanilla sponge sweetness and a zesty lemon icing finish; positioned as a smooth, sweet everyday decaf. Lightly roasted to protect the beans.

beans.name: Eastern Highlands, Papua New Guinea (Decaf)
beans.producer: Eastern Highlands; Sem Manmeri Kopi community lot from many smallholders; 1,600-1,850m; Blue Mountain, Bourbon
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A community lot called Sem Manmeri Kopi ('People's Coffee' in Tok Pisin) from smallholders in PNG's Eastern Highlands, grown at 1,600-1,850m in volcanic soil. Only the ripest cherries are hand-picked, then washed and sun-dried to keep a bright profile through sugarcane decaffeination. Chocolate and caramel with lemon curd freshness; reviewers call it smooth, balanced and not bitter.

beans.name: Popayan, Colombia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Meseta de Popayan, Cauca; about 65 farmers via import partner Cofinet; 1,700m; Caturra, Castillo
beans.processFull: Fully washed; sugarcane decaf (about 97% of caffeine removed)
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A fully washed Caturra and Castillo from the Meseta de Popayan in Cauca at about 1,700m, bought through Cofinet, which works with about 65 farmers there. Decaffeinated with sugarcane (ethyl acetate from fermented sugarcane), which the page calls the only completely natural method. Cinnamon sweetness and smooth dark chocolate with a rose finish, with a raw sweetness from the washed process.

beans.name: Bensa Bombe, Ethiopia (Decaf)
beans.producer: Bensa Bombe, Sidamo; about 650 smallholders (about 3 hectares each) via exporter Tariku Kare; 1,990-2,150m; Heirloom
beans.processFull: Natural; sugarcane decaf (97% of caffeine removed)
beans.listedNotes: Orange lolly, Caramel brittle, Red berries
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian heirloom lot from about 650 smallholders at 1,990-2,150m in Sidamo, hand-picked and dried whole on raised beds, exported by Tariku Kare, which the page says supports local communities with school supplies, household financial help and farmer training. Sugarcane decaffeinated. Sweet and sticky: bright orange lolly, then lingering caramel brittle and a faint red berry finish.

beans.name: Half Caf - Popayan, Colombia
beans.producer: Meseta de Popayan, Cauca; about 65 farmers via import partner Cofinet; Caturra, Castillo
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, French press, AeroPress, moka pot (grind-matched; omni roast)
beans.desc: Craft Decaf's first half caf, from the Meseta de Popayan in Cauca: half sugarcane-decaffeinated and half caffeinated, both washed Caturra and Castillo. Meant for balanced morning cups or an afternoon pick-me-up, with chocolate, biscuits and butterscotch. Reviewers praise the flavour and the balanced caffeine level.

beans.name: FEDERACION CAMPESINA Espresso Roast
beans.producer: Cauca; Federación Campesina del Cauca (2,000+ rural families); 1,700m; Caturra, Colombia, Typica
beans.desc: A Fairtrade-certified espresso roast of Caturra, Colombia and Typica from the Federación Campesina del Cauca, which sources from more than 2,000 rural families who avoid toxic agrochemicals and conserve native seeds, soil and water. Grown at 1,700m and fully washed; berry-forward as espresso with chocolate, blackberry, redcurrant and grape, balanced acidity and a smooth, lasting aftertaste.

beans.name: SUGAR CANE DECAF
beans.processFull: Washed; sugarcane (ethyl acetate) decaf, at least 97% caffeine removed, done in Manizales
beans.desc: A single-origin Huila decaf from Garzón, decaffeinated at a plant in Manizales with ethyl acetate made from Colombian sugarcane molasses: the beans are steamed, repeatedly washed until at least 97% of caffeine is gone, steamed again, vacuum dried and cooled. Almond, panela and a bright orange acidity.

beans.name: FEDERACION CAMPESINA Filter Roast
beans.producer: Cauca highlands; Federación Campesina del Cauca; 1,700m; Caturra, Typica
beans.desc: The filter roast of the Federación Campesina Cauca coffee: 100% Arabica, Caturra and Typica, fully washed at about 1,700m and Fair Trade from origin. Balanced with lively acidity, a full body and a smooth, lingering aftertaste, with chocolate and sweet fruit.

beans.name: OXFORD BLEND
beans.producer: 50% Finca El Porvenir, Albán, Cundinamarca (natural; Caturra, Tabi, Colombia); 50% Federación Campesina del Cauca (fully washed; Caturra, Typica); 1,600-1,700m
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, Balanced, Chocolate (espresso); Caramel, Chocolate, Almond (with milk)
beans.desc: A two-process Colombian blend, half natural coffee from Hacienda El Porvenir and half fully washed coffee from the Federación Campesina del Cauca, meant to show the strengths of both. Sweet and balanced with hints of chocolate as espresso; with whole milk it turns smooth and full-bodied, with caramel, chocolate and almond.

beans.name: FINCA EL PORVENIR
beans.producer: Albán, Cundinamarca; Finca El Porvenir, Orlando Fierro; 1,600m; Caturra, Tabi
beans.listedNotes: Honey, Vanilla, Dried peach (aroma); Roast cacao, Chocolate finish
beans.desc: A red-honey coffee from a small Andean farm run by Orlando Fierro, uncle of the roaster's co-founder Milly. In red honey processing the cherry is partly pulped but the sticky mucilage stays on while drying, giving a syrupy body with more intensity than washed coffees and a richer character than naturals; balanced acidity, creamy body, roast cacao and a chocolate finish.

beans.name: Finca Tamaná Natural Process (Filter Roast)
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: A natural-process Castillo and Colombia from Elías Roa and his wife at Finca Tamaná in Huila, at 1,750m; the page says leading roasters and coffee houses favour their coffees and give feedback on improving production. Peach, nutty and dried fruit notes.

beans.name: Finca Tamaná Natural Process (Espresso Roast)
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Castillo, Colombia
beans.desc: The espresso roast of the Finca Tamaná natural lot from Elías Roa and his wife in Huila (Castillo and Colombia, 1,750m), with peach, nutty and dried fruit notes.

beans.name: Half Caff Blend
beans.producer: La Falda, Garzón (Huila) and Inza (Cauca); decaf half is the Sugar Cane Decaf; 1,000-1,900m; Caturra, Castillo, Colombia, Typica
beans.processFull: Washed; decaf half by the sugarcane method
beans.listedNotes: Almond, Raw cane sugar, Hazelnut, Berries
beans.desc: A half-caffeinated blend of the roaster's sugarcane decaf with a washed coffee from Inza, Cauca, where smallholders dry their crops at the farm of Jesús Volvera, which shields the beans from unpredictable rain. Positioned as an everyday energy source with less caffeine; almond, raw cane sugar, hazelnut and berries.

beans.name: EL LATINO BLEND
beans.producer: Several small farms; no region named
beans.desc: A blend of the harvests of several small Colombian farms, designed for espresso and described as sweet and balanced.

beans.name: El Indio Microlot Natural Process (Filter Roast)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; several family farms; 1,500-2,150m; Caturra
beans.desc: A limited-edition natural Caturra from family farms in Planadas, Tolima, some from indigenous communities who work with local cooperatives to improve farming and master natural processing. The roaster credits the natural process for the sweet, fruity character.

beans.name: El Indio Microlot Natural Process (Espresso Roast)
beans.producer: Planadas, Tolima; several family farms; 1,500-2,150m; Caturra
beans.desc: The espresso roast of the El Indio natural microlot from Planadas, Tolima: Caturra from several family farms, sweet and fruity thanks to natural processing.

beans.name: Café Sofía Espresso Roast
beans.producer: Antioquia, Risaralda and Valle del Cauca; Santa Teresita mill; 1,500m; mix of Arabica varieties
beans.listedNotes: Milk caramel, Mandarin, Creamy toffee, Chocolate chip cookie
beans.desc: A blend of washed Arabicas from three Colombian regions, graded and sorted at the Santa Teresita mill and roasted for espresso; rich aroma and pleasant acidity with milk caramel, mandarin, creamy toffee and chocolate chip cookie.

beans.name: CABALLERO ESPRESSO Special Edition
beans.producer: Huila; Finca Tamaná, Elías Roa and his wife; 1,750m; Papayo
beans.listedNotes: Fruity, Red wine, Red and black berries
beans.desc: A special edition of the roaster's classic Gentleman's Espresso using Papayo, a large-beaned variety named for its papaya-like shape, natural-processed at Finca Tamaná in Huila by long-term partner Elías Roa; a balanced espresso shot with natural-process sweetness and a rich, fruity aroma.

beans.name: Foundation Beans: Cafe Vida Washed, Costa Rica
beans.producer: Central Valley; imported by Cafe Imports via Oxcart Coffee; 1,200-1,800m; common Costa Rican varieties (Caturra, Catuai, Bourbon, Villa Sarchi and others)
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.listedNotes: Rounded sweetness, Mellow acidity, Full mouthfeel
beans.desc: The roaster's Foundation tier: a washed Costa Rican that shows the country's rounded sweetness, mellow acidity and full mouthfeel, from Cafe Imports' Oxcart sourcing programme, which works with the same micromills each year.

beans.name: Discovery Beans: Aceh Gayo Natural, Indonesia
beans.producer: Pegasing District, Aceh, Sumatra; Asman Gayo Mill (Asman Arianto); 1,300-1,650m; Ateng, Bor Bor, Catimor, Timor
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.desc: A natural-processed Sumatran that the roaster rarely sources, since wet-hulled lots tend to taste earthy and herbaceous; this one keeps the body and bold fruit of Indonesian coffee with blackcurrant, a spiced finish and a winey depth.

beans.name: Rare Beans: Gara Agena Natural, Ethiopia
beans.producer: Karamo, Bura, Sidama; Gara Agena washing station (Testi Coffee, Faysel Abdosh Yonis); 2,235-2,350m; Ethiopian heirloom
beans.roastNote: Filter or espresso roast (chosen at purchase)
beans.desc: A natural heirloom lot from Gara Agena, a steep hillside site at about 2,250m above the Geta River, overseen by Testi Coffee's Faysel A. Yonis, who has traded coffee since he was a schoolboy; rich, ripe, blueberry-like fruit.

beans.name: Gesha Beans: El Cerro Washed, Peru
beans.producer: El Corazón, Chirinos, Cajamarca; El Cerro farm, Yulisa Carhuallocllo Arévalo; 1,875-1,950m; Gesha
beans.processFull: Washed with 72-hour dry fermentation in tanks
beans.desc: A washed Gesha from Yulisa Carhuallocllo, who learned coffee from her father (second at Peru's first Cup of Excellence in 2017) and won Best of Cajamarca in 2023 and again in October 2025 with 90.25 points; dry-fermented for 72 hours in tanks with no added water. Floral with fruity sweetness and a tea-like finish.

beans.name: SOLO
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; smallholders via the Regional Select Programme; 1,400-2,200m; Bourbon, Catimor, Caturra, Maragogype, Pache
beans.listedNotes: Molasses sweetness, Gentle berry acidity, Syrupy body
beans.desc: A seasonal single-origin Guatemalan from Huehuetenango smallholders selling through a collective programme that rewards quality and keeps value in the region: molasses sweetness, gentle berry acidity, a heavy syrupy body and a long finish.

beans.name: TRIO
beans.producer: 34% Araku Valley (India), 33% Mchana AB (Kenya), 33% Mount Sunzu (Zambia)
beans.listedNotes: Complex fruit, Floral aromatics, Good acidity, Sweet syrupy body
beans.desc: A seasonal espresso blend from the Discovery range that pairs washed African coffees with an Indian one for lively acidity and a sweet, syrupy body, curated for consistency season to season on a clean house espresso base.

beans.name: Decaf Beans: Rwanda Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Smallholders; region not shown; 1,500-2,000m; Red Bourbon, Jackson, Mibirizi, BM139
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from Rwanda decaffeinated with sugarcane, keeping the stewed fruit and spice flavours typical of Rwandan coffee; the roaster's first Rwandan decaf, following an earlier Ethiopian one.

beans.name: Dos Pueblos (house espresso blend)
beans.producer: 67% Minas Gerais (Association of Producers of the Volcanic Region, via Vequis); 33% Udessa, Yirgacheffe (Mulugeta Tsige Exporters); 800-2,400m; Ethiopian 74158, Kurume, Dega
beans.processFull: Brazil natural; Ethiopia washed (48h tank fermentation)
beans.desc: The house espresso blend: a 67% natural Brazilian from smallholders of the Volcanic Region, adding milk-chocolate, caramel and a smooth medium body, with 33% washed Ethiopian microlot from Udessa for fruit-forward acidity. Sweet, smooth and balanced, for use alone or with milk.

beans.name: Caña Decaf
beans.producer: Huila; smallholders via Café Imports; Castillo, Caturra
beans.processFull: Pulped, fermented, washed; sugarcane (ethyl acetate) decaf
beans.listedNotes: Hazelnut praline, Milk chocolate, Caramel sweetness
beans.desc: A sweet, rich Huila decaf from smallholders, with caffeine removed using ethyl acetate derived from sugarcane fermentation, applied to steamed green beans in repeated tank cycles. Works as espresso or filter; harvested June-August 2024 and landed in the UK in November 2024.

beans.name: Blueberried
beans.producer: Edinson Argote, Quebraditas farm (Colombia); Mustefa Abakeno, Beshasha washing station, Jimma (Ethiopia, 2,040m); Caturra, Heirloom
beans.processFull: Colombian blueberry and wine-yeast co-ferment; Ethiopian washed
beans.desc: A Colombian Caturra co-fermented with ripe blueberries and wine yeast, blended with a washed Ethiopian heirloom for citrus brightness and structure. Concentrated blueberry sorbet and grape soda character.

beans.name: Gley Diaz
beans.producer: Nueva York hamlet, Amazonas; Gley Diaz, smallholder; Geisha
beans.processFull: Washed; 18-24h fermentation, dried on raised beds in covered tunnels (about 25 days)
beans.desc: The first lot from Gley Diaz, who grows Geisha on small family plots in the cloud-forested highlands of Amazonas, introduced via export partner Collective Bean. Clean, refined and elegant with apricot, wildflower honey and soft florals.

beans.name: Rumudamo
beans.producer: Sidama; Rumudamo station (Daye Bensa), about 600 smallholders; up to 2,200m; Heirloom
beans.processFull: Natural; dried whole on raised beds 3+ weeks
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, Tropical, Floral, Jasmine as it cools
beans.desc: A sweet, floral natural from Daye Bensa's Rumudamo station, which placed second and third at Ethiopia's first Cup of Excellence in 2020 and funds preschools and processing classes for farmers' children. Layered strawberry and tropical fruit turning to jasmine as it cools.

beans.name: Nafkot
beans.producer: Gedicho, Yirgacheffe; Nafkot Admasu, 2-hectare farm; 2,170m; Heirloom
beans.listedNotes: Peach iced tea, Wild berries, Tropical fruit
beans.desc: Grown by Nafkot Admasu under native enset trees on her own 2-hectare farm with its own processing station. Part of the Ama Commitment Project (Ephtah Coffee) for female producers; bought via Covoya. Peach iced tea, wild berries and tropical fruit.

beans.name: Bookkisa
beans.producer: Bookkisa kebele, Shakiso, Guji; Sookoo Coffee (Ture Waji); 2,000-2,150m; Gibirinna 74110, Serto 74112
beans.desc: A clean, fruit-forward natural from smallholders delivering to the Bookkisa washing station run by family-owned Sookoo Coffee, dried in thin layers and turned at least six times daily. Two Jimma Research Centre selections; blueberry, honey and raspberry.

beans.name: Sumatra Mandheling
beans.listedNotes: Very full flavour, Heavy low notes
beans.desc: A washed Arabica Sumatra Mandheling described as very full in flavour without burnt characteristics. The dense bean needs about 14 minutes of roasting; heavy, low notes.

beans.name: Colombia Excelso Fairtrade
beans.desc: A medium-roasted washed Colombian, balanced and lemony with mild acidity and gentle body; presented as a good introduction to speciality coffee.

beans.name: Jersey Blend
beans.desc: A classic washed Arabica blend from Central America, sold as a taste of Jersey to enjoy anywhere.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe (Hama Co-operative)
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe; Hama Co-operative (from URL and tags)
beans.desc: A medium-roast washed Yirgacheffe with pronounced fruit balanced by gentle underlying sweetness, presented as a good representative of the region.

beans.name: Morning Coffee
beans.desc: A morning blend described as smooth and easy to drink, a good start to the day.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.desc: A coffee aged for three years for a smooth, heavy flavour; the roast removes off-flavours picked up during maturing so it stays lively. Aimed at people unsure about dark roast who want something on the darker side.

beans.name: Bologne Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Daterra estate (Brazil Arabica); Sethuraman estate (southern India Robusta)
beans.listedNotes: Low acidity, Full body, Smooth (description only)
beans.desc: A medium-roast Arabica and Robusta blend that mimics a classic European coffee style: low acidity, full and smooth body.

beans.name: Brazil Daterra Santa Colomba (Medium Roasted)
beans.producer: Daterra Farm; Cerrado (Minas Gerais) and Mogiana (São Paulo)
beans.listedNotes: Gentle acidity, Caramel finish, Delicate sweetness
beans.desc: A medium roast from Daterra Farm with soft acidity and a caramel-toned finish; as espresso it is light and delicately sweet, suiting cappuccinos. The roaster has bought from this farm for years.

beans.name: Bourbon Dark Espresso Blend
beans.desc: One of the shop's most popular espresso coffees, also good in a cafetiere: Sumatran and Brazilian Arabica with speciality Indian Robusta for a heavy, smooth and rich cup.

beans.name: Heritage Blend
beans.roastNote: Dark Java with much lighter Malabar
beans.desc: An espresso blend created in 2021 by shop manager Josh from two aged heritage coffees, Malabar and Java. Pairing darker Java with much lighter Malabar gives a deep, rich coffee, especially good as cappuccino.

beans.name: Coopers Red Packet (coffee and chicory)
beans.desc: A ground blend of 70% robusta and 30% chicory reviving the Jersey tradition of Breton farmers stretching coffee with roasted chicory.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.processFull: Washed; extra 8-16h soak in clean water, sun-dried
beans.desc: A washed blend from Nyeri smallholders, processed with recirculated river water and a Kenyan-style extended soak before sun-drying; deep dark chocolate and red fruit.

beans.name: Colombia Excelso
beans.brew: V60, French press, AeroPress or moka pot
beans.desc: A single-origin Colombian roasted medium-dark for a strong, heavy-bodied cup with caramel, chocolate and red apple. No farm, variety or process given. Suits French press, V60, AeroPress and moka pot.

beans.name: House Espresso
beans.producer: Not shown; Caturra, Castillo, Typica, Catuai, Mundo Novo
beans.desc: The roaster's signature espresso blend of Brazil, Colombia and El Salvador, developed for espresso and home bean-to-cup machines; a chocolatey darker roast with a caramel finish.

beans.name: Morning Blend
notes: Nutty (Colombian Excelso adds citron and lemon)
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, Nutty (Colombian Excelso adds citron and lemon)
beans.brew: Any (espresso to cafetiere per grind guide)
beans.desc: A dark-roast blend of Colombian Excelso and Vietnamese coffee sold as a morning pick-me-up, with dark chocolate and nut flavours.

beans.name: Ethiopia Limu
beans.brew: Espresso or moka pot (roaster says best suited)
beans.desc: A washed heirloom from Limu grown at 1,500-1,900m, roasted medium; the roaster rates it best as espresso or moka pot, with chocolate, blackberry and orange.

beans.name: Seasonal Winter Warmer
beans.brew: Any (bean-to-cup, V60; good with steamed milk)
beans.desc: A seasonal blend of a fruity Ethiopian and a richer, rum-like El Salvadoran, likened by the roaster to Christmas pudding.

beans.name: The Clubhouse Coffee
beans.producer: Not shown; Catuai, Mundo Novo, Heirloom
beans.desc: A sweet, versatile Brazil and Ethiopia blend made with The Clubhouse Project, a Surrey day service for young adults with learning disabilities; 50p from every bag goes to the charity.

beans.name: Rwanda Coproca
beans.producer: Nyamasheke, Western Province; Kanjongo Sector; 603 smallholders; 1,800m (1,830-1,950m in text); Red Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Apple, Liquorice, Black tea, Caramel, Dark chocolate
beans.brew: Any (espresso to cold brew per grind guide)
beans.desc: A natural Red Bourbon from 603 smallholders in Nyamasheke, selected, floated and dried 35-40 days on raised beds; sweet and fruity with apple, liquorice and black tea.

beans.name: Brazil Monteiro Lobato
beans.producer: Rio Pardo; Ocafi blend from farms around Fazenda Pinheiro
beans.processFull: Natural (patio dried 12 days, mechanical 10h, rested 15 days)
beans.desc: A smooth, balanced natural from the Rio Pardo region, blended by Ocafi from neighbouring farms around Fazenda Pinheiro, with chocolate, hazelnut and vanilla.

beans.name: Costa Rica Decaffeinated
beans.brew: French press, V60, AeroPress or moka pot
beans.desc: A single-origin Costa Rican Red Catuai decaffeinated with CO2, roasted medium-dark for a strong cup with pear, cherry, cacao nibs and liquorice.

beans.name: Rwanda Karengera
beans.producer: Nyamasheke, Western Province; Karengera washing station; 11 smallholders; 1,600-1,850m; Red Bourbon
beans.listedNotes: Raspberry, Cherry, Black tea, Jasmine, Toffee
beans.brew: Any (espresso to cold brew per grind guide)
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from 11 smallholders delivering to the Karengera washing station, grown on volcanic soil; raspberry, cherry, black tea, jasmine and toffee.

beans.name: El Salvador Borbollon
beans.producer: El Borbollon mill; 19 farms, Apaneca-Ilamatepec range; 1,300-1,400m; Red Bourbon
beans.processFull: Washed; fermented overnight, patio dried 8-10 days
beans.brew: Any (espresso to cold brew per grind guide)
beans.desc: A blend of 19 RFA-certified farms assembled at the El Borbollon mill by the Alvarez family, washed and patio dried, hand sorted by about 40 women; stone fruit, milk chocolate and hazelnut.

beans.name: Clubhouse Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A classic-style espresso blend that tones down acidity.

beans.name: Fazenda Pantano
beans.producer: Cerrado, Minas Gerais; Fazenda Pantano (Ferrero family)
beans.desc: A natural Yellow Bourbon from a 550-hectare Cerrado farm.

beans.name: B-SIDE Blend
beans.desc: A fruitier blend suited to black coffee and flat whites.

beans.name: Atunkaa SICEET Decaf
beans.desc: A decaf from an indigenous Nasa farmer association in Cauca.

beans.name: Nyabumera 1033
beans.desc: A natural Red Bourbon from the Nyabumera washing station.

beans.name: Hacienda La Luisa
beans.desc: A washed Costa Rican coffee from a farm bought in 1954.

beans.name: Bochesa
beans.desc: A natural Sidama coffee from a smallholder-supplied washing station.

beans.name: Bibiana Mena Narino Micro Lot
beans.producer: El Tambo, Nariño; Finca La Cumbre (Lopez Mena)
beans.desc: A washed single-origin from a family farm in Nariño.

beans.name: FILTER FOCUS Los Nubarrones
beans.producer: Mozonte, Nueva Segovia; Los Nubarrones (Mariano Montealegre)
beans.desc: A lighter roast suited to filter brewing.

beans.name: Afternoon Blend
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: Blend of beans from Central America, South America and Africa, with a caramel sweetness (summary of the roaster's page).

beans.name: Coffee Break Blend
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: Arabica blend of two varieties from Central and South America, naturally sweet and low in acidity, with nougat, caramel and wafer notes; suggested for filter, espresso or cafetiere and best from day six after roasting (summary of the roaster's page).

beans.name: My Time Blend
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A mild blend with some Robusta so the flavour holds up in milk.

beans.name: Really Nice Blend
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A sweet, citrusy Arabica blend with mixed-fruit flavour.

beans.name: Honduras SHG
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: High-altitude beans with fruity acidity settling to a caramel finish.

beans.name: Colombian Supremo
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A full-bodied coffee with sweet, cherry-like fruitiness.

beans.name: Nicaragua Plan Vivo
beans.producer: Jinotega and Matagalpa; co-operative of 2,655 farmers
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: Organic coffee grown under the Plan Vivo carbon-capture scheme.

beans.name: Everyday Blend
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A soft blend with thick crema and natural sweetness.

beans.name: Brazil Donas
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: Thick crema, fruity notes and a syrupy natural sweetness.

beans.name: Peruvian Swiss Water Decaf
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A high-altitude decaf with sweet aroma and mild acidity.

beans.name: Smooth Sensation
beans.brew: AeroPress, filter, espresso, French press, moka pot
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A rich, smooth blend with dark crema and low acidity.

beans.name: Dark Spice Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark cocoa, treacle, smoky spicy finish
beans.brew: AeroPress, filter, espresso, French press, moka pot
beans.source: Corby Coffee Roasting Co product page
beans.desc: A blend of two aged coffees with a lingering smoky, spicy taste.

beans.name: Brazilian Avela
beans.producer: Fazenda Campo Alegre, Cerrado Mineiro (Cafe Delas women-farmer programme)
beans.desc: A natural Cerrado Mineiro coffee from a woman-run farm.

beans.name: Burundi
beans.desc: A fruity, lively coffee with firm acidity, reminiscent of Malbec.

beans.name: Colombia Excelso Decaf
beans.desc: A caramel and chocolate base with citrus and red apple acidity.

beans.name: Oolite Blend
beans.desc: A Kenyan blend intended for filter brewing.

beans.name: Quack Quacks Blend Americas
beans.desc: A blend of two honey-processed coffees with a sweet, rich finish.

beans.name: Guatemalan Coffee
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan from Huehuetenango.

beans.name: Decaffeinated Coffee
beans.desc: A seasonal Swiss Water decaf chosen each year.

beans.name: Somerford Breakfast Blend
beans.desc: A breakfast blend made for a village coffee morning.

beans.name: Rwandan Coffee
beans.desc: A washed Bourbon from Lake Kivu.

beans.name: Colombian Coffee
beans.desc: A natural Colombian from Anserma, Caldas.

beans.name: Sumatran Coffee
beans.desc: A double-picked medium-roast Sumatran recommended for V60.

beans.name: Costa Rica Coffee
beans.desc: A black honey Tarrazú with added sweetness and fuller body.

beans.name: Half Caf House Blend
beans.desc: A blend of a fruity Colombian single origin and a naturally decaffeinated Colombian, roasted separately.

beans.name: Mexico Bankilal
beans.producer: Los Altos de Chiapas, Tenejapa Communities
beans.desc: A smooth, easy-drinking, complex coffee grown in shade under traditional milpa farming by the Tenejapa communities of Los Altos de Chiapas. The name honours the Tzeltal "older brother" figure who protects the community. Described as ridiculously easy to drink on espresso or filter.

beans.name: Ethiopia Chelichele
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian grown under Enset trees and sun-dried on raised beds.

beans.name: Mexico Juba
beans.producer: Guerrero, Montaña Alta; Me'phaa families (via Ensambles)
beans.desc: A natural from shade-grown smallholder farms, fruit-forward and distinct.

beans.name: Guatemala Finca Gomez
beans.desc: Hand-crafted at a local wet mill by a first-generation producer and her family.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Aracacu
beans.producer: Três Pontas, Fazenda Aracaçu; Carmem Lucia
beans.desc: A creamy, velvety micro-lot from a multi-award-winning estate.

beans.name: Burundi Masenga Hill
beans.desc: A balanced Burundian with citrus aromatics and brown sugar sweetness.

beans.name: El Salvador El Molino
beans.desc: A rich, chocolate-forward coffee with citrus-toned brightness.

beans.name: Brazil Bossa Nova
beans.producer: Cerrado and Sul de Minas; Volcafe Santos (~600 farms)
beans.desc: A smooth, crowd-pleasing natural Brazilian with soft sweetness.

beans.name: Colombia El Muro
beans.desc: A full-bodied, complex coffee; bronze at the Global Coffee Awards (Europe) single-origin espresso category.

beans.name: Development House Blend (espresso)
beans.desc: A bold, modern-classic dark blend that suits milky drinks and works black.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia Tumbaga
beans.desc: A bright, sweet washed decaf with flavour retained through decaffeination.

beans.name: Shoondhisa Anaerobic Natural
beans.producer: Guji; Sookoo Coffee (Ture Waji), via Osito
beans.processFull: Anaerobic natural (86h in Grain Pro, raised beds)
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
beans.desc: A bright, clean Guji natural with floral notes and acidity from extended anoxic fermentation.

beans.name: Edinson Argote, Finca Quebraditas TS Orange Bourbon
beans.processFull: Anaerobic washed, yeast inoculated, thermal shock
beans.desc: A standout Orange Bourbon processed with advanced methods; rest 3 weeks after roast.

beans.name: Rumudamo Anaerobic Washed
beans.producer: Arbegona, Sidama; Rumudamo village lot (Daye Bensa)
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
