beans.name: Inmaculada Fellows Bourbon Aji
beans.producer: Valle del Cauca; Inmaculada Coffee Farms and Fellows partner farms
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
beans.desc: A complex Colombian with tropical fruit, juicy citrus and dry vermouth-like sweetness.

beans.name: El Jaragual TS Washed Pink Bourbon
beans.producer: Amalfi, Antioquia; El Jaragual farm (via MiCafe)
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
beans.desc: A washed, thermal-shock Pink Bourbon from a farm bought from for four years.

beans.name: Carlos Hernandez Natural
beans.producer: Sierra Sur, Oaxaca; Carlos Hernandez (Union San Pedro)
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
beans.desc: One of the first Mexican naturals from a grower the roaster visited.

beans.name: Eddy Macdonald Lopez Lopez - Finca La Gardenia
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; Eddy Macdonald Lopez Lopez, Finca La Gardenia
beans.roastNote: Not stated (roasted in Exeter, Loring S15)
beans.brew: Cafetière, V60, AeroPress, moka pot, espresso
beans.desc: A natural Marsellesa from a high-altitude, conservation-focused farm.

beans.name: Rumudamo Washed

Cherries are pre-sorted and hand-sorted at the Gigesa station, floated, then dried 15-21 days on raised African beds to 11-12% moisture. Red fruits, molasses, tangerine and blackcurrant; score 87.

beans.name: Nensebo Mundayo

beans.brew: Espresso, moka pot, AeroPress, filter, French press
beans.desc: An exceptional heirloom lot from Mundayo village in the Refisa municipality of Nensebo District, Oromia, grown at 1,945-2,100m by about 750 smallholders who deliver to the family-owned AASH-Testi Coffee Washing Station. An improved washed process: cherries are depulped within 6-8 hours, fermented 36-48 hours, washed in channels until the water runs clear and dried slowly on raised beds under shade nets. Black tea, honey and grapefruit; score 87.

beans.name: Mr Claus Christmas Blend
beans.producer: San Ignacio, northern Peru; Santa Mónica farm, Armenia, Quindío, Colombia (Jairo Arcila)
beans.processFull: Colombian component: 48-hour anaerobic cinnamon co-ferment in sealed tanks, then washed and slowly dried
beans.listedNotes: Cinnamon bun, cacao nib, brown sugar, a twist of lime
beans.brew: Black, with milk; espresso, moka pot, AeroPress, filter, French press
beans.desc: Mr Claus is the steady, warm and spiced centre of Christmas: the much-loved San Ignacio bean from northern Peru paired with a mischievous Colombian lot from Jairo Arcila's Santa Mónica farm in Armenia, Quindío, where Castillo grows at about 1,500m in volcanic soil. The ripe cherries ferment 48 hours in sealed tanks with cinnamon before being washed and slowly dried, so it tastes like a cinnamon bun with no flavourings. Rich, sweet and softly spiced; lovely black and holds up well with milk.

beans.name: Mrs Claus Christmas Blend

beans.desc: Mrs Claus is the bright, fruity, slightly indulgent half of the Christmas pair (Mr Claus is warm and spiced). Two washed Kenyan AB coffees, Nyota (1,500-2,000m, Central Highlands: berries, plum, caramel, gentle spice) and Adumu (volcanic Central Kenya, up to 2,000m: cherry, raspberry, milk chocolate, a hint of cola), join a rare Colombian Chiroso grown by Jairo Arcila at Santa Mónica, Quindío, fermented 45 hours and dried whole in the cherry (88.75 points). Like a slice of Christmas cake: plum, cherry, raspberry, caramel and chocolate with a hint of spice. Best black as a pour-over or filter, sweet enough for espresso.

beans.name: Replay
beans.desc: The coffee the roaster has spent years perfecting and takes home: balanced rather than showy, with natural sweetness, good body, a pleasant acidity and enough complexity to stay interesting. Brazilian Daterra brings body and sweetness with cocoa and a slight nuttiness, Guatemala adds milk chocolate with pear and subtle florality, and Colombia lifts it with strawberry and sweet citrus. Toffee, milk chocolate and strawberry, medium roast; best for espresso, stove top and cafetiere.

beans.name: Ember
beans.origin: Brazil (Black Strix, CARPEC cooperative, Cerrado), Colombia (Excelso)
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, almond, molasses; low acidity
beans.desc: The blend the roaster has been perfecting since day one and still one of the most popular: deeper flavour notes, low acidity, built for the morning. Brazilian Black Strix from the CARPEC cooperative in Cerrado with a Colombian Excelso, taken to a medium dark roast. Dark chocolate, molasses and almond; delicious with milk and takes a sprinkle of sugar well. Best for stove top, espresso and cafetiere.

beans.name: Blossom
beans.listedNotes: Nectarine, apple, honey; fruit, sweet acidity, floral aftertaste
beans.desc: Repetition's omni roast, built to work across espresso and filter. It began as an experimental espresso blend and became an evergreen filter favourite. Brazilian Daterra, Ethiopian Sidamo and a natural Monte Cristo from Nicaragua, taken to a medium light roast to keep fruit and florals intact. Nectarine, apple and honey; as espresso, fruit, sweet acidity and a floral aftertaste.

beans.name: Swiss Water - Decaf
beans.desc: A single origin Colombia Excelso decaffeinated by the Swiss Water process, which uses only water, temperature and time with no chemical solvents. Roasted medium light to hold onto the milk chocolate and caramel sweetness while letting the citrus through. Made for people who drink decaf for the flavour rather than as a compromise; works with any brew method.

beans.name: Workhorse
notes: cola nut and black tea from the Limu
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, cacao, nectarine; cola nut and black tea from the Limu
beans.desc: The roaster's pick for oat or other milk alternatives and a go-to for iced lattes. Roasted a little further than Replay, towards the complexity of good dark chocolate without the bitterness. Brazilian Savannah (Daterra's sister farm) with a washed Ethiopian Limu, giving caramel, cacao and nectarine with enough going on to stand up to milk.

beans.name: Colombia Viani - Single Origin
beans.producer: Vianí, Cundinamarca; collected by Sr Joseel Castiblanco, about 90 producers (Racafe CRECER programme)
beans.listedNotes: Mandarin, caramel, molasses; bright acidity, medium body
beans.desc: A coffee that represents Cundinamarca, just outside Bogotá, chosen for Racafe's balanced acidity and clean fruit. Gathered by collector Sr Joseel Castiblanco from around 90 producers working to Racafe's CRECER programme; cherry is depulped the same day, fermented 48 hours, dried, then sorted and cupped twice in Bogotá. Mandarin, caramel and molasses with a bright acidity and medium body. Roasted light, best through filter.

beans.name: Costa Rica Hermosa - Single Origin
beans.producer: Santa María de Dota; Coope Dota cooperative (about 1,100 members)
beans.listedNotes: Grapefruit, plum, toffee, apple; about as sweet as a washed coffee gets, big body
beans.desc: A lot from Coope Dota, the Santa María de Dota cooperative that began in 1960 with 96 producers and now represents around 1,100, and was the first coffee processor certified carbon neutral (2011). Dry fermented 16-18 hours, washed and dried slowly below 40°C. As sweet as a washed coffee gets with a big body: grapefruit and apple up front, plum and toffee underneath. Roasted light, best through filter.

beans.name: Daterra Stardust - Single Origin
beans.listedNotes: Nectarine, pineapple, peach, apricot; sugar cane sweetness; velvety texture
beans.desc: A Brazilian that does not behave like most Brazilians: Yellow Bourbon dried whole on the tree for a velvety texture and lots of ripe fruit. From Daterra in the Cerrado, a carbon negative farm and the first coffee farm to become a B Corp, of which 3,500 of 6,300 hectares are protected forest. Roasted light: nectarine, pineapple, peach and apricot with sugar cane sweetness. Works on all brew methods; the roaster makes it as filter.

beans.name: Nicaragua Monte Cristo - Single Origin
beans.producer: Monte Cristo farm, Peñas Blancas, Jinotega; producer Victor Robelo; Las Nubes dry mill
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, milk chocolate, brown sugar; strong tropical fruit, lower acidity, slightly boozy
beans.brew: Espresso, filter, AeroPress, batch brew, cafetiere, cold brew
beans.desc: A natural from Victor Robelo's Monte Cristo farm in Peñas Blancas, Jinotega, bordering the Peñas Blancas Massif reserve (part of Bosawás). Slow ripening in fog and shade builds density and sweetness; hand-picked and dried 35-40 days on shaded raised beds at the Las Nubes mill. Strawberry, milk chocolate and brown sugar with strong tropical fruit, lower acidity and a boozy edge. Works as filter, espresso and cold brew.

beans.name: Siena

beans.name: Decaf Colombia Huila
beans.producer: Huila and Tolima; smallholder farms ("El Buho")
beans.desc: A sugarcane-process decaf from smallholders in Huila and Tolima that keeps the character and sweetness of Colombian Arabica. Toasted nuts, golden syrup and lemonade; performs across a range of roast profiles.

beans.name: Decaf Guatemala Antigua
beans.producer: Antigua (also Atitlan, Nuevo Oriente); El Durazno, San Jeronimo, Rabanales, San Jorge, Gascon
beans.desc: A rich, full-bodied sugarcane-process decaf from farms in Atitlan, Antigua and Nuevo Oriente. Orange, almond and pineapple.

beans.name: Wake Up Espresso
beans.desc: A dark-roast espresso blend of Guatemalan and Papua New Guinean coffees, described as a kick start in a cup. Dark chocolate, caramel and stone fruit.

beans.name: Move
beans.desc: A blend of Papua New Guinea and Colombia coffees, roasted a little darker as a pre-exercise boost. Chocolate, praline and orange marmalade.

beans.name: Create
beans.roastNote: Light to medium (described as a lighter roast)
beans.desc: A lighter-roast Colombia and Guatemala filter blend for the afternoon slump; more delicate in flavour but still able to deliver a boost. Milk chocolate, butter toffee and cherry.

beans.name: Indulge Decaf
beans.desc: A specialty decaf from Huila, Colombia, for coffee flavour without the caffeine, roasted medium to bring out its full character. Citrus fruit, shortbread and almond.

beans.name: Para Ti - Colombia - Gran Galope
beans.desc: A washed single origin from El Tambo in Colombia's Cauca region, grown high in the central volcanic mountain range. Chocolatey and sweet with fruity notes of pear and orange. Part of the roaster-selected Para Ti ("for you") range.

beans.name: Bilong Yu - Papua New Guinea
beans.desc: A rich, sweet and smooth coffee from the Wahgi Valley in the Western Highlands of Papua New Guinea, and a best-selling base for Cuckfield's Wake Up espresso blend. Big, bold cocoa and toffee with subtler liquorice and citrus.

beans.name: Para Ti - Guatemala Huehuetenango
beans.desc: A single-origin Guatemalan from Huehuetenango, chosen for its clear regional character, where indigenous communities play a large role in production. Crisp acidity with lemon, grape and apple, balanced by toffee and sweet almond. Cupping score 87.

beans.name: Manesty Wood Signature Blend
beans.producer: Bom Jesus and Sao Lucas (per description)
beans.processFull: Not stated for the Brazilian blend
beans.listedNotes: Creamy, sweet caramel, cocoa; milky chocolate; balanced acidity
beans.desc: A Lake District-inspired blend of two Brazilian coffees, Bom Jesus and Sao Lucas, named after Manesty Wood beside Derwentwater beneath Catbells. Rich and indulgent, with creamy texture, sweet caramel and a hint of cocoa.

beans.name: Dawn Chorus Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Karambi, Kasese District, Rwenzori foothills (importer Agri Evolve)
beans.listedNotes: Red fruit sweetness, milky chocolate, caramel, cocoa, blackberry
beans.desc: Darkhouse's signature espresso blend, roasted in the Lake District from direct-trade Karambi beans from the Rwenzori foothills, sourced via Agri Evolve. Sweet caramel, cocoa and blackberry with red fruit and milky chocolate; SCA 84.

beans.name: Stone Circle
beans.producer: Ibanda/Katanda, Kasese District, Rwenzori foothills (importer Agri Evolve)
beans.listedNotes: Stone fruit acidity, milk chocolate, caramel
beans.desc: A natural, fermented and sun-dried Ugandan single origin from Ibanda in the Rwenzori foothills, sourced via Agri Evolve. Well structured, sweet and fruity with good body: stone fruit acidity, milk chocolate and hints of caramel. SCA 84.

beans.name: Nature is my Buzz (Decaffeinated)
beans.desc: A Swiss Water decaffeinated Peruvian coffee imported by Rawmaterial, from Bourbon, Catucai, Caturra and Typicaff varieties. Caramel, dark chocolate and citrus.

beans.name: Early Summit
beans.producer: Kaptagat; Lot 20 Coffee (Kericho and Bomet counties)
beans.listedNotes: Prune, brown sugar, berry fruit sweetness
beans.desc: A natural Kenyan single origin from Lot 20 Coffee, founded in 2019 by Sidney Kibet to export carefully selected lots from smallholders in western Kenya, with its own Metibellion washing station in Kericho. Dominant prune and brown sugar followed by berry fruit sweetness.

beans.name: Brazil Eagle Monte Carmelo
beans.producer: Cerrado Mineiro; Andrea Ribeiro Silva, Fazenda Aragao (Cafe Delas Program)
beans.desc: A Brazilian from Cerrado Mineiro, grown by Andrea Ribeiro Silva at Fazenda Aragao and part of the Cafe Delas Program, which sources only from women farmers and reinvests part of sales in gender equality programmes. The region was Brazil's first to receive Denomination of Origin status, in 2013.

beans.name: Nicaragua Finca Argentina
beans.desc: A Nicaraguan from the Dipilto area of Nueva Segovia, near the Honduran border, on steep, cloud-covered, wooded hills in one of the country's highest growing regions.

beans.name: Colombia Supremo La Manuela
beans.producer: La Manuela Estate, near Aranzazu, Caldas (manager Fernando Gomez Chica)
beans.desc: A washed Colombian Supremo from La Manuela Estate near Aranzazu in Caldas, grown on the slopes of the central mountain range under thorny bamboo and banana trees. Sweet caramel, crisp apple and bergamot, medium body and low acidity.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea Jeffrey Usaka
beans.processFull: Fully washed (72-hour wet ferment, sun-dried 5-7 days)
beans.desc: A single-estate washed coffee from the Obura district of Papua New Guinea's Eastern Highlands, hand-picked using Brix readings, floated, wet-fermented 72 hours and sun-dried 5 to 7 days. Rich and full with low acidity: gingerbread, toffee, apple and dried fruits.

beans.name: Tanzania Mondul Estate Honey Process
beans.processFull: Washed (page conflicts with "Honey Process" in the name)
beans.desc: From Mondul Estate, founded in 1931 in Arusha and owned by Burka Estates, which pays staff 20% above the government minimum and protects Burka Forest, whose spring supplies the wet mill. Full-bodied with caramel, lemon, apple and cherry.

beans.name: Kenya Kanjathi
beans.producer: Kanjathi wetmill, Kangiri Farmers' Cooperative, Murang'a
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from the Kanjathi wetmill, founded in 1971 and run with the Kangiri Farmers' Cooperative Society, serving over 1,000 smallholders in Murang'a. Full-bodied with dark caramel, blackcurrant, grape and lemon.

beans.name: Colombia Mountain Water Decaffeinated
beans.desc: An ethically produced Colombian decaf using the Mountain Water process, which removes caffeine with water at varying temperature and pressure and uses no chemicals. Full, lingering, smooth body.

beans.name: Flaming Bean Espresso Blend
beans.origin: Two South American coffees and one Indonesian coffee
beans.desc: An easy-drinking, well-balanced medium roast blend of two South American coffees and one Indonesian coffee, suitable for any time of day. Brown sugar, caramel and cinnamon.

beans.name: Brazil Santos
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, nutty, sweet, caramel, clean finish
beans.desc: A standard specialty-quality Brazilian, hand-harvested and dry-processed for a slight fruitiness and a heavy, sweet, complex brew. Chocolate, nutty, sweet and caramel with a clean finish.

beans.name: Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.listedNotes: Savoury, citrus, milk chocolate, tea-like, floral, lemony
beans.desc: Wild-arabica Ethiopian coffee from Sidamo, typically grown without agricultural chemicals and under shade. Bright acidity, smooth soft body and a clean finish: savoury, citrus, milk chocolate, tea-like, floral and lemony.

beans.name: Indian Monsoon Malabar
beans.desc: A dark-roast monsooned Indian arabica, exposed to moisture-laden Southwest Monsoon winds on the West Coast for about 12 to 16 weeks, echoing the sea-voyage ageing of old. Spicy, earthy, smoky, with tobacco and wood notes.

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.producer: East end of Java, old colonial estates
beans.desc: Also called Old Brown or Old Government Java, from old colonial estates at the east end of Java, once used as ballast on sailing ships to Europe. A monsooned process of 2 to 6 years gives mild acidity, heavy body and sweetness.

beans.name: Costa Rica San Rafael Tarrazu
beans.listedNotes: Not listed; clean, aromatic, naturally sweet, bright acidity
beans.desc: A coffee from Tarrazu, the "Area of the Saints" in Costa Rica's central mountains, grown on volcanic soil and hand-picked with traditional processing. Clean, aromatic and naturally sweet with bright acidity and complex flavours.

beans.name: Vietnam Son La
beans.producer: Son La, northwest Vietnam; small family farms (H'Mong and Thai communities)
beans.listedNotes: Sweetness, nuts, caramel, cocoa, clean finish
beans.desc: A washed arabica from the volcanic, misty highlands of Son La, grown by H'Mong and Thai communities using shade and fruit-tree intercropping. Smooth to medium body and balanced acidity: sweetness, nuts, caramel and cocoa with a clean finish.

beans.name: Mach One Espresso
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A blend of speciality single-origin arabicas roasted dark and long for a balanced, full-bodied espresso extraction, suited to bean-to-cup and home espresso machines.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred; page does not label prices by size)

beans.name: Colombia El Eden
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A collective blend from 18 producers in Colombia's Quindio region, tuned in a cupping lab for consistency across lots. Clean structure, balanced sweetness and vibrant clarity: hazelnut, caramel, chocolate and peach.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred; page does not label prices by size)

beans.name: Brazil Vinte
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A classic natural Brazilian arabica, roasted gently just past the mid point for a smooth, full-bodied filter coffee. Chocolate, berries and marzipan.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred; page does not label prices by size)

beans.name: Kenyan Zawadi Peaberry
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A rich coffee made from Kenyan peaberries, the small single beans. Suited to a mid-afternoon break or a smooth start to the day. Chocolate and sweet raisin.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred headline price; page does not label prices by option)

beans.name: Wings
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A special medium-roast blend supporting Wings for Warriors, a UK charity that trains wounded, injured or sick servicemen and women to become professional pilots. Roasted with cafetiere and filter in mind to bring out chocolate and fruit.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred; page does not label prices by size)

beans.name: Dreamliner Decaf (Ethiopian Sidamo 4 Decaf)
beans.processFull: Water-based decaf with in-house Green Coffee Extract
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A decaf made with a water-based process and an in-house Green Coffee Extract that keeps flavour compounds intact. Gently roasted light to medium to bring out subtle Ethiopian flavours with a hint of acidity: chocolate and lime.

beans.name: Tanzania Mbili Twiga
beans.source: Ground Effect Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A smooth, versatile Tanzanian from the Arusha and Kilimanjaro regions that suits various brewing methods. Blackberry, chamomile, citrus and toffee.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (inferred; page does not label prices by size)

beans.name: Brazil Sitio Gourita
beans.producer: Sitio Gourita, Minas Gerais (Edison Ferreira Carson)
beans.brew: Cafetiere, Clever Dripper, pour over, filter, Aeropress, stove top, espresso (grind options)
beans.desc: A natural Topazio from Sitio Gourita in Minas Gerais at 1,100 m, a farm started almost forty years ago with 3,000 trees by Edison Ferreira Carson, who takes a considered approach to both the product and the environment. Nutty, raisins, cacao and toffee.

beans.name: Brazil Vinte Natural
beans.producer: Nova Resende, Minas Gerais; 20 smallholders (SMC Especialissimo programme)
beans.desc: A soft, balanced, approachable natural from 20 smallholder farmers in Nova Resende, Minas Gerais, supported by SMC's Especialissimo programme. Dark chocolate, hazelnut and lime.

beans.name: Burundi Kinama Natural
beans.listedNotes: Blackcurrant jam, brown sugar, honey, fruit cake
beans.desc: A natural Red Bourbon from the high-altitude Migoti washing station in Bujumbura Rurale, grown by thousands of smallholders, with bright, syrupy sweetness. Blackcurrant jam, brown sugar, honey and fruit cake.

beans.name: Colombia Gilberto Chilo Washed
beans.producer: San Lorenzo, Caldono; Gilberto Chilo (Nasa community)
beans.listedNotes: Honeycomb toffee, sugared almonds, nectarine, ginger cake
beans.desc: A clean, expressive washed micro-lot from Gilberto Chilo in the Nasa community of San Lorenzo, Caldono, solar-dried after careful fermentation. Honeycomb toffee, sugared almonds, nectarine and ginger cake.

beans.name: Colombia Quebraditas Yeast Co-Ferment
beans.producer: Huila; Edinson Argote and Luz Angela, Quebraditas
beans.processFull: Double anaerobic, yeast inoculated, thermal shock
beans.listedNotes: Peach yoghurt, raspberry iced tea, strawberry, blood orange, grapefruit
beans.desc: A Pink Bourbon crafted by Edinson Argote and Luz Angela in Huila using double anaerobic fermentation, yeast inoculation and thermal shock. Peach yoghurt, raspberry iced tea, strawberry, blood orange and grapefruit.

beans.name: Colombia Viani Washed
beans.desc: A washed Colombian from Racafe, a family-run business representing over 5,000 producers and 45 producer groups, in Cundinamarca. Caramelised chocolate, orange zest and honeycomb.

beans.name: Colombia XO Natural
beans.desc: A natural Colombian from Cafe Granja La Esperanza in Cauca at 1,450-1,627 m. Red wine, cherry and floral notes.

beans.name: Decaf Blend Swiss Water
beans.desc: A smooth, chocolatey decaf blend of Colombia, Guatemala, Brazil and Peru, processed with the Swiss Water method to keep flavour without caffeine. Cocoa, nutty and mild acidity.

beans.name: Ethiopia Hambela Natural
beans.desc: A clean, sweet, complex natural heirloom lot from METAD's Guji estate in Oromia, with a vibrant cup. Blueberry, citrus, amaretti and strawberry mousse.

beans.name: Ethiopia Hambela Washed
beans.desc: A vibrant, floral washed lot from the Hambela farm in Guji, crisp and juicy, with a historic legacy. Raspberry, nectarine, dates and honey.

beans.name: Guatemala Fedecocagua Washed
beans.desc: A washed lot from more than 20,000 smallholders in the Fedecocagua Cooperative: a smooth, nutty cup with sweet acidity and milk chocolate, a classic Guatemalan profile.

beans.name: India Monsoon Malabar
beans.desc: A bold, low-acid monsooned coffee from Karnataka with a mellow, strong, earthy character. Chocolate and spice.

beans.name: Landmark Blend
beans.desc: A signature espresso blend of Colombia, Guatemala, Brazil and Peru, roasted for clarity, sweetness and depth, with a rich chocolate body and smooth mouthfeel, black or with milk.

beans.name: Peru Sol y Cafe Washed
beans.producer: San Ignacio, Cajamarca; Sol y Cafe Cooperative (organic)
beans.desc: Grown organically in Cajamarca by the Sol y Cafe Cooperative of over 1,000 farming families: smooth and caramel-sweet with citrus acidity and a creamy, nutty body.

beans.name: Rwanda Humeka Anaerobic
beans.producer: Kibuye, Western Province; Rwamatamu (near Lake Kivu)
beans.desc: An anaerobic Red Bourbon from a family business near Lake Kivu focused on youth empowerment and community impact, bursting with raspberry, nectarine and jelly sweets with lively acidity.

beans.name: Uganda Rwenzori Natural
beans.desc: A sweet, rich, fruity natural from smallholders in the Rwenzori Mountains, processed by Agri Evolve, a B Corp with community at its core. Black cherry, honey, cocoa and apricot.

beans.name: Original Blend
beans.desc: Lytham Coffee Co's best seller and the blend that built the business, giving a noticeable hit of flavour with every mouthful when drunk with milk. Strength 3 on the shop's scale, sometimes creeping into 4.

beans.name: Triple Certificate
beans.desc: A blend of 100% organic, 100% Fairtrade and 35% Rainforest Alliance coffees, with smoky, spicy and nutty notes and a smooth finish.

beans.name: Original Blend Coffee Bags x20
beans.listedNotes: Hit of flavour through milk; strength 3, sometimes 4
beans.desc: The best-selling Original Blend in tea-bag style coffee bags, 20 to a resealable packet, each making one large cup. Add not-quite-boiling water, leave about 3 minutes, then remove the bag.

beans.name: Decaf Swiss Water Blend
beans.desc: A dark-roast decaf blend using the non-chemical Swiss Water process, ground for filters and cafetieres. Hints of caramel and sugar browning.

beans.name: Brazilian Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Bahia, Cerrado Mogiana and Sul de Minas (various estates)
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate sweetness (stovetop); hazelnut nuttiness and buttery mouthfeel (espresso)
beans.brew: Espresso, stovetop/hob, cafetiere, filter machine, Aeropress
beans.desc: A sweet, rich, low-acidity dark-roast espresso that has been the shop's stalwart since it opened, loved for depth of body and sweetness. Made from naturals, pulped naturals and washed Brazilian coffees from several estates. Milk chocolate sweetness on the stovetop; hazelnut and a buttery mouthfeel as espresso.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: TCRoasters House Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Pantano and Sao Silvestre (Brazil); Finca El Aguila (El Salvador)
beans.brew: Espresso, hob percolator, cafetiere, filter machine, Aeropress
beans.desc: The seasonal house espresso: two Brazilian coffees (Fazenda Pantano and Sao Silvestre) and a Salvadoran (Finca El Aguila), roasted together at their peak where sweetness and liveliness join. Lighter than their BSCA#1 blend, with a fruity end to the shot.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: La Mariposa EA Decaf
beans.producer: Cauca, Narino, Huila, Tolima; various smallholders
beans.processFull: Washed; EA decaf (method not spelled out on the page)
beans.listedNotes: Heavy body, chocolate, brown sugar, plum, raisin
beans.brew: Any style: espresso, hob percolator, cafetiere, filter machine, Aeropress
beans.desc: A decaffeinated blend of washed Colombian coffees from smallholders in Cauca, Narino, Huila and Tolima, grown under shade at 1,450-2,140 masl and roasted quite dark so it suits any style of preparation. Heavy body with chocolate, brown sugar, plum and raisin.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: Fazenda Castanhas Natural
beans.producer: Fazenda Castanhas, Tres Pontas, Sul de Minas (Cocatrel Cooperative)
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, honey, fig, hints of plum; nutty
beans.brew: Any method: espresso, hob percolator, cafetiere, filter machine, Aeropress; good with milk
beans.desc: A well-rounded, nutty Brazilian pulped natural from Fazenda Castanhas in Tres Pontas, Sul de Minas, sold by the Cocatrel Cooperative. A crowd pleaser for every brewing method and great with milk, with dark chocolate, honey, fig and hints of plum.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: Lalesa Black Honey Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Red berries, jasmine, vanilla, blueberry, peach, sweet dried fruits; floral with a boozy candy tone
beans.brew: Filter, cafetiere, Aeropress (best black; longer extraction for syrupy body)
beans.desc: A very complex black honey natural from Bette Buna in Lalesa, Gedeb, Yirgacheffe (batch 9, cup score 87.25). Red berries, jasmine, vanilla and blueberry with light floral top notes and a candy, boozy tone. Best drunk black on filter, cafetiere or Aeropress.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: San Lorenzo Colombia
beans.listedNotes: Jam doughnut, gooseberry, caramel, chocolate, panela, apricot, apple acidity; creamy body, juicy
beans.brew: Any method: espresso, hob percolator, cafetiere, filter machine, Aeropress
beans.desc: A fully washed Colombian from 64 smallholders in Cauca at 1,800-2,100 masl: juicy, creamy bodied and beautifully balanced, with jam doughnut, gooseberry, caramel, chocolate, panela, apricot and green apple.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: El Borbollon
beans.producer: La Reforma and El Cerro farms, Santa Ana, Ahuachapan (Alvarez family)
notes: Dark chocolate with a touch of fruitiness
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate with a touch of fruitiness; rich, clean mouthfeel, long aftertaste
beans.desc: A versatile washed Red Bourbon from the Alvarez family farms La Reforma and El Cerro in Santa Ana, Ahuachapan, roasted dark for rich dark chocolate with just a touch of fruitiness. Long aftertaste and a rich, clean mouthfeel, for those who prefer chocolate to fruity.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: Musasa Nkara Anaerobic Natural
beans.producer: Musasa washing station, Gakenke district, Northern Province (Dukunde Kawa Cooperative, 226 producers)
beans.processFull: Anaerobic natural (raised African beds, dried to 11% humidity)
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, dried fruit (blueberry, raisin, black cherry, plum); berry, stone fruit; velvety body, long finish
beans.brew: Any method: cafetiere, filter machine, espresso, hob percolator, Aeropress
beans.desc: A well-balanced anaerobic natural Red Bourbon from the Musasa washing station in Gakenke, Northern Province, from Dukunde Kawa Cooperative (226 producers, about 0.25 ha each). Velvety body and a long finish with chocolate and dried fruit: blueberry, raisin, black cherry and plum.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: Uten Kupi
beans.producer: Gajo, Aceh, Sumatra; cooperative of 20 farmers
beans.listedNotes: Pineapple, papaya, dark chocolate, rum cream, fig, fudge; nutmeg, black tea; peach and strawberry twist as it cools
beans.brew: Any method: cafetiere, filter machine, espresso, hob percolator, Aeropress
beans.desc: An elegant Sumatran from a cooperative of 20 farmers in Gajo, Aceh, grown on rich volcanic loam at 1,400-1,600 masl and processed wet hulled. Big body, with dark chocolate, nutmeg and black tea, plus pineapple, papaya, fig, fudge and rum cream and a peach and strawberry twist. Cup score 84.25.
beans.priceBasis: Per 100g (as listed by roaster; bag sizes not stated)

beans.name: Brazil Caveman House Espresso
beans.brew: Espresso; also flat whites, lattes or black
beans.desc: A smooth, versatile, specialty-grade Brazilian espresso, sustainably sourced and produced entirely by women farmers, freshly roasted in London. Notes of chocolate, hazelnut and dried fruits. Suited to flat whites, lattes or drinking black. Part of the proceeds support female producers through education and financial independence.

beans.name: Colombia Dulima Filter
beans.listedNotes: Sweet milk chocolate, clean and fresh apple acidity
beans.desc: Award-winning Colombian coffee from the high altitudes of the Tolima and Huila growing regions, carefully sourced for its distinctive flavour. Sweet milk chocolate with a clean and fresh apple acidity.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia Sugarcane
beans.processFull: Sugarcane ethyl acetate (E.A.) decaffeination, done at source in Colombia
beans.desc: A decaf that keeps caffeine out using what the roaster calls the most natural decaffeination method: sugarcane ethyl acetate made from fermented molasses, with growing, processing and decaffeination all carried out at source in Colombia. Freshly roasted in London. Melon, cocoa and citrus notes.

beans.name: Brazil Fairtrade
beans.producer: Sul de Minas; six women farmers of the Coopfam co-operative (Sitios Serra Negra, Lavrinha, Grota Grande, Cardoso, Gonçalves, Posses)
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, chocolate, nuts; smooth, creamy finish
beans.desc: A special Fairtrade certified natural lot from six women farmers in the Sul de Minas region of Brazil, all members of the Coopfam co-operative. Notes of caramel, chocolate and nuts with a smooth and creamy finish.

beans.name: Kenya Kamwangi
beans.desc: Kamwangi has consistently produced some of the roaster's favourite Kenyan coffees over several seasons. Hand-roasted and freshly roasted in London. Black cherry, lemon and toffee notes.

beans.name: Uganda Sipi Tangwen
beans.producer: Sipi Falls Project co-op, Sipi, Kapchorwa District, near Mount Elgon
beans.desc: Organic, AA grade coffee (the highest quality standard in Uganda) from the Sipi Falls Project co-op in Sipi, Kapchorwa District, grown and milled on volcanic loam in the foothills of Mount Elgon. Double handpicked. Black grape, lemon, caramel and almond notes.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Worka Wuri
beans.producer: Worka Wuri washing station, Gedeb, Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Peach, cherry, apple, lime, fruit salad candy
beans.desc: Single origin, naturally processed Grade 1 coffee from the Worka Wuri washing station in Gedeb, Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia. Freshly roasted. Vibrant notes of peach, cherry, apple, lime and fruit salad candy.

beans.name: Rwanda Dujundekawa Nkara Natural
beans.desc: A naturally processed single origin from the Nkara washing station in Gakenke District, Rwanda, grown at high altitude from Bourbon trees and freshly roasted in London. Cherry, strawberry, floral aroma and caramel, with sweetness and fruit character.

beans.name: Sweet Breeze
beans.desc: A spring/summer house blend with a sweeter, fruitier profile, combining washed Ethiopia Sidamo (mixed heirloom, 1,200-1,800 masl) and Guatemala Huehuetenango (Typica, Bourbon, Catura, Catuai, 1,350 masl). Medium roast with notes of milk chocolate and citrus. Suited to espresso and filter.

beans.name: Winter Nights
beans.producer: Brazil Ipanema Estate; Colombia Excelso (various farms)
beans.desc: A medium-roast best seller and Great Taste award winner blending Brazil (Ipanema Estate) and Colombia (Excelso, various farms). Brown sugar, caramel and dark chocolate. Suited to espresso and filter.

beans.name: Autumn Fire
beans.desc: A bold, full-bodied medium-roast blend of washed Guatemala Huehuetenango and monsooned India Manjarabad. Nutmeg, cinnamon and smoky tobacco. Suited to espresso, moka pot and French press.

beans.name: Storm
beans.desc: The roaster's dark roast: monsooned India Manjarabad (Monsoon Malabar) with dark chocolate and brown spice notes, "the perfect strong coffee". Suited to espresso and filter.

beans.name: Single Origin (Kenya Oreti Estate)
beans.producer: Oreti Estate (Harries family, farming since the 1950s)
beans.desc: A light, juicy, refreshing single origin from Oreti Estate in Kenya, farmed by the Harries family since the 1950s. Fully washed SL28 and SL34 grown at 1,560-1,650 masl. Blackberry, black tea and lime. Suited to V60, batch brew and espresso. The offering rotates.

beans.name: Limited Edition (Costa Rica Tarrazu)
beans.desc: A seasonal Christmas limited edition single origin from Tarrazu, Costa Rica, processed by anaerobic fermentation. A vibrant, juicy cup with plum, apple, cinnamon bun and orange notes. Best brewed as V60.

beans.name: Abner & Vanessa - Natural Brazilian Catucaí
beans.producer: Caldas, Minas Gerais; Abner and Vanessa Carvalho, Sítio Baixão da Serra
beans.processFull: Natural (sun dried, turned during the day, covered overnight)
beans.listedNotes: Hobnob biscuit, pear, creamy macadamia, baker's chocolate
beans.brew: Espresso (with milk or black); filter (black or white)
beans.desc: A sweet, comforting and versatile natural Brazilian from husband-and-wife producers Abner and Vanessa Carvalho at Sítio Baixão da Serra, Caldas, Minas Gerais. Catucaí beans, small-batch convection roasted, with a biscuity, chocolatey profile that suits milk drinks and filter. Hobnob biscuit, pear, creamy macadamia and baker's chocolate. Q Score 85.50.

beans.name: Primavera Family - Washed Guatemalan Caturra
beans.producer: San Antonio Huista, Huehuetenango; about 15 smallholders via Primavera Green Coffee
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, brownie bites, Hobnob biscuit, cocoa
beans.desc: Harmony's new "Easy Drinker": a sweet, smooth, forgiving washed Caturra from about 15 smallholders in San Antonio Huista, Huehuetenango, suited to milk drinks and filter. Strawberry, brownie bites, Hobnob biscuit and cocoa.

beans.name: El Vergel Decaf (Colombian Sugarcane Decaf)
beans.producer: El Vergel farm, Tolima; Shady & Elias Bayter
beans.processFull: Sugarcane E.A. decaffeination (listed as natural; an image caption says washed)
beans.listedNotes: Candied lime, mango, red berries, brown spice
beans.desc: A sugarcane E.A. decaf from El Vergel farm in Tolima, Colombia, called "quite possibly the best decaf we've ever found" by the roaster. Under 0.1% caffeine. Candied lime, mango, red berries and brown spice.

beans.name: Malawo - Washed Ethiopian 74158
beans.producer: Malawo village, Arbegona, Sidama; Malawo Smallholders with Daye Bensa
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, lemonade, candied lemon, lemongrass, white peach
beans.desc: A washed Ethiopian from smallholders around Malawo village, Arbegona, Sidama, working with exporter Daye Bensa. Bright citrus acidity, silky body and floral aromatics: jasmine, lemonade, candied lemon, lemongrass and white peach.

beans.name: Musaza Lot 1 - Washed Rwandan Red Bourbon
beans.producer: Lake Kivu, Nyamasheke, Western Province; Rwamatamu estate (Laetitia & Gaston), Mbare washing station
beans.desc: A clean, incredibly delicate washed Red Bourbon from the family-run Rwamatamu estate on Lake Kivu, Nyamasheke, hand-picked, washed with spring water and sun-dried. Tangerine, orange blossom and lemon tea.

beans.name: Bookkisa - Natural Ethiopian 74110 / 74112
beans.producer: Shakiso, Guji; Ture Waji, Sookoo Coffee
beans.desc: A natural Ethiopian from Ture Waji of Sookoo Coffee in Shakiso, Guji. Super juicy tropical fruit with a clean, floral, crisp profile: pineapple, blueberry juice and white peach.

beans.name: Niguse Jilo - Natural Ethiopian Kurume
beans.producer: Halo Bariti, Gedeb, Yirgacheffe; Niguse Jilo, Bore Nageso farmer group
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry compote, honey, Earl Grey, white peach
beans.desc: A natural Kurume from Niguse Jilo, lead farmer of the Bore Nageso group in Halo Bariti, Gedeb, Yirgacheffe. Jammy sweetness and a delicate tea-like finish: blueberry compote, honey, Earl Grey and white peach.

beans.name: Bekele Yutute - Anaerobic Natural Ethiopian 74158
beans.producer: Bensa, Sidama; Bekele Yutute, Murago farm
beans.listedNotes: Orange Starburst, peach yoghurt, blueberry, Earl Grey; chewy syrupy body
beans.desc: A wild, fruit-forward anaerobic natural from Bekele Yutute's Murago farm in Bensa, Sidama, one of the roaster's customers' favourites last year. Orange Starburst sweets, peach yoghurt, blueberry and Earl Grey with a chewy, syrupy body.

beans.name: Red Sparrow - Anaerobic Natural Chinese Yun Catimor
beans.producer: Baoshan, Yunnan; Lao Wang, Red Dragon Estate
beans.listedNotes: Honeydew melon, dragonfruit, mint, black tea
beans.desc: An expressive, fruit-forward anaerobic natural from Red Dragon Estate in Baoshan, Yunnan, a coffee that won the 2021 Chinese Barista Championship for Pan Wei. Honeydew melon, dragonfruit, mint and black tea.

beans.name: El Dorado - Natural Ecuadorian Wush Wush
beans.producer: Loja; Elder family and Bernard Uhe, El Dorado farm
beans.desc: A versatile natural Wush Wush micro-lot from the Elder family's El Dorado farm in Loja, southern Ecuador, established in 2017 on former almond land. Pineapple, banana brûlée, lime and candyfloss.
beans.priceBasis: 150g (confirmed by user; 125g/150g bags accepted as an exception)

beans.name: (You Gotta) Fight For Your Right (To Latte) - Brazil
beans.producer: Poço Fundo; Osmar Pereira with Cleusa and the local community
beans.listedNotes: Black cherry, milk chocolate, praline (page also mentions toffee, caramel, black forest gateau)
beans.brew: Espresso, cortado; AeroPress, cafetière, moka pot; filter for fruitier notes
beans.desc: A pulped natural lot from Osmar Pereira, who has grown coffee for decades in the hills of Poço Fundo, Brazil, with his wife Cleusa and their community. Red and Yellow Catuai grown at 1,100 m, pulped and dried on small patios and turned often. Grown-up chocolate, praline and black cherry. Especially popular as espresso, and also good in AeroPress, cafetière, moka pot or filter.

beans.name: Born Sippin'
beans.producer: Smallholders in Guji and Sidamo (Awash River), delivering cherries to local wet mills
beans.listedNotes: Blossom honey, blueberry jam, milk chocolate; blueberry, strawberry, raspberry
beans.desc: A fruit-forward Ethiopian natural from smallholders in Guji and Sidamo, with masses of blueberry, strawberry and raspberry up front, finishing with creamy milk chocolate and blossom honey sweetness. Bright acidity. Heirloom and Typica at 1,950-2,150 m. Great in a flat white, pour-over or filter.

beans.name: Dancing In The Bloomlight (Colombia Ombligón)
beans.producer: El Diviso estate, Huila; brothers Néstor and Adrián Lasso
beans.processFull: Washed (exclusive protocol: controlled oxidation, anaerobic fermentation, thermal shock wash)
beans.listedNotes: Guava, pineapple, strawberry laces; bright citrus and red-fruit acidity
beans.desc: An exclusive Ombligón release from Néstor Lasso, an ultra-small-batch micro-lot from the El Diviso estate in Huila, Colombia. "An absolute flavour bomb": medium-bodied with tart pineapple, sweet guava and strawberry laces, from a washed process with controlled oxidation, anaerobic fermentation and a thermal shock wash.

beans.name: Espresso Yourself
beans.producer: Posses, Brazil; San Cristóbal de las Casas, Mexico
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, dark chocolate, toffee, fruit, bittersweet cocoa
beans.desc: The roaster's house espresso blend of Brazil (Posses) and Mexico (San Cristóbal de las Casas): rich, chocolatey body with toffee sweetness, fruity notes and a hint of bittersweet cocoa. Award-winning and designed for espresso but works in other methods, milk drinks and cold brew.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £13.00-£31.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Every Brew Every Me
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe (Gedeb); 650 smallholders, Worka Wuri wet mills
beans.listedNotes: Peach iced tea, juicy raspberry, mango
beans.brew: V60 (black); espresso with milk; AeroPress, cafetière, moka pot
beans.desc: A washed Ethiopian from a group of 650 smallholders around Worka Wuri wet mills in Gedeb, Yirgacheffe, with incredible tea-like clarity and a sweet floral aroma. Peach iced tea, juicy raspberry and a hint of mango. Best black on a manual brewer, or with milk as espresso.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £14.00-£39.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Half Caf The World Away
beans.producer: Cauca, Colombia (decaf part); Finca El Carrizal, Fraijanes, Guatemala (Carlos Durán Matias)
beans.processFull: Sugarcane E.A. decaf (Colombia); fully washed, patio dried (Guatemala)
beans.listedNotes: Blood orange, fruit cake, milk chocolate; raisin, cranberry
beans.desc: A low-caffeine blend with half the caffeine and all the flavour: 50% sugarcane E.A. decaf from Cauca, Colombia and 50% washed coffee from Finca El Carrizal, Guatemala. Blood orange, fruit cake and milk chocolate. Suits all brew methods.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £11.50-£29.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: (I Can't Get No) Caffeination
beans.producer: Caldono, Cauca; farmers around Piendamo, Cajibio and Popayán
beans.listedNotes: Cherry, chocolate, treacle (black cherry, black forest gateau, toffee in the meta text)
beans.brew: All methods: filter, cafetière, V60, Chemex, espresso, AeroPress
beans.desc: An award-winning ethyl acetate decaf from the Cauca region of Colombia, so good you'll struggle to know it's a decaf. Coffees from farms around Caldono, Piendamo, Cajibio and Popayán are blended and decaffeinated in Colombia. Cherry, chocolate and treacle.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £12.25-£31.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: I Don't Feel Like Tampin'
beans.processFull: Anaerobic natural (9 days fermentation, 15 days drying)
beans.listedNotes: Cherry cola, port, pomegranate; velvety mouthfeel
beans.brew: V60, espresso, AeroPress, cafetière, moka pot
beans.desc: A wild, fruit-forward anaerobic natural Ethiopian from Ephtah Coffee in Halo Beriti, Yirgacheffe, with a velvety mouthfeel, pomegranate sweetness, port-like richness and lively, playful acidity. Cherry cola and port notes.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £14.50-£39.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Islands In The Steam (Mexico Chiapas)
beans.desc: A Mexican coffee from the Chiapas highlands with caramelised brown sugar, jammy raisins and a milk chocolate body. Suits milk drinks, espresso or black coffee.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £13.50-£34.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Oh Frappé Day (Kenya)
beans.listedNotes: Blackcurrant, lemon sorbet, rhubarb, lemon zest
beans.desc: A fresh-crop Kenyan from the Kamwangi co-operative (about 1,500 smallholders), released for summer: zingy and fruity, made for clean black coffee. Blackcurrant, lemon sorbet, rhubarb and lemon zest, with caramel in cafetière and moka pot brews.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £13.50-£38.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Signed, Sealed, Delivered - It Pours (Guatemala)
beans.processFull: Anaerobic natural (120 hour fermentation, patio and sun dried)
beans.listedNotes: Old school cake, cherry, chocolate raisins; stone fruit, cherry brandy acidity
beans.brew: Espresso, moka pot, filter, V60, cafetière
beans.desc: A fresh twist on a previous Guatemala release: an anaerobic natural from the Santa Rosa highlands (Lake Ayarza) with stone-fruit jamminess, sweet cherry and a silky chocolate body that tastes like school cake with milk. Cherries ferment for 120 hours before patio and sun drying.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £14.50-£42.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: You've Got A Blend In Me
beans.producer: Konga mill, Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia; Posses, Brazil
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry, chocolate praline, tangerine, nutty complexity
beans.desc: A bold, characterful house blend of Ethiopia (Konga mill, Yirgacheffe) and Brazil (Posses): juicy blueberry, bright tangerine acidity and a smooth chocolate praline finish. 3 Star Great Taste Award winner 2026.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £14.00-£39.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Get Ground Tonight (Colombia Ombligón Natural)
beans.processFull: Anaerobic natural (38 hour yeast-inoculated anaerobic fermentation, 48 hour controlled oxidation, 50°C thermal shock, 15 days on parabolic beds)
beans.brew: AeroPress/moka pot, cafetière, Chemex, espresso, filter, V60
beans.desc: An exclusive Ombligón release from award-winning Néstor Lasso of El Diviso, Colombia: a natural Ombligón given a specialised anaerobic fermentation and thermal shock treatment to hyper-intensify its fruit. Rich maraschino cherry, bright apricot and the sweet-tart edge of an amaretto sour. A hyper-limited release.

beans.name: Bohemian Like Brew (Peru)
beans.processFull: Fully washed, extended fermentation (92-hour double fermentation, 18 days on raised beds)
beans.listedNotes: Blood orange, dark chocolate, ruby grapefruit
beans.desc: A seasonal favourite returns. This new Peruvian harvest pairs zesty citrus sweetness, decadent blood orange and bright grapefruit, with a luxurious, chocolatey body. A 92-hour double fermentation and 18 days of drying on raised beds give a depth of flavour, especially when brewed manually. Versatile: a bold espresso or a vibrant pour over.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £13.50-£38.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Smile Like You Bean It (Tanzania)
beans.brew: AeroPress, cafetière, Chemex, espresso, filter, V60 (no method recommended)
beans.desc: Back by popular demand: a vibrant yet comforting washed Tanzanian from the highlands, with buttery rhubarb crumble, orange marmalade sweetness and a jammy cranberry lift. A returning seasonal favourite.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £12.00-£30.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Son of a Peacher Man (Colombia Peach Co-Ferment)
beans.desc: A refreshing peach co-ferment from Colombian innovator Jairo Arcila, a third-generation producer farming since 1987 and known for experimental processing. Sweet peach, floral hibiscus and crisp prosecco notes, with a bright, tropical cup. Scores 88 on the SCA scale. Best as a pour-over, or as an iced Americano.

beans.name: What Christmas Beans To Me
beans.processFull: Pulped natural and natural; cinnamon infused
beans.desc: A speciality Christmas house blend inspired by the Christmases we all remember: rich stollen, warming cinnamon and sweet gingerbread, in a comforting, indulgent and nostalgic cup. Pulped natural and natural coffees, cinnamon infused.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £14.50-£38.00 range, 250g and 1kg sizes; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Alto San Juan (Costa Rica)
beans.producer: Alto San Juan Coop, Alto San Juan, Tarrazu
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, milk chocolate, slightly floral finish; rich, buttery mouthfeel
beans.desc: Wonderfully moreish, quaffable coffee from small growers at the Alto San Juan co-op in Tarrazu. A select small lot, hand-picked at peak ripeness; washed (pulped, fermented, washed, patio-dried), rested for at least 60 days, then hand sorted and graded before export. Rich and buttery mouthfeel, caramel, milk chocolate, super sweet with a slightly floral finish.

beans.name: Finca El Porthron (El Salvador)
beans.producer: Finca El Porthron, Urrutias family, Atiquizaya, El Balsamo Mountain Range
beans.listedNotes: Milk and dark chocolate, sweet floral; super clean mouthfeel
beans.source: Coffee Real product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An exclusive to Coffee Real from the Urrutias family estate. Finca El Porthron is a 200 acre farm with 130 acres of coffee and the rest forest and habitat. Washed Bourbon grown at 1,110 masl. Milk and dark chocolate with a sweet floral balance and a super clean mouthfeel.

beans.name: Pacific Rescue - San Pancho Turtle
beans.listedNotes: Tangerine, baking chocolate, raw cane sugar sweetness, fine citrus acidity, long finish
beans.source: Coffee Real product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A conservation coffee: all profit goes to the San Pancho Turtle Fund, a small volunteer-run project protecting Olive Ridley sea turtles in San Pancho, Mexico. Very well balanced cup, with fine citrus acidity balanced by raw cane sugar sweetness, tangerine and baking chocolate notes and a long finish.

beans.name: San Martin - Honey Process (Costa Rica)
beans.producer: San Martin Coop (Coopetarrazu community lot), San Martin, Tarrazu
beans.listedNotes: Mango, orange marmalade, cascara; creamy body, long honey finish
beans.desc: A community lot from smallholder farmers of San Martin, one of the highest hamlets of the Tarrazu region, all members of the Coopetarrazu cooperative. Part of the cooperative's traceability programme that separates lots by community, with a premium paid back to the community. Honey processed. Mango, orange marmalade and cascara, with a creamy body and a long honey finish.

beans.name: Bwenda Washing Station (Rwanda)
beans.producer: Bwenda Smallholders, Bwenda Washing Station (owner Bernard Uwitije), Nyamagabe
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine florals, bergamot, apple, milk chocolate; juicy round acidity, velvety body
beans.desc: From the Bwenda washing station in Nyamagabe, southern Rwanda, owned by Bernard Uwitije, who built it in 2018 for a group of isolated smallholders and is developing extension programmes for them. Washed Bourbon at 1,500-1,700 masl. Jasmine florals, bergamot, apple and milk chocolate, with a juicy, round acidity and velvety body.

beans.name: Latin Connection (espresso blend)
beans.producer: Brazil Fazenda Rio Verde (20%, washed), Brazil Sitio Sao Jose (30%, natural), El Salvador Finca El Ingenio de los Ausoles (50%, washed micro lot)
beans.listedNotes: Big creamy sweetness, fruity acidity, deep chocolate, macadamia nuts
beans.desc: An espresso blend of three select coffees: a washed micro lot from Finca El Ingenio de los Ausoles in El Salvador (50%), a washed Brazil from Fazenda Rio Verde (20%) and a natural from Sitio Sao Jose (30%) to balance the washed acidity. Big creamy sweetness, fruity acidity and deep chocolate with macadamia nuts.

beans.name: Masangula Extended Fermentation (Tanzania)
beans.producer: Masangula Smallholder Farmers, Masangula Washing Station, Mbozi District, Mbeya Region
beans.listedNotes: Stone fruit, apricot, peach/nectarine, fresh tobacco leaf; ripe sweet stone fruit throughout
beans.desc: A small micro lot from smallholder farmers around the Masangula washing station in Mbozi District, Mbeya Region, grown at cooler temperatures with gentler soil pH. Only prime red cherry is pulped, then given a 36 hour ferment, washed and dried. Stone fruit, apricot, peach/nectarine and fresh tobacco leaf, with ripe sweet stone fruit all the way through.

beans.name: Masangula Natural Process (Tanzania)
beans.producer: Masangula Smallholder Farmers, Masangula Washing Station, Mbozi District, Mbeya Region
beans.listedNotes: Blood orange, plum, blueberry, pineapple, vanilla
beans.desc: A tiny 30kg micro lot from smallholder farmers around the Masangula washing station in Mbozi District, Mbeya Region, grown in cooler temperatures. Natural processed: cherry left two hours on raised beds, turned every 30 minutes for the first 5-7 days, then dried over 9-12 days. Blood orange and plum with blueberry, pineapple and vanilla notes.

beans.name: Mexico Tierra Libertad
beans.producer: Coop Tierra Libertad, Angel Diaz, Siltepec, Chiapas
beans.listedNotes: Fine lemongrass acidity, brown sugar sweetness, tangerine finish
beans.desc: From a group of small producers called Tierra Libertad in Angel Diaz, Siltepec, Chiapas, farming at up to 1,900 masl. Selectively picked and pre-sorted, then wet processed on the day of harvest, fermented overnight, washed and sun-dried on patios. A fine lemongrass acidity balanced by brown sugar sweetness, with tangerine notes in the finish.

beans.name: San Ignacio Mountain Water Decaf (Peru)
beans.producer: Association of small growers, San Ignacio, Cajamarca
beans.listedNotes: Tomato vine, lemon, rich butter, refined citrus acidity
beans.desc: Decaf from the San Ignacio District, Cajamarca, grown shade-covered at 1,250-1,480 masl by an association of small growers on plots averaging 3 hectares. Washed and sun dried, then decaffeinated by the Mountain Water Process in Veracruz, Mexico (99.9% caffeine free, organic and Kosher certified). Tomato vine, lemon and rich butter with a refined citrus acidity.

beans.name: Genaro Machaco (Honduras)
beans.producer: Genaro Machado, Finca El Corazon, San Andres, Lempira
beans.processFull: Washed, 120 hour extended fermentation, raised beds
beans.listedNotes: Plum, apple, creamy milk chocolate, hazelnut finish
beans.desc: From second generation farmer Genaro Machado at El Corazon in San Andres, Lempira, a trained agronomist who bought new land above 1,600 masl four years ago. Washed with a 120 hour extended fermentation, then dried on raised beds. Plum and apple with creamy milk chocolate and a hazelnut finish.

beans.name: Sitio Sao Jose (Brazil)
beans.producer: Luiz Roberto, Sitio Sao Jose, Carmo de Minas, Minas Gerais
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, sweet-meal biscuit, dark dried fruit acidity; full body, thick mouthfeel
beans.desc: Owned and managed by Luiz Roberto in Carmo de Minas, on the rim of the Mantiqueira Mountain Range in southern Minas Gerais. Selectively hand picked onto cloth, then dried on terraces and rested at least 30 days. Dark chocolate and sweet-meal biscuit with a dark dried fruit acidity, a full-bodied cup and thick mouthfeel.

beans.name: Finca Santa Maria (Nicaragua)
beans.producer: Victor Robelo, Finca Santa Maria, Matagalpa/Jinotega (page also places the farm in Dipilto, Nueva Segovia)
beans.listedNotes: Stone fruit, baker's milk chocolate, orange acidity, creamy mouthfeel
beans.desc: A micro lot from Victor Robelo's Finca Santa Maria, a 50 hectare sustainably managed farm grown under Inga and banana shade at around 1,400 metres, with the coffee dry milled at Beneficio Las Nubes. Washed Bourbon. Stone fruit and baker's milk chocolate with a creamy mouthfeel and orange acidity.

beans.name: Santa Isabel (Guatemala)
beans.producer: Finca Santa Isabel (Don Luis), San Cristobal Verapaz, Coban
beans.listedNotes: Ripe orange, almond, sweet cocoa; delicately bright, silky mouthfeel
beans.desc: From Finca Santa Isabel, a 300 acre farm near San Cristobal Verapaz in Coban, run by the Valdes family (Don Luis and his son Wicho), who have twice placed in Guatemala's Cup of Excellence. Washed, fermented up to 48 hours, and slowly dried. Ripe orange and almond with sweet cocoa, delicately bright with a silky mouthfeel.

beans.name: Inga Mystique Narino (Colombia)
beans.producer: Sandona Group (about 17 growers), Montebello, Sandona, Narino
beans.listedNotes: Swiss chocolate, vanilla, orange creamsicle; piquant acidity, creamy body
beans.desc: The Inga Mystique lot is produced by Sandona Group, a small producers' association of about 17 growers in Sandona, Narino, working with exporter Inconexus. Grown at 1,900-2,000 masl under Inga shade trees and wet-milled at Belcosub. Swiss chocolate, vanilla and orange creamsicle with a piquant acidity and creamy body.

beans.name: Isabella de Triunfo Decaf MW (Mexico)
beans.producer: Alberto Preez, Finca Isabella de Triunfo, Tuxtla Gutierrez, Chiapas
beans.listedNotes: Candied sweetness, bakers chocolate, red berries, a little orange; bright acidity, smooth long finish
beans.desc: Mountain Water decaf from Alberto Preez's 7.3 hectare Finca Isabella de Triunfo, next to the El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve in the Sierra Madre de Chiapas. Selectively picked, wet processed on the day of harvest, fermented overnight, washed and sun dried on patios. Candied sweetness and bright acidity with baker's chocolate, red berries and a little orange.

beans.name: Six am (espresso blend)
beans.producer: Ethiopia Djimmah Wild Grown (28%), Guatemala Finca El Bosque (32%), India Sethuraman Pulped Natural (40%)
beans.listedNotes: Creamy and smooth, a little bright acidity, good depth, body and crema; takes milk well
beans.desc: An espresso blend of Ethiopia Djimmah Wild Grown for brightness and personality, Guatemala Finca El Bosque for sweet fruit, and India Sethuraman Pulped Natural for richness and body. Never pre-mixed before roasting, so each component reaches its ideal roast. Creamy and smooth with depth, body and crema, and it takes milk well.

beans.name: Genesis Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Bought direct from farmers; no producer named for the blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, cherry, caramel, toasted nut
beans.desc: A versatile all-rounder for espresso-based drinks such as lattes, cappuccinos and straight shots, abundant in chocolate richness, nutty undertones and a delicate earthy essence. Rwandan lots add fruity complexity and Brazilian beans add body and creaminess. Dark chocolate, cherry, caramel and toasted nut.

beans.name: Brazil Eagle Carmelo
beans.producer: Jaqueline Borges and Jordana Tacila Almeida Conti, Monte Carmelo, Cerrado Mineiro (Cafe Delas programme)
beans.desc: Creation Coffee's take on a classic Cerrado Mineiro profile, aiming for consistency from lot to lot and year to year. Part of its Cafe Delas programme, which sources from women farmers and reinvests a portion of profit in gender equality initiatives. Chocolate, hazelnut and dried fruits.

beans.name: Colombia El Buho Sugarcane Decaf
beans.producer: Finca El Paraiso Villa Esperanza (Yenny Esperanza Bermudez and family), Tambo, Cauca
beans.processFull: Anaerobic (two 48-hour anaerobic ferments); sugarcane ethyl acetate decaf
beans.listedNotes: Malt loaf, golden syrup, vanilla, grape
beans.desc: A decaffeinated Castillo. Mature cherries are washed with ozonated water and given two 48-hour anaerobic fermentations, one before and one after pulping. Caffeine is removed with natural ethyl acetate from sugarcane and high mountain spring water, with no synthetic additives. Malt loaf, golden syrup, vanilla and grape.

beans.name: Colombia Planadas
beans.producer: 1,325 small organic farmers in 25 groups, Planadas, South Tolima
beans.processFull: Fully washed; dried in parabolic greenhouse 10-18 days
beans.desc: A washed lot from 1,325 small organic growers in 25 farmer groups in Planadas, South Tolima, on farms up to 2,050 masl in the Andean foothills with volcanic soils. Cherries are selected, depulped, fermented, washed and dried in parabolic greenhouses. Apple, blackberry, caramel and milk chocolate.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: lowest of three unlabelled prices, £11/£19/£32, for 250g/500g/1kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Guatemala Jabiru Union Cantinil
beans.producer: Smallholder farmers around Union Cantinil, Huehuetenango (SHB EP)
beans.listedNotes: Butterscotch, green apple, dark chocolate, cranberry
beans.desc: A single-origin washed SHB EP from small producers in Union Cantinil, Huehuetenango, on farms averaging 1.5 hectares at high altitude. Creation Coffee runs a micro-warehouse and buying station there, collecting from within about 15 km. Cherries are pulped, fermented overnight, washed and sun-dried. Butterscotch, green apple, dark chocolate and cranberry.

beans.name: Ethiopia Lala Salama Decaf
beans.producer: Lala Salama wet and dry mill (owner Alemu Adama), Bensa Woreda, Sidama
beans.listedNotes: Plum, cherry jam, dark chocolate, chocolate mousse, almond finish
beans.desc: Sugarcane decaf from the Lala Salama station in Sidama, owned by Alemu Adama and supplied by about 350 farmers. Full flavour without caffeine. Plum, cherry jam, dark chocolate and chocolate mousse with an almond finish.

beans.name: Brazil Eagle Mogiana
beans.producer: Mogiana region (São Paulo / Minas Gerais border); lots from producers including Jose Carlos Alves Pinto and Marcio Martins Ferreira
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, citrus, red fruits; heavy body; cherry and macadamia essence
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An organic certified coffee with a delicate cream and floral aroma, with essence of cherry and macadamia for a rich, creamy espresso. Chocolate, citrus and red fruits with a heavy body. Hand-selected lots from individual Mogiana farms, aiming for a consistent profile from lot to lot and year to year.

beans.name: Abrazo Brazil Colombia Blend
notes: dark chocolate with a hint of acidity
beans.listedNotes: Earthy, dark chocolate with a hint of acidity
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An organic certified blend of Colombian and Brazilian coffees with a strong cream and a chocolate finish: a rich, creamy espresso that is perfect with milk. Earthy, dark chocolate with a hint of acidity.

beans.name: Ugly Duckling Espresso Blend
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An organic certified blend of Colombian, Brazilian and Ethiopian coffees with a strong cream and a floral finish, making a rich, creamy espresso. Earthy, chocolate, blackberry and floral.

beans.name: Colombia Dulima
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, citrus, red fruits; heavy body
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: The Dulima lot was created in 2009 to capture the quintessential coffee profile of central and south Huila, named after the Pijao word for "Snow Queen". Huila is Colombia's first historic coffee department and produces 18% of its coffee, from farms between 1,500 and 2,300 masl. Chocolate, citrus and red fruits with a heavy body.

beans.name: Colombia Regional Inza Cauca - Asorcafe
beans.producer: Asorcafe association (290 members), Inza, Cauca; partner Siruma
beans.processFull: Fully washed (20-40 hour ferment, parabolic dryers)
beans.listedNotes: Blood orange, yellow apple, smoked green tea florals, toffee sweetness; bold big body, very long finish
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: From Asorcafe, an association of 290 small producers in Inza, Cauca, on plots of 1.8-2 hectares at altitudes up to 2,100 masl on the Macizo Colombiano. Fully washed, fermented 20-40 hours and dried 8-15 days in parabolic dryers. Blood orange, yellow apple and smoked green tea florals with toffee sweetness, a bold big body and a very long finish.

beans.name: Colombia Decaf (sugarcane)
beans.producer: 7 producers across Acevedo, Palestina, Pitalito and Timana, Huila (Azahar Coffee Company lot)
beans.processFull: Washed, double fermentation; sugarcane ethyl acetate decaf (Descafecol, Manizales)
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A decaf single origin Colombian coffee, roasted with as much care as any other. A sugarcane decaf lot from Azahar Coffee Company, sourced from 7 producers across 4 municipalities in Huila. Washed with a double fermentation, sun dried for 20-30 days, and decaffeinated with sugarcane-derived ethyl acetate at the Descafecol plant. Hazelnut, chocolate and red apple.

beans.name: Peru Yoner Celis Guerrero
beans.producer: Yoner Celis Guerrero, Huabal, Jaen, Cajamarca (via Falcon)
beans.processFull: Washed; overnight tank ferment, sun dried 10-14 days
beans.listedNotes: Floral like magnolia, lemon, nougat; round, smooth mouthfeel
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A high scoring single origin from Yoner Celis Guerrero's small parcel high in Huabal at 1,700 masl, planted with caturra, pache and nacional (typica). Only 20 bags of exportable coffee were produced. Fermented overnight in concrete tanks, washed and dried on tarpaulin in the sun for 10-14 days. Floral like magnolia, with lemon and nougat and a round, smooth mouthfeel.

beans.name: Rwanda Peaberry Huye Mountain
beans.processFull: Dried on raised African beds for 3-4 weeks (washed assumed not stated)
beans.listedNotes: Cranberry, tonic water, custard; well balanced
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A high scoring 86+ single origin peaberry from Huye Mountain, started in 2012 by David Rubanzangabo, working with smallholder farmers (over 1,300 today) and a Cup of Excellence 2nd place in 2012. Cherries are hand selected, floated, then sun dried on raised African beds for 3-4 weeks. Cranberry, tonic water and custard, well balanced.

beans.name: Costa Rica Honey - BV Arleen & BV Maria Jimenez
beans.producer: Women producers supported by Bean Voyage (BV Arleen and BV Maria Jimenez), via Falcon
beans.listedNotes: Papaya, cherry, plum, milk chocolate, roasted hazelnut; orange acidity, creamy body
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A high scoring single origin honey processed coffee from women producers supported by Bean Voyage, a non-profit working to close the gender gap in farming communities. Papaya, cherry and plum with milk chocolate and roasted hazelnut, orange acidity and a creamy body.

beans.name: Kenya Kii AB 89+
beans.producer: Kii factory, Rungeto Farmers Coop Society, Ngairiama, Kirinyaga
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A high scoring 89+ single origin from the Kii factory, one of three making up the Rungeto Farmers Coop Society (about 3,507 members, founded 1953) in Kirinyaga, grown on red volcanic soil at 1,700-1,900 masl. Handpicked, fermented 24 hours then 12-24 hours, soaked under clean water and dried on tables. Citrus, dark chocolate and raspberry jam.

beans.name: Ethiopia Bombe Dry Fermentation
beans.producer: Bombe washing station (Daye Bensa), Bombe, Shantawene and Keramo communities
beans.listedNotes: Bergamot, blueberry, black tea, lemon drizzle; sweet, intense mouthfeel
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A single origin scoring 87.75 from the Bombe washing station, named for the Bombe Mountains. Processed by a dry fermentation, a washed variation that adds no water to the tank, developed with Los Volcanes Coffee in Guatemala. Bergamot, blueberry, black tea and lemon drizzle with a sweet, intense mouthfeel.

beans.name: Kenya Kabngetuny Washed AB Lot 2
beans.producer: Kabngetuny Farmers Co-operative Society, Kericho County
beans.listedNotes: Lemonade, black currant, blood orange, spicy cinnamon; long sweet finish
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A single origin scoring 88.25 from the Kabngetuny Farmers Co-operative Society in Kericho County, Rift Valley, at around 2,000 masl, which gives women full ownership of land and coffee trees. Lemonade, black currant and blood orange with spicy cinnamon notes and a long sweet finish.

beans.name: Kenya Nduma AA Washed
beans.producer: Nduma factory, Rumukia Farmers Coop Society, Nyeri (about 1,200 smallholders)
beans.listedNotes: Raspberry, lemon, dried pineapple, black tea; complex balanced acidity, deeply sweet
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A single origin scoring 88.25 from the Nduma factory on the southern slopes of Mount Kenya, part of the Rumukia Farmers Coop Society, with about 1,200 contributing smallholders. Bought directly from the auction through a local Kenyan company. Raspberry, lemon, dried pineapple and black tea with a complex balanced acidity and deep sweetness.

beans.name: Ethiopia Organic Danisa
beans.producer: Danisa sub-kebele (37 farmers, Ture Waji drying stations), Guji
beans.listedNotes: Tropical fruits, honeydew melon, dark chocolate; sweet, creamy, subtle bergamot aftertaste
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A single origin scoring 88 from Danisa, a hamlet of 37 farmers in Guji, grown under a natural forest canopy on fertile red clay and loam. Farmers are trained by Ture Waji, who runs the drying stations, where each lot is tagged and its moisture tracked daily for a slow, even dry. Tropical fruits, honeydew melon and dark chocolate, sweet and creamy with a subtle bergamot aftertaste.

beans.name: Colombia Geisha - Hermel Alvarez
beans.producer: Hermel Alvarez, Anserma, Caldas (sourced by Esnayder Quartas)
beans.processFull: Washed (from earlier automated read of the page)
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine florals, bergamot, apricot; delicate, cream-butter body
beans.source: Brood Roastery product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A special single origin Geisha from Hermel Alvarez's farm in Anserma, Caldas, on steep slopes from 1,500 masl, sourced personally by Esnayder Quartas. The Geisha variety traces back to the Gori Gesha forest in Ethiopia and became famous after The Best of Panama auction in 2004. Jasmine florals, bergamot and apricot with a delicate, cream-butter body.

beans.name: Uganda Bukalasi
beans.producer: Smallholders around Bududa and Bukalasi, Mount Elgon, via Zukuka Bora Coffee Company
beans.desc: A natural lot from smallholder farms around Bududa and Bukalasi on Mount Elgon, sourced through Zukuka Bora, which channels a premium and profits into community programmes including education, clean water, savings groups, health and farming support. Cherries are floated, fermented in sealed drums for 12 hours and dried on raised shaded beds for up to 30 days. Strawberry, stone fruits and orange.

beans.name: Kenya Eaagads
beans.desc: From Eaagads Estate in Kiambu County, one of Kenya's earliest coffee-growing areas, founded by Catholic missionaries and owned today by Eaagads Company Limited, listed on the Nairobi Stock Exchange. Washed, fermented 12-48 hours and sun-dried for 2-3 weeks on raised African beds. Blackcurrant, lime and vanilla, juicy.

beans.name: Ethiopia Aroresa
beans.producer: Smallholders, Melesse station (Melesse Mekuria), Aroresa woreda, Sidama; importer Covoya
beans.desc: A grade 1 natural microlot from the Melesse station in Aroresa, Sidama, grown on heirloom varieties at high altitude. Cherries are sun dried on raised beds for 12-15 days, then milled, graded, hand sorted and bagged in GrainPro. Apricot, nougat, caramel and dried fruit.

beans.name: Colombia Dulima
beans.producer: Various smallholders, Huila (Dulima lot); importer Covoya
beans.desc: The Dulima lot was created in 2009 to capture the typical coffee profile of central and south Huila, with lots selected through sensory analysis at origin for consistency. Named from the Pijao word for the Tolima volcano, meaning "Snow Queen". Citrus, red berries, caramel and chocolate.

beans.name: Honduras El Aguacatillo
beans.producer: Alix Yovani Ramirez, Finca El Aguacatillo, Guinope, El Paraiso; importer Covoya
beans.processFull: Washed (16 hour dry fermentation, solar dome dried)
beans.listedNotes: Lime, maple syrup, nutty, red apple
beans.desc: From Finca El Aguacatillo, run by Alix Yovani Ramirez, who began as a farm labourer, bought his first plot in 2005 and now manages 14 hectares in Guinope. Cherries are floated, dry fermented for 16 hours, mechanically washed and dried in solar domes for 8-15 days. Lime, maple syrup, nutty and red apple.

beans.name: DR Congo Kahondo
beans.producer: Smallholders, Kahondo washing station (Virunga Coffee Company), North Kivu; importer Covoya
beans.desc: From the Kahondo washing station, one of nine run by Virunga Coffee Company near Virunga National Park in North Kivu, which has trained over 11,000 farmers and supports Organic and Rainforest Alliance certification. Natural processed, floated and sun dried for 12-15 days on raised African beds. Maple syrup and blackcurrant.

beans.name: Indonesia Patra
beans.producer: Iwannitosa (Iwan) Putra, Atu Lintang, Takengon, Aceh (lot from 50 farmers in Bener Meriah); importer Covoya
beans.listedNotes: Dried cranberry, tropical fruits, dark chocolate
beans.desc: From Iwan Putra, a farmer and processor in Atu Lintang, Takengon, who buys cherries from 440 local smallholders with a strict tolerance for cherry selection, and runs a wet mill, drying tents and wastewater treatment. This lot comes from 50 farmers in Bener Meriah, central Aceh. Natural processed. Dried cranberry, tropical fruits and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Drift Espresso
beans.desc: A medium-dark espresso blend (70% Kalingwe, 30% Bukonzo) roasted deeper than the roastery's usual style, with a rich, heavy body, low acidity and a lingering finish. Made for a fuller, more traditional espresso that performs well in milk and as a straight shot. Dark chocolate, toasted nuts and caramel.

beans.name: Decaf Colombia El Buho
beans.producer: Various smallholders, Huila and Cauca (page also says Huila and Tolima); importer Covoya
beans.desc: A decaf from Colombian smallholders, decaffeinated with ethyl acetate derived from sugarcane: beans are steamed, rinsed with the solvent, dried to 10-12% humidity and sealed with a neutral wax. Toasted nuts, syrup and lemonade.

beans.name: Extrawelt Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, caramel, a hint of whisky; full body, velvety mouthfeel
beans.desc: An espresso blend that works as a classic shot with rich crema and a bold taste, and pairs well with milk. Smooth and rich, with chocolate, caramel and a hint of whisky, a full body, velvety mouthfeel and balanced acidity with a subtle brightness.

beans.name: Honduras SHB
beans.listedNotes: Green apple, juicy apricot, almond kernel, grape-like sweetness
beans.desc: Honduran SHB (strictly high bean) coffee. High-altitude growing slows the plant's maturation and gives a fruitier flavour. Roasted medium for a well-rounded, smooth cup. Green apple, juicy apricot, almond kernel and a grape-like sweetness.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Costa Rican Decaf (Swiss Water)
beans.origin: Costa Rica (from the link name; not stated on the page)
beans.listedNotes: Crisp sweet vanilla finish, creamy chocolate, nutty; low acidity
beans.desc: A medium/dark roast, full-bodied and smooth decaf, decaffeinated with the Swiss Water Method, which uses water and CO2 rather than chemical solvents. Crisp, sweet vanilla finish with creamy chocolate and nutty notes and low acidity.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Espresso Blend

beans.name: House Blend

beans.listedNotes: Light, floral, chocolatey undertones; easy drinking
beans.desc: A blend of three single-origin beans, each roasted separately: lighter roasts keep the floral notes and a slightly darker roast adds a chocolatey undertone. Origins change from time to time. Light, floral flavour with chocolatey undertones, easy drinking, designed for a cafetiere or filter machine.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Coban (Guatemala)
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, rich hazelnut, hints of dark fruit
beans.desc: A high-grown Guatemalan bean with an extraordinarily full body that dominates the palate, from Fairtrade farms. Suggested as an evening coffee, black or with a splash of milk. Dark chocolate, rich hazelnut top notes and hints of dark fruit.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Huehuetenango (Guatemala)
beans.listedNotes: Smooth dark cocoa, sweet cherry aftertaste
beans.brew: Any method; with or without milk
beans.desc: A dark roast Guatemalan coffee grown on the high slopes of Huehuetenango, from Fairtrade farms, good with or without milk. Smooth dark cocoa flavours and a sweet cherry aftertaste.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Old Brown Java
beans.processFull: Aged (unique ageing process, details not stated)
beans.desc: A coffee to be savoured, grown on the volcanic island of Java from a Fairtrade farm, with a distinctive taste from a unique ageing process. Cocoa, dark chocolate and tobacco.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £8.25-£25.00 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Sumatran Mandheling
beans.listedNotes: Herbal, earthy, chocolate; gentle acidity, cocoa sweetness, smooth caramel
beans.brew: Any method; with or without milk
beans.desc: A complex Fairtrade Sumatran coffee with gentle acidity balanced by cocoa sweetness and smooth caramel with an earthy finish, good with or without milk. Herbal, earthy and chocolate notes.
