beans.name: Monsooned Malabar
beans.processFull: Monsooned (aged in open warehouses in monsoon winds)
beans.desc: Beans stored in open warehouses, where monsoon winds and rains make them swell and lose much of their acidity, giving a heavy-bodied, mellow coffee. Chocolate, spice and nuts.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (assumed: low end of the £9.50-£26.50 range, sizes 227g, 454g, 1kg and 4kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Costa Rica Alto San Juan
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, milk chocolate, super sweet; slightly floral finish; rich and buttery mouthfeel
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. listing (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Wonderfully moreish, quaffable coffee from small growers at the Alto San Juan co-op in Tarrazu, a select small lot picked by hand in baskets only when the cherries reach perfect ripeness. Rich and buttery mouthfeel, caramel and milk chocolate, super sweet with a slightly floral undertone in the finish.

beans.name: Costa Rica San Martin Honey Process
beans.producer: San Martin Coop (Coopetarrazu community lot), San Martin de Tarrazu, Tarrazu
beans.listedNotes: Mango, orange marmalade, cascara; creamy body, long honey finish
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. listing (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A community lot produced entirely by smallholder farmers of San Martin de Tarrazu, a very small hamlet at the highest elevations of Tarrazu, all members of the Coopetarrazu cooperative (founded 1960 by 228 growers, now over 3,000 members). The roastery visited in 2016 as part of its investment in cooperative coffee. Honey processed. Mango, orange marmalade and cascara, with a creamy body and a long honey finish.

beans.name: El Salvador Finca El Porthron
beans.producer: Urrutias family (Rene Urrutias), Finca El Porthron, El Balsamo Mountain Range
beans.listedNotes: Milk and dark chocolate, sweet floral; super clean mouthfeel
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: From the Urrutias family's Finca El Porthron, a 200 acre farm with 130 acres of coffee and the rest forest and habitat, grown at 1,110 masl in the El Balsamo Mountain Range. The roastery has worked with Rene Urrutias for three seasons and visits every year to develop different processing and picking. Washed. Milk and dark chocolate with a sweet floral balance and a super clean mouthfeel.

beans.name: Mexico Coop Tierra Libertad
beans.producer: Coop Tierra Libertad, Angel Diaz, Siltepec, Chiapas
beans.listedNotes: Fine lemongrass acidity, brown sugar sweetness, tangerine finish
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: From a group of small producers called Tierra Libertad in Angel Diaz, Siltepec, Chiapas, farming Bourbon at around 1,800-1,900 masl after a three-day journey from Mexico City including 47 miles of dirt track. Chiapas coffees are a little brighter and sweeter than most Mexican growing areas, closer to Huehuetenango. Washed. A fine lemongrass acidity balanced by brown sugar sweetness, with tangerine notes in the finish.

beans.name: Mexico Isabella de Triunfo Decaf MW
beans.producer: Alberto Preez, Finca Isabella de Triunfo, Chiapas (next to the El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve)
beans.listedNotes: Candied sweetness, bright acidity, bakers chocolate, red berries, a little orange; smooth long finish
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A Mountain Water decaf from Alberto Preez's 7.3 hectare Finca Isabella de Triunfo, next to the El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve in the Sierra Madre de Chiapas, at 1,200-1,500 masl. Selectively picked, pre-sorted and wet processed on the day of harvest. Candied sweetness and bright acidity with bakers chocolate, red berries and a little orange, and a smooth long finish.

beans.name: Colombia Inga Mystique Narino
beans.listedNotes: Swiss chocolate, vanilla, orange creamsicle; piquant acidity, creamy body
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Produced by Sandona Group, a small producers' association of about 17 coffee growers in Sandona, Narino, in partnership with exporter Inconexus. Grown under Inga shade trees at 1,900-2,000 masl and wet-milled at Belcosub. Swiss chocolate, vanilla and orange creamsicle with a piquant acidity and creamy body.

beans.name: Colombia Condor Cerro Bravo CO2 Decaf
beans.producer: Juan Camilo Restrepo, La Sierra farm, Palomos, Fredonia, Antioquia
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, pecan; silky, rich, full round body, soft finish
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A decaf grown at La Sierra, Juan Camilo Restrepo's third generation 68 hectare farm in Palomos near Fredonia, Antioquia, shade grown under guamo and fruit trees facing the Cerro Bravo peak at 1,420-1,590 masl. CO2 decaffeinated. Silky and rich with a full round body and notes of caramel and pecan with a soft finish.

beans.name: Peru San Ignacio MW Decaf
beans.producer: Association of small growers, San Ignacio, Cajamarca
beans.listedNotes: Tomato vine, lemon, rich butter; refined citrus acidity
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Decaf from the San Ignacio District in Cajamarca, grown shade covered at 1,250-1,480 masl by an association of small growers on plots averaging 3 hectares, washed and sun dried. Decaffeinated by the Mountain Water Process in Veracruz, Mexico (99.9% caffeine free, organic and Kosher certified). Tomato vine, lemon and rich butter with a refined citrus acidity.

beans.name: Rocket 88 Blend
beans.producer: 50% El Salvador Finca El Ingenio los Ausoles (washed micro lot), 30% Brazil Sitio Sao Jose (natural), 20% Brazil Fazenda Rio Verde (washed)
notes: fruity acidity and deep chocolate with macadamia nuts and a long finish
beans.listedNotes: Big creamy sweetness, fruity acidity and deep chocolate with macadamia nuts and a long finish
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. Electric Blends listing (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An espresso blend built on Brazil and El Salvador: 50% El Salvador Finca El Ingenio los Ausoles (a washed micro lot), 30% Brazil Sitio Sao Jose (natural, to balance the washed acidity) and 20% Brazil Fazenda Rio Verde (washed). Big creamy sweetness, fruity acidity and deep chocolate with macadamia nuts and a finish to die for.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £9.50-£34.00 range; sizes 250g, 500g, 1kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Electric Blend
beans.producer: 55% Brazil Fazenda Progresso, 25% Colombia Finca Sabintas, 20% El Salvador Finca La Arada

sweet nuttiness and almond (marzipan) balanced by fruity acidity

Good body and a rich fruity base, sweet nuttiness and almond (marzipan) balanced by fruity acidity, with a lovely rounded, lush finish.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of £9.50-£34.00 range; sizes 250g, 500g, 1kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Traction Blend
beans.producer: 40% India Sethuraman Pulped Natural, 30% Guatemala Finca El Bosque, 30% Ethiopia Djimmah Wild Grown
notes: Creamy and smooth with a little bright acidity
beans.listedNotes: Creamy and smooth with a little bright acidity, good depth, body and crema; takes milk well
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. Electric Blends listing (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A blend with nice complexity and a little brightness from the wild grown Ethiopian Djimmah, with sweet fruit from Guatemala Finca El Bosque and India Sethuraman Pulped Natural for richness and depth. Creamy and smooth with a little bright acidity and a good depth, body and crema, and it takes milk well. Same blend as Coffee Real's Six am.

beans.name: Short Circuit Decaf Blend
beans.producer: 40% Colombia Condor Cerro Bravo CO2 decaf, 34% El Salvador Santa Adelaida CO2 decaf, 26% Brazil Oberon Cerrado CO2 decaf
beans.listedNotes: Mellow roundedness, bright fruit notes, medium-ish finish; crema holds up well; great with milk
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)

Down on caffeine but not on flavour; shots are a little smaller for decaf espresso, stopping as the consistency becomes loose or the colour blondes. Mellow roundedness with bright fruit notes, a medium-ish finish and a crema that holds up surprisingly well, great with milk.
beans.priceBasis: 250g (assumed: low end of the £9.80-£36.00 range, sizes 250g, 500g and 1kg; unconfirmed)

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Rainha
beans.producer: Fazenda Rainha (family farm since 1890; 2011 Brazil Cup of Excellence 1st place), Minas Gerais / Sao Paulo state line
beans.listedNotes: Stone fruit, chocolate, caramel, toffee; excellent sweetness
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: From Fazenda Rainha, a family farm since 1890 and 1st place producer in the 2011 Brazil Cup of Excellence, on the Minas Gerais state line with a 190 hectare coffee area farmed entirely by hand because of the topography, at 1,150-1,350 masl. The owner runs native tree planting, wastewater treatment and a school van, club and housing for employees. Natural processed. Fruity for a Brazil (stone fruit) with the normal Brazil chocolate, caramel and toffee notes and excellent sweetness.

beans.name: Brazil Sitio Sao Jose
beans.producer: Sitio Sao Jose, Luiz Roberto, Carmo de Minas, Mantiqueira, Minas Gerais
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, sweet-meal biscuit, dark dried fruit acidity; full bodied, thick mouthfeel
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Owned and managed by Luiz Roberto in Carmo de Minas, southern Minas Gerais, on the rim of the Mantiqueira range at about 1,150m. The mountainous farm and its springs and streams suit high quality beans, with average rainfall of 1,800mm and 18C. Luiz Roberto grows alongside sustainability and environmental preservation. Natural processed. Dark chocolate, sweet-meal biscuit and dark dried fruit acidity, with a full body and thick mouthfeel.

beans.name: Ethiopia Djimmah Forest Harvested
beans.producer: Kaffa (south west Ethiopia), various small growers; forest harvested
notes: winey finish with a lasting aftertaste
beans.listedNotes: Fusty wild chocolate, malty caramel sweetness, winey finish with a lasting aftertaste
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Natural processed coffee grown in the Kaffa and Illubabor regions of south western Ethiopia, which account for around half of Ethiopian coffee exports (mostly commercial grade) but also produce a limited amount of specialty grade, mainly forest harvested: self sown and growing under the shade of natural forest trees. Fusty wild chocolate notes, malty caramel sweetness and a winey finish with a lasting aftertaste.

beans.name: India Sethuraman Estate Plantation A
beans.producer: Sethuraman Estate, Chikmagalur (near Magundi, Bhadra river), producer Nishant Gurjer
notes: a little pepper in the background
beans.listedNotes: Buttery smoothness, rich earthy undertones and nuttiness, a little pepper in the background; aromatic wood, flowers and dark chocolate
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An Indian single estate from deeply forested mature Sethuraman Estate in Chikmagalur, near Magundi on the Bhadra river. Ethiopian heritage varietal, described in the text as pulped natural (the spec lists washed). Restrained, elegant, delicate balance of aromatic wood, flowers and dark chocolate; buttery smooth with rich earthy undertones, nuttiness and a little pepper.

beans.name: Rwanda Bwenda Washing Station
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine florals, bergamot, apple and milk chocolate; juicy, round acidity, velvety body
beans.source: Electric Coffee Co. product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Bwenda washing station in Nyamagabe, southern Rwanda, owned by Bernard Uwitije, who built his first wet mill in 2016 and Bwenda, his third, in 2018 to serve isolated farmers without a nearby station. First operated in 2019 with one container of cherries; he is developing farmer extension programmes and expanding capacity. Jasmine florals, bergamot, apple and milk chocolate with juicy, round acidity and a velvety body.

beans.name: Neighbourhood Blend
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa nibs, raisins; smooth and rich
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A much-loved blend of Brazil, Guatemala and Ethiopia, natural processed, refined over some seven years. A top-end espresso rich in body with balanced acidity and a sweet finish, and a perfect cafetiere with gentle acidity, big mouthfeel and chocolate and raisin notes. Cocoa nibs, raisins, smooth and rich. Suits all brewing methods; the roaster recommends it for espresso.

beans.name: Exe-Mas Roast
notes: added almond and dark chocolate notes
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa nibs, raisins; smooth and rich; added almond and dark chocolate notes

For Christmas it adds notes of almond and dark chocolate for a smooth, indulgent roast with a festive character. Contains added almond and dark chocolate flavourings. Suits all brewing methods; the roaster recommends espresso.

beans.name: Neighbourhood Blend Dark Roast
beans.listedNotes: Cocoa nibs, raisins; smooth and rich
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)

A top-end espresso rich in body with balanced acidity and a sweet finish, and a cafetiere with gentle acidity, big mouthfeel and chocolate and raisin notes. Cocoa nibs, raisins, smooth and rich. Versatile for all brew methods; the roaster recommends espresso.

beans.name: Decaf Brazil (Swiss Water Process)
beans.listedNotes: Custard cream biscuits, caramel, chocolate, nutty; malty, biscuity
beans.brew: Espresso, flat white, latte; any brew method
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A Brazilian decaf (Bourbon and Catuai, 1100-1600m) decaffeinated by the Swiss Water Process, which uses only water to gently filter away the caffeine so it is caffeine-free and chemical-free. beans.name: Kenya Kericho

Fertile land, high altitude and a temperate climate give bold, balanced flavours and a distinctive profile, sourced ethically to support Kenyan farmers. Smooth, chocolate, honey and fruit compote. Ideal for cappuccino, flat white or latte.

beans.name: Ethiopia Duromina #3 Organic

beans.desc: Duromina, from Ethiopia's Agaro region (organic, washed; Kurume and Wolisho varietals), delivers a vibrant cup bursting with ripe fruity sweetness and lemony acidity. Smooth, velvety mouthfeel with layered fruit notes for a well-rounded, deeply satisfying brew. Fruit floral, tangy citrus and peach, balancing lively acidity with rich sweetness.

beans.name: Community Roast
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, hibiscus, caramel, black tea, berries; vanilla
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A bright, balanced blend with a smooth body and juicy lift, bringing together a creamy, chocolate-rich Brazil and a vibrant Kenya bursting with fruit and florals (washed and natural). Roasted medium for balance and versatility; brews beautifully as espresso or filter. Chocolate, caramel and vanilla from the Brazil, with hibiscus, black tea and berries adding brightness from the Kenya.

beans.name: Guatemala Huehuetenango
beans.listedNotes: Butterscotch, peach compote, pear, white chocolate
beans.brew: Filter (V60, pour-over); softer espresso; with or without milk
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A refined high-altitude single origin grown in the cool mountain air of northwestern Guatemala (Huehuetenango, 1,200-2,000m; Bourbon, Caturra and Pache; washed). Slow ripening brings natural sweetness and clarity for a clean, elegant cup with soft fruit and creamy depth. Butterscotch, peach compote, pear and a white chocolate finish. Best as filter to show its clarity and fruit, but lovely as a softer espresso; works with or without milk.

beans.name: Peru Villa Rica Organic #1
beans.producer: Villa Rica, Pasco; Finca Schuler and Finca Vidurrizaga (family-run)
beans.brew: Milk drinks (flat white, cappuccino, latte); espresso
beans.source: Exe Coffee Roasters product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An organic and Fairtrade coffee from two family-run farms, Finca Schuler and Finca Vidurrizaga, in the Villa Rica highlands of Pasco, Peru (1,200-1,800 masl, washed). Soft milk chocolate, gently toasted nuts and a lingering caramel sweetness: reliable, rounded and very drinkable. Best with milk in a flat white, cappuccino or latte, but smooth and balanced black; the roaster says it shines as espresso.

beans.name: A Grinch Before Coffee
notes: earthy roast with dark chocolate and walnut
beans.listedNotes: Rich, earthy roast with dark chocolate and walnut
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Christmas time has a way of awakening the Grinch in all of us. A seasonal coffee to keep festive grumpiness at bay with a boost of caffeine: a rich, earthy roast infused with the indulgent flavours of dark chocolate and walnut.

beans.name: Miracle on Gordon Street
notes: Naturally sweet with subtle chocolate undertones
beans.listedNotes: Naturally sweet with subtle chocolate undertones
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A festive Christmas roast, a celebration of the miracle of coffee. Naturally sweet with subtle chocolate undertones, infused with the warmth of love and joy: the perfect brew to brighten up the festive season.

beans.name: Rise & Shine Roast
beans.listedNotes: Light-bodied, fruity undertones, vibrant Rwandan acidity
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A blend of beans from Rwanda, Guatemala and Brazil, giving a delightful, light-bodied cup with fruity undertones. It highlights the vibrant acidity characteristic of Rwandan coffee, an ideal choice for an invigorating morning brew to kickstart your day.

beans.name: Glasgow Roast
beans.listedNotes: Balanced; rich chocolate with milk, natural sweetness, long comfortable finish; tannin-like notes on the tongue as espresso (Great Taste judges)
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: The coffee that started it all: a mix of beans from India, Kenya, Brazil and Guatemala with a perfectly balanced flavour. Rich Arabica beans plus a wee kick of Indian Red Cherry give it some extra oomph, the roaster's pick for starting the day the Glasgow way. A Great Taste Award winner in 2026, praised by the judges for good balance as an espresso and, with milk, rich chocolate and natural sweetness with a long, comfortable finish.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.listedNotes: Deliciously sweet, chocolatey, balanced with fruity caramel
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A wee dream of a coffee: a vibrant mix of beans from Brazil, Guatemala and Ethiopia. A deliciously sweet, chocolatey flavour balanced with fruity caramel, perfect for a smooth afternoon pick-me-up. Great Taste Award winner (the page text says 2021 in the copy, 2026 in the title).

beans.name: Edinburgh Roast
notes: with milk ripe peach and sweet creamy milk chocolate (Great Taste judges)
beans.listedNotes: Fruity, earthy accents, hazelnut undertones; with milk ripe peach and sweet creamy milk chocolate (Great Taste judges)
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Blended and roasted for Auld Reekie: a flavourful mix of beans from Africa and Central America with fruity notes, earthy accents and undertones of hazelnut. A Great Taste Award winner in 2026; judges found a mellow aroma and pronounced initial sourness with fruit, with milk softening it into layered stone fruit (ripe peach) and sweet creamy milk chocolate.

beans.name: Peru El Oso
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A smooth, balanced Fairtrade organic coffee from Peru with comforting notes of milk chocolate, caramel and gentle citrus. Grown near the Tabaconas Namballe sanctuary; the project supports farmers, forest restoration and endangered spectacled bears through sustainable growing, composting and low-impact processing, improving quality while protecting nature.

beans.name: Brazil Santos
beans.listedNotes: Naturally sweet with chocolate undertones; smooth, mellow, low acidity, slight earthiness
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A light roast that is naturally sweet with chocolate undertones and a medium to good body. The Santos cherries are naturally processed, bringing out the sugars and oils from the bean for a smooth, mellow liquor with low acidity and slight earthiness.

beans.name: Colombian Excelso
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Grown in the volcanic soils of Colombia at 1,400 masl, a citrusy medium roast aimed at adventurous coffee palates, with lemon hints and a sweet finish to wake up your taste buds.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Fruit-like acidity, traditional winey mocha taste, lots of body
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Handpicked and wet processed from the birthplace of coffee, one of the world's most sought after coffees. A distinct fruit-like acidity, traditional winey, mocha taste and lots of body: a smooth all-day coffee.

beans.name: Three Peaks
beans.listedNotes: Light, smooth body, vibrant juicy fruit; well balanced
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A new light blend of three favourite beans from three favourite coffee regions, named for the mountainous regions where coffee is grown. Guatemalan, Brazilian and Ethiopian beans deliver a cup with a light, smooth body and vibrant, juicy fruit notes: well balanced for those who enjoy a bit of everything.

beans.name: Rwanda Kinini
beans.listedNotes: Zesty lemon, tropical passion fruit, creamy white chocolate
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A light roast from Rwanda with zesty lemon, tropical passion fruit notes and creamy white chocolate undertones for a refreshing and indulgent experience.

beans.name: Kenya AA Blue Mountain
beans.listedNotes: Complex, bright acidity, distinctive blackcurrant and cocoa; smooth palate
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: One of the most sought after African coffees, displaying complexity and bright acidity with distinctive blackcurrant tones and cocoa notes. Uplifting and vibrant with a smooth palate and a medium to light body.

beans.name: Lively Latin Roast
notes: Well-rounded and balanced South American profile
beans.listedNotes: Well-rounded and balanced South American profile
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: Highlighting the finest qualities of the roaster's South American selection, this medium roast blend combines beans from Colombia, Brazil and Guatemala for a well-rounded, balanced flavour profile that captures the essence of South American coffee.

beans.name: Ethiopian Djimmah
beans.listedNotes: Rich, earthy, dark cocoa, walnut; low acidity, good chocolate aftertaste
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A medium roast Ethiopian Djimmah (also called Jimma), from the Illubabor and Kaffa regions at 1,341-1,829m, in the largest catchment area in Ethiopia. Plants are shaded by larger forest trees, and the variety is thought closest in flavour to the original wild plant. Rich and earthy with dark cocoa and walnut, full of flavour with low acidity and a good chocolate aftertaste; a mild character offset by a subtle gamey aftertaste.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: A Central American coffee decaffeinated using the solvent-free Swiss Water Process. The roaster always recommends coffee in its natural caffeinated form, but for those who like a wee decaf this uses fresh clean water and no chemicals, which the page says removes 99.9% of caffeine versus about 97% for chemical decaffeination.

beans.name: Black Forest Roast
beans.listedNotes: Powerful dark chocolate and cherry, hint of red fruit; smooth, good body

beans.name: Italian Rich Roast

beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: With a high percentage of Robusta beans, this coffee has a significant caffeine content and is one of the roaster's strongest roasts, not one for the faint hearted. A robust and daring flavour from a blend of beans from Brazil, Guatemala and the Indian Cherry Robusta.

beans.name: Full French
beans.source: Gordon Street Coffee product page (pasted by user)
beans.desc: An extra dark roast: intense and smoky, giving the caffeine kick you are looking for.

beans.name: Guatemalan Rich Roast

beans.name: Colombian Jazz

A complex medium to dark roast with chocolate, caramel and cherry notes, a pleasant cherry acidity and full body. Suits cafetiere, espresso and moka pot, and is a good base for a flat white.

beans.name: Brazilian Samba

Flexible, works well in milk-based drinks; the roaster recommends cafetiere. Holds a 2-star Great Taste Award.

beans.name: Zambia, Kateshi Estate
beans.producer: Northern Province; Kateshi Estate, Mafinga Plateau
beans.desc: A medium-roast natural from one of Zambia's oldest farms, on a high plateau. Lime candy, boozy notes and toasted nuts.

beans.name: Colombia, ASOMUJER, EA Decaf de Cana (Women Producers)
beans.listedNotes: Malt, mild vanilla, dried citrus; mellow sweetness
beans.desc: A sugarcane decaf from a women-led cooperative in Huila, decaffeinated with naturally derived ethyl acetate to keep its sweetness and clarity. Medium roast with malt, mild vanilla and dried citrus.

beans.name: Rwanda, Abadatezuka Coop
beans.producer: Western Province, Cyato sector, Nyamasheke; Abadatezuka coop
beans.listedNotes: Fruity with mellow spice notes; tart acidity
beans.desc: A natural anaerobic microlot from a highland smallholder co-op, with cherries processed at Cyato Washing Station. Fruity with mellow spice notes and tart acidity.

beans.name: Kenya, Etago Extra Special, Lot 20
beans.processFull: Anaerobic, 4 days with natural yeasts and Ava mould, raised beds
beans.desc: A microlot from West Kenya fermented anaerobically for four days with natural yeasts and Ava mould to enhance fruit flavours, then dried on raised African beds.
beans.priceBasis: Size not stated (single option) (page one-time price)

beans.name: Malawi, Pamwamba Cooperative, AA Plus
beans.producer: Mpanga and Ngapani estates (Rainforest Alliance certified)
beans.listedNotes: Floral, tropical stone fruit; citric acidity, smooth body
beans.desc: A medium-roast washed coffee from the Mpanga and Ngapani estates in Malawi, both Rainforest Alliance certified. Floral and tropical stone fruit notes with a citric but unobtrusive acidity and a smooth body.

beans.name: Hawaii, Kona Prime
beans.producer: Kona district, slopes of Hualalai; Kona Coffee & Tea (Waiono Meadows)
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, hazelnut, peach, pineapple, strawberry; silky, sweet mouthfeel
beans.desc: A medium-roast washed Kona coffee from the family-owned Kona Coffee & Tea estate on the slopes of Hualalai, grown above 2,000 feet. Smooth and delicate, with caramel, hazelnut, peach, pineapple and strawberry and a silky, sweet mouthfeel.

beans.name: D. R. Congo, North Kivu, Kahondo Coffee Washing Station
beans.producer: North Kivu, Isale; Kahondo washing station (Virunga Coffee Company)
beans.desc: A washed Bourbon from the Kahondo washing station, one of nine run by Virunga Coffee Company on the edge of Virunga National Park in North Kivu. Sun-dried on raised beds, it is juicy with strawberry, lemon and raspberry.

beans.name: Breakfast Coffee
beans.listedNotes: Light, smooth; medium body, low acidity
beans.source: The House of Coffee product page
beans.desc: A smooth all-day blend of gourmet beans, freshly roasted. Light and smooth with a medium body and low acidity. It suits cafetière and filter.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (lowest price in range, confirmed by user)

beans.name: Indonesian Surprise
beans.source: The House of Coffee product page
beans.desc: A smooth, aromatic espresso blend of Indonesian and Ethiopian Arabica beans. Chocolatey and rich, and described as a good way to end a meal.
beans.priceBasis: 227g (lowest price in range, confirmed by user)

beans.name: Honduras APROCOMSA
beans.desc: Naturally processed coffee from Marcala, Honduras, with notes of stone fruit, blueberry and chocolate. Part of the Sweet & Funky range: expressive and a little wild, but still beautifully sweet and balanced.

beans.name: Three Years Late
beans.source: Mac & Me Roasting product page (Three Years Late)
beans.desc: A blend that sits between the roaster's Homeblend and Born 40: the fruitiness of Homeblend with the heavier mouthfeel of Born 40, for a rounded, balanced cup. Works with or without milk and suits any brew method.

beans.name: Costa Rica - Land Between Two Rivers
beans.listedNotes: Freeze-dried raspberries, rose petals, lemon iced tea
beans.brew: Cafetière, V60, Chemex, AeroPress (not best for espresso)
beans.desc: A microlot from the century-old Aquires estate on the slopes of the Turriabla volcano, picked over many passes for ripe cherries only. The estate is carbon neutral. Expect freeze-dried raspberries, rose petals and lemon iced tea with a bright, effervescent finish. Best as filter or cafetière and without milk.

beans.name: Born 40
beans.desc: The alter ego of the roaster's Homeblend, leaning towards the chocolatey, nutty and biscuity end of the spectrum. Works with or without milk and suits any brew method.

beans.name: Mac&Me Homeblend
beans.desc: The roaster's house blend, made from South American origins: wonderfully fruity with notes of marzipan and hazelnut, a silky mouthfeel and balanced acidity. Works with or without milk and suits any brew method.

beans.name: Verity's Birthday
beans.desc: Three Years Late combined with an Ethiopian coffee from Sidama, grown by about 940 producers in a co-op and washed at the Buncho station. With the Brazilian and Colombian origins it makes a rich-bodied cup with blackcurrant, chocolate and a slight orange acidity.

beans.name: Mac&Me CBI Decaffeinated
beans.desc: Chemical-free decaffeinated single origin, currently from Finca Nuevo Esperanza in Mexico, a pesticide-free family farm at 1,200-1,500m. Decaffeinated with the Mexican water process, which uses no chemicals and keeps the flavour. Expect toffee, marzipan and almonds, with or without milk.

beans.name: Colombia - Finca La Joyeria
beans.producer: Finca La Joyería, Santa Barbara Estate, Antioquia
beans.desc: Finca La Joyería (the jewel), one of five sister farms on the Santa Barbara Estate in Antioquia, grown at 1,700m in the Andes. Fully washed and milled on the farm, with a creamy mouthfeel and notes of yellow plum, caramel and almonds. Best without milk.

beans.name: Brazil - Lot A40 - Ipanema
beans.producer: Rio Verde farm, area B68, Premier Cru range
beans.brew: V60, Chemex, AeroPress, cafetière, filter (not espresso)
beans.desc: A Premier Cru micro lot of Yellow Bourbon from the highest part of Rio Verde, the estate's oldest farm, hand-picked at 1,200m. A dry anaerobic fermentation gives moderate acidity, raspberry fruit and a long aftertaste. Not for espresso and best without milk.

beans.name: Costa Rica: ARBAR - El Manantial
beans.producer: Arbar micromill (Carlos Arrieta and Maria Barboza), Lourdes de Naranjo, Western Valley
beans.desc: A honey-processed Villa Sarchi from the Arbar micromill in Costa Rica's West Valley: a zing of lemon and white sugar softening into sweet Cantaloupe melon, with orange and white grape as it cools. Sweet, bright and clean.

beans.name: Costa Rica: Arbar - La Isla
beans.producer: Finca La Isla, processed at the Arbar micromill (Arrieta Barboza family), Lourdes de Naranjo
beans.desc: A honey-processed Caturra and Catuai blend from Finca La Isla, processed at the Arbar micromill: crisp green fruit starting with lime marmalade, then white grape and a gentle gooseberry aftertaste for a crisp but sweet finish.

beans.name: Costa Rica: Arbar, San Roque Kenya, Honey
beans.producer: Arbar micromill (Arrieta Barboza family), Lourdes de Naranjo, Western Valley
beans.listedNotes: Lemon and lime, white sugar, apricot
beans.desc: A honey-processed San Roque Kenya variety from the Arbar micromill, best as a filter: bright lemon and lime over delicate white sugar sweetness, with apricot emerging as it cools. Also makes a fruit-forward espresso.

beans.name: Costa Rica: Don Joel - Finca Carmela
beans.producer: Finca Carmela, processed at the Don Joel micromill (Allan Oviedo), Alajuela, Western Valley
beans.desc: A honey-processed Villa Sarchi from Finca Carmela, a three-hectare farm. It opens with silky wine gums and a lift of lime and raspberries, with juicy black grapes on the finish.

beans.name: Costa Rica: Don Mayo - La Ladera
beans.producer: La Ladera (Pablo Bonilla), Don Mayo micromill, Tarrazú
beans.desc: A honey-processed Catuai from La Ladera in Tarrazú: a dessert in a cup that starts with soft cooked peach, finishes with brown sugar and has a delicate strawberry edge. Well balanced and all-day drinking.

beans.name: Costa Rica: Granitos - Ortiz 1800
beans.producer: Granitos de Altura del Ortiz micromill (Johana and Joyce Calderón), Tarrazú
beans.desc: A yellow-honey Catuai from the family-run Granitos de Altura del Ortiz micromill in Tarrazú: gentle peach sweetness slipping into marzipan, with sultanas and a dash of cream on the aftertaste.

beans.name: Brazil: Nova Alianca, SC Decaf
beans.producer: Nova Alianca; coffee information lists Fazenda Cruz Alta
beans.desc: A decaffeinated Brazilian single origin: a sweet cup of chocolate milk with roasted hazelnuts and creamy walnuts, for any time of day. The decaf origin changes through the year.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, Centroamericano H1, Natural
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.desc: A natural Centroamericano H1 from Finca Argentina: like banana bread spread with thin-cut marmalade and topped with pomegranate seeds. Sweet, tangy and balanced.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, Icatu, Natural
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.desc: A rare natural Icatu (a Brazilian variety) from Finca Argentina: warm apple strudel with almonds and a toffee drizzle. Gentle, rounded and easy drinking.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, SL28, Natural
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.desc: A natural SL28 from Finca Argentina: sweet but crisp honeydew melon with gentle yellow plum, and the darker sweetness of dates and figs on the finish. Smooth and silky.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, SL28, Washed
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.desc: A washed SL28 from Finca Argentina: a sweet, sticky hit of lime marmalade that shifts into milk chocolate with a little walnut as it cools.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, Yellow Pacamara, Natural
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.desc: A natural Yellow Pacamara from Finca Argentina: fresh, sweet pear with a restrained natural funk that adds a miso caramel edge, and a bite of bitter orange on the aftertaste.

beans.name: El Salvador: Finca Argentina, Yellow Pacamara, Washed
beans.producer: Finca Argentina (Martinez family), Ahuachapán; dry milled at Los Ausoles
beans.listedNotes: Tinned peaches, strawberry, fruit salad sweets
beans.desc: A washed Yellow Pacamara from Finca Argentina: tinned peaches and strawberries up front, shifting to pineapple as it cools, with a lingering fruit-salad-sweets sweetness. Super sweet and elegant.

beans.name: Festive Blend
beans.producer: 50% El Salvador Finca Argentina (washed), 30% Guatemala San Patricio El Limón (washed), 20% Brazil Matas de Minas (pulped natural)
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, dark caramel, hazelnut praline
beans.desc: Ozone's limited-edition Christmas blend: dark caramel swirling through creamy milk chocolate, finished with hazelnut praline. Sweet, balanced and easy drinking. A donation goes to the charity Felix with each bag.
beans.priceBasis: 220g (giftable presentation box; 500g and 1kg options are not boxed)

beans.name: Festive Single Origin
beans.producer: Yukro kebele, Jimma (27 smallholders; Telila washing station, Mike Mamo)
beans.desc: Ozone's 2026 Christmas single origin from Yukro in Jimma, Ethiopia: a classic clean washed coffee bursting with sweet lemon, passionfruit and dried apricot, with a hint of malted milk biscuit on the finish.
beans.priceBasis: 220g (giftable presentation box; 500g and 1kg options are not boxed)

beans.name: Guatemala: San Patricio El Limón, Caturra, Natural
beans.producer: San Patricio El Limón (Reyes family), Palencia
beans.desc: A natural Caturra from San Patricio El Limón: black cherry yoghurt at the heart of the cup, with plum and currants, and the warmth of brandy and sweet almonds on the finish.

beans.name: Half Caff
beans.producer: 50% Brazil Matas de Minas (sugarcane decaf, natural), 50% El Salvador Argentina Estate (washed)
beans.desc: A 50/50 blend of decaf and regular coffee, so you get all the flavour for half the caffeine: sweet milk chocolate and brown sugar over a delicate biscuit edge. Components change with the seasons.

beans.name: Hodson
beans.producer: 40% Ethiopia Tokuma Group, 40% El Salvador Finca Argentina, 20% Brazil Nova Aliança
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, brown sugar, red fruit
beans.desc: Ozone's founders' blend: a sweet base of brown sugar and milk chocolate that shows off soft red fruit for a balanced but characterful cup. Components change with the seasons.

beans.name: Nicaragua: Limoncillo, Ethiosar, Natural
beans.listedNotes: Rum & raisin fudge, sultana, red apple
beans.desc: A natural Ethiosar from Finca Limoncillo: a big punch of rum and raisin fudge, sweet sultanas through the middle and a gentle red apple note for balance.

beans.name: Organic Single Origin
beans.producer: Comite Agua Azul, San Antonio de Chingama, Huabal (Jaén), Cajamarca
beans.desc: Ozone's year-round certified organic single origin, currently from the Agua Azul comité in Cajamarca, Peru (also Fairtrade): an easy-drinking cup of cookies and cream, starting with milk chocolate and a biscuit edge and finishing in caramel. The origin changes every 4 to 6 months.

beans.name: Our House
beans.producer: Costa Rica Atenas, Brazil Nova Aliança and Matas de Minas, Nicaragua Limoncillo
beans.desc: Ozone's signature seasonal blend and the coffee they'd hand to anyone: a well-balanced medley of milk chocolate and caramel with a sprinkle of roasted nuts. Works in espresso, filter and any other method.

beans.name: Paramount
beans.producer: 80% Brazil Selvatech peaberry (natural), 20% Costa Rica Atenas (washed)
beans.desc: Ozone's darker roast: toffee and cacao nibs up front, finishing long on dark chocolate. Full-bodied and chocolatey, it stands up in milk drinks and works as filter too.

beans.name: Seasonal Blend
beans.producer: Costa Rica Finca Licho (honey), Guatemala San Patricio El Limón (washed), El Salvador Finca Argentina (natural)
beans.desc: A sweet seasonal blend that works as espresso or filter: a punnet of nectarines with a handful of almonds, and silky dried apple that lingers. Components change with the harvest.

beans.name: House Coffee
beans.desc: A dark-roast house blend with hints of milk chocolate.

beans.name: Nogales Nocturne
beans.desc: A one-of-a-kind limited-edition Colombian Geisha with notes of lavender, orange blossom and brown sugar.

beans.name: House Espresso
beans.desc: A dark espresso-roast blend with hints of milk chocolate.

beans.name: Decaf House Blend
beans.desc: A decaf version of the house blend: a dark roast with hints of milk chocolate.

beans.name: Sitio De Jaja
beans.desc: A dark-roast Brazilian single origin with hints of dark chocolate and cocoa nibs.

beans.name: Tutti Frutti Espresso
beans.desc: A medium espresso-roast Colombia and Rwanda blend with hints of tutti frutti sweets.

beans.name: Fruit & Nut Espresso
beans.desc: A dark espresso-roast Brazil and Tanzania blend with hints of milk chocolate, almond and raisin.

beans.name: Mi Regalo
beans.desc: A medium-roast Honduran single origin with hints of dark chocolate and orange.

beans.name: Fazenda Reis
beans.desc: A medium-dark roast Brazilian single origin with hints of chocolate and peanut butter. Marked as a best seller.

beans.name: Bourbon Cream Filter
beans.desc: A dark-roast Brazil and Colombia blend with hints of Bourbon cream biscuits. Marked as a best seller.

beans.name: Bourbon Cream Espresso
beans.desc: A dark espresso-roast Brazil and Colombia blend with hints of Bourbon cream biscuits. Marked as a best seller.

beans.name: El Diamante La Reserva
beans.desc: A light-roast Colombian single origin with hints of white stone fruit and milk chocolate.

beans.name: La Cascada
beans.desc: A light-roast Honduran single origin with hints of strawberry and raspberry.

beans.name: El Aguacate
beans.desc: A light-roast Honduran single origin with hints of strawberry candy.

beans.name: Samuel's Coffee
beans.desc: A medium-roast Colombian single origin with hints of milk chocolate and biscuit.

beans.name: Matazano
beans.desc: A medium-roast Honduran single origin with hints of dark chocolate.

beans.name: Montecillos Espresso
beans.desc: A medium espresso-roast Honduran single origin with hints of raspberry and black cherry.

beans.name: Zapote Espresso
beans.desc: A light espresso-roast Honduran single origin with hints of dark chocolate.

beans.name: Kibuye Decaf
beans.desc: A light-roast decaffeinated Rwandan single origin with hints of blackcurrant.

beans.name: El Laurel
beans.desc: A light-roast Honduran single origin with hints of orange and mandarin.

beans.name: Haro Wachu Kebele
beans.desc: A light-roast Ethiopian single origin from Haro Wachu Kebele with hints of black tea and stone fruit.

beans.name: El Durazno Espresso
beans.desc: A medium espresso-roast Honduran single origin with hints of plum sauce.

beans.name: Rich Christmas Coffee 250g
beans.desc: A rich, comforting medium roast with creamy hints of chocolate orange.

beans.name: Rich Christmas Espresso 250g
beans.desc: A rich, comforting medium espresso roast with creamy hints of chocolate orange.

beans.name: Rich Christmas Decaf 250g
beans.desc: A smooth, balanced decaf medium roast with rich hints of chocolate tiffin and shortbread.

beans.name: Fruity Christmas Coffee 250g
beans.desc: A bright, fruity medium roast with vibrant hints of cherry liqueur.

beans.name: Fruity Christmas Espresso 250g
beans.desc: A bright, fruity medium espresso roast with vibrant hints of cherry liqueur.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.desc: A blend of well-selected Arabica beans from Brazil, El Salvador and India. A large, robust espresso with a touch of caramel sweetness, mild acidity and good balance: rich, creamy, smooth and sweet, with a milky base and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Dark Roast
beans.desc: The House Blend roasted a little darker, giving a stronger, richer-bodied coffee with a flavour that is almost roasty without being burnt. One for strong-coffee drinkers.

beans.name: Tricontinental Harmony Blend
beans.listedNotes: Berry, stone fruit, sweet vanilla, milk chocolate
beans.desc: A blend of premium Arabica speciality beans from Indonesia, Brazil and Costa Rica: a vibrant espresso bursting with berry and stone fruit aromas, sweet and complex with a velvety body. With milk it tastes of sweet vanilla and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Global Origins Medley Blend
beans.desc: A rich, full-bodied espresso blend for those who enjoy complex coffees: intense flavours with notes of dark chocolate and a very mild, velvety acidity. With milk it has a rich nougat sweetness and baker's chocolate flavour.

beans.name: BrazilaGuatamagic Blend
beans.desc: A unique Arabica mix of Guatemalan and Brazilian beans: an espresso with a medium body, mild acidity, sweetness from maple syrup and subtle pecan notes.

beans.name: Brazil
beans.desc: A mild, balanced Brazilian single origin roasted to a flavour that is easy to enjoy, with caramel and chocolate notes. Brazilian coffee is often the foundation of blends because it is so well balanced.

beans.name: El Salvador
beans.desc: A sweet, mild El Salvador single origin from the Las Isabellas farm, which has 175 acres of natural forest, springs and waterfalls, grown at 1,200 to 1,450m. Delicious chocolate and plum flavours.

beans.name: Ethiopia
beans.desc: Grown at about 1,600m in Oromia in south-western Ethiopia. A full-bodied coffee with a wild, winey flavour: sweet, fruity and vinous.

beans.name: Guatemala
beans.producer: Estates in the volcanic valleys around Antigua
beans.desc: From estates in the volcanic valleys around Antigua, encircled by the Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes at 1,650m. A delightful body that tastes sweet and chocolaty, with hints of blackberries in the fragrance.

beans.name: Colombia
beans.desc: A chocolatey, nutty Colombian Supremo from Medellin. Best as a filter, where it is delightfully mild; as an espresso it is sweet and slightly bright.

beans.name: Costa Rica
beans.producer: Tarrazu, the Area of the Saints (Strictly Hard Bean)
beans.desc: A Strictly Hard Bean coffee from Tarrazu, the Area of the Saints, grown in rich volcanic soils. Hints of chocolate and plums with a nice creamy body.

beans.name: Metal Mickey
beans.desc: A classic South American blend of Colombian and Brazilian beans with a traditional, chocolatey profile. Designed for versatility and at its best in bean-to-cup machines and traditional espresso, but works well black or with milk. Tasting notes of pecan, maple syrup and cream.

beans.name: Drake
beans.listedNotes: Honey roasted hazelnut, bittersweet cocoa (with milk)
beans.desc: A smooth, clean and sweet blend of El Salvador, Colombia and Brazil coffees, with notes of chocolate and hazelnut. One of the roastery's most versatile blends, it works in espresso, flat whites or a cafetiere. Tasting notes of honey roasted hazelnut and bittersweet cocoa.

beans.name: The Party
beans.desc: A vibrant, fruity blend of Kenyan peaberry, Colombian and Ethiopian coffees: citrus acidity and tropical sweetness over a crowd-pleasing chocolate base. Best suited to espresso. Tasting notes of cranberries, peach and vanilla.

beans.name: El Carmen Sugar Cane Decaf
beans.desc: A Colombian washed coffee from Huila, decaffeinated by the sugar cane process, and a perfect introduction to decaf. Balanced acidity and high sweetness suit both espresso and filter. Tasting notes of cane sugar, raisin and black cherry.

beans.name: Hokey Pokey
beans.desc: A sweet, nutty blend of Brazil, Colombia and El Salvador coffees with Antipodean-inspired flavours: sweet vanilla soft serve, golden honeycomb and a sprinkling of nuts. Designed for longer milk drinks, cappuccinos and lattes. Tasting notes of almond, cream and dark chocolate.

beans.name: The Captain
beans.desc: The original Roasting Party blend of Kenya, Colombia and Sumatra coffees, with layers that mean everyone takes away something different. An introduction to fruit with a pinch of salt for an unconventional edge, and the definitive milk blend. Tasting notes of blackcurrant, sultana and salted caramel.

beans.name: Joe’s Green Balloon
beans.desc: A versatile all-rounder and the roastery's go-to filter blend of Guatemala, Brazil and Colombia coffees. Comforting chocolate flavours with a tea-like quality. Tasting notes of roasted walnut, nougat and chocolate.

beans.name: Los Nisperos
beans.desc: A new single origin from Huehuetenango, Guatemala. A clean, well-defined washed cup with honey sweetness and tangerine brightness, balanced by a smooth cashew-like texture. Bright, balanced acidity lets the body and velvetiness shine in espresso.

beans.name: Sodoci
beans.desc: A beautifully balanced natural Brazilian single origin from Minas Gerais with a creamy mouthfeel and distinctive macadamia nut notes. The finish is bright and delicate, with sweet toffee and crisp clementine.

beans.name: Marcala
beans.desc: The roastery's guest espresso: a well-structured Honduran single origin from La Paz with a rounded body, syrupy caramel sweetness, notes of nougat and a soft dark chocolate finish.

beans.name: House Blend
beans.source: The Suffolk Coffee Company online order page
beans.desc: An espresso blend of different African and Central American coffees, and an ideal way to start your day.

beans.name: Signature Blend
beans.source: The Suffolk Coffee Company online order page
beans.desc: A bold, punchy and smooth coffee at strength 4 out of 5, slow-roasted in small batches to avoid bitterness.

beans.name: Seasonal Blend
beans.source: The Suffolk Coffee Company online order page
beans.desc: A smooth coffee at strength 3 out of 5, slow-roasted in small batches to avoid bitterness. The blend changes with the season.

beans.name: Autumn Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, sweet caramel, hazelnut, cherry, ripe plum
beans.desc: A rich and comforting seasonal blend of 100% Arabica coffee, with indulgent notes of dark chocolate, sweet caramel and hazelnut, balanced by the fruity richness of cherry and ripe plum. Rated 3 out of 5 for strength.

beans.name: Odin: King of the Gods
beans.desc: A bold, complex 100% Arabica blend of Indonesian Java and Ethiopian beans, roasted medium-dark. Full-bodied, with layered notes of cocoa, warm spice and subtle earthiness, lifted by vibrant citrus and delicate floral aromas. Ideal for espresso, cafetiere, filter or bean-to-cup machines.

beans.name: Hengist & Horsa: Kent Blend
beans.desc: A smooth, rich 100% Arabica blend of Papua New Guinea and Indonesian coffees, combining the bright, fruity notes of Papua New Guinea with the deep, earthy tones of Indonesian beans for a balanced, invigorating cup.

beans.name: Ymir: Ancestor of Giants
beans.desc: The roastery's favourite: a bold 100% Arabica blend of Papua New Guinea, Brazil and Indonesia coffees. Rich and full-bodied with deep, earthy undertones and subtle hints of cocoa and tropical fruit, a smooth finish and balanced acidity. Tasting notes of chocolate, cocoa, stoned fruit and nuts.

beans.name: Crema Italia Espresso Blend
beans.listedNotes: Toasted almonds, bittersweet chocolate, hint of caramel, sweet aromatics
beans.desc: A bold, intense Italian roast espresso blend, roasted dark and smoky, with notes of bittersweet chocolate, toasted almonds and a hint of caramel. Full-bodied and velvety with a lingering, slightly spicy finish. 90% Arabica from South America and Africa with 10% Robusta from Asia. Strength 4 out of 5.

beans.name: Freya: Goddess of War
beans.listedNotes: Fruity brightness, smooth nuttiness, deep crema
beans.desc: The coffee shop favourite: a bold blend of Brazilian and Ethiopian Arabica with 10% Indian Robusta. Rich and full-bodied, with fruity brightness from the Ethiopian beans, a smooth nutty undertone from Brazil and a velvety crema from the Robusta.

beans.name: Magni: God of Strength
beans.desc: The premium 100% Arabica blend of Rwanda, Brazil and Ethiopia coffees: a harmonious balance of sweetness, acidity and body, with bright, fruity notes from Ethiopia, nutty and chocolatey undertones from Brazil and a smooth, balanced finish from Rwanda.

beans.name: Heyannir: Smooth & Creamy Blend
beans.listedNotes: Sweet, fruity, rich chocolate, caramel, toffee
beans.desc: A perfectly balanced, smooth and creamy 100% Arabica blend of Colombian and Costa Rican coffees, with sweet, fruity undertones, decadent chocolate, luscious caramel and a touch of buttery toffee. Ideal for espresso, and also shines as an aromatic drip coffee. Medium roast, strength 3 out of 5.

beans.name: The Daily Raid Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A bold 100% Arabica espresso blend of premium beans from across the Americas: a harmonious fusion of chocolate, caramel and stoned fruit. A medium roast with full body and velvety crema, for straight shots and milk drinks, and also good in a French press or moka pot. Strength 3 out of 5.

beans.name: Grand Crema Espresso Blend
beans.listedNotes: Apricot, caramel, dark chocolate, puffed rice, stoned fruit, nuts
beans.desc: An espresso blend created primarily for commercial customers: 75% Arabica from Asia and South America with 25% Robusta, roasted dark. It cuts through milk beautifully in lattes, cappuccinos and flat whites, with depth of flavour as an Americano or straight espresso. Notes of apricot, caramel, dark chocolate, puffed rice, stoned fruit and nuts. Strength 4 out of 5.

beans.name: Super Crema Espresso Blend
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, hazelnuts, puffed rice, sweet fruits, chocolate, cacao
beans.desc: An espresso blend created primarily for commercial customers: 75% South American Arabica with 25% Robusta, roasted medium. It cuts through milk in lattes, cappuccinos and flat whites, with a hint of nuttiness and subtle chocolate undertones, and an amazing crema as an espresso or Americano. Notes of caramel, hazelnuts, puffed rice, sweet fruits, chocolate and cacao. Strength 3 out of 5.

beans.name: Breakfast Blend
beans.listedNotes: Citrusy brightness, hint of nuttiness, subtle chocolate
beans.desc: A 100% Arabica morning blend of Costa Rican and Ethiopian coffees, roasted for a full-bodied character. Lively notes of citrusy brightness, a hint of nuttiness and a subtle chocolate undertone make a well-balanced, energising cup, black or with milk. Strength 3 out of 5.

beans.name: Relaxing Weekend Blend
beans.desc: A smooth, medium roast 100% Arabica blend of Honduran and Rwandan coffees for a leisurely weekend. Velvety caramel, a touch of toasted hazelnuts and a hint of vanilla make a mellow, soothing cup. Strength 3 out of 5.

beans.name: Baldr Decaf: God of Light & Purity
beans.desc: A premium, full-bodied decaf of 100% Brazilian Arabica, decaffeinated by the Swiss Water Process for a smooth, chemical-free cup. A nutty, chocolatey profile with subtle hints of caramel.

beans.name: Vidar: God of Vengeance (High Caffeine)
beans.listedNotes: Deep earthy notes, subtle hint of bitterness
beans.desc: A bold, high caffeine roast made from 100% Indian Robusta beans: smooth and robust, with deep earthy notes and a subtle hint of bitterness. For early mornings or a busy day.

beans.name: Old Brown Government Java
beans.desc: A strong, intense, rich and full-bodied Indonesian coffee grown on the volcanic island of Java and aged for 2 to 5 years, during which the beans turn from green to brown. Medium to dark roasted, with earthy flavours of cocoa, dark chocolate and spice.

beans.name: Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.listedNotes: Lemon, citrus, cocoa, with jasmine, bergamot and tea-like notes
beans.desc: An elegant washed Ethiopian coffee from a smaller area within the Sidamo zone, known for high-grown, high-quality coffees. Lemon, citrus and cocoa notes under fragrant jasmine and bergamot, with bright, crisp acidity and a soft, smooth finish.

beans.name: Brazil: Santos
beans.listedNotes: Earthy, smooth, moderate acidity, medium body
beans.desc: A smooth Brazilian Santos from the Sao Paulo region, with moderate acidity and medium body. Its flavour is dominated by the earthiness characteristic of dry processed coffees. Patio-dried then finished in mechanical driers, which use pergamino from the hulling machines as fuel.

beans.name: Honduras: Abeja Honey
beans.processFull: Not stated (pulped at the cooperative, sun-dried 15 to 22 days)
beans.desc: A Honduran coffee from the Capucas cooperative, produced by families who also keep bee hives. The project promotes honey production among coffee producers and beekeepers, and the extra pollinators and shade trees of plum, banana and guama help yields. Cherries are hand-picked, pulped at the cooperative and sun-dried for 15 to 22 days.

beans.name: Indian Mysore
beans.listedNotes: Smooth, full-bodied, very low acidity, spicy undertones
beans.desc: A premium single-origin Arabica from the shade-covered, high-altitude hills of Karnataka, India (formerly Mysore). Smooth and full-bodied with exceptionally low acidity, a mellow, complex cup that is gentle on the stomach. Intercropped with pepper, spices and fruit trees, which give signature spicy undertones.

beans.name: Monsoon Malabar
beans.processFull: Dry processed, then monsooned for 12 to 16 weeks
beans.desc: A distinctive specialty coffee from the Malabar Coast of southern India, famous for its monsooning process. The dried beans are exposed to the moist southwest monsoon winds for 12 to 16 weeks, swelling and turning pale golden. The result is an exceptionally heavy-bodied, low-acidity coffee with a smooth, syrupy mouthfeel and a pungent flavour profile.

beans.name: Papua New Guinea: AX
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, stone fruit, walnuts; delicate citric acidity; smooth, creamy body
beans.desc: An A-grade, X-sorted coffee from the Papua New Guinea plantation highlands: uniform, clean and reasonably balanced, with pronounced body and acidity and a rich, distinct fragrance. Flavours of chocolate, stone fruit and walnuts, with delicate citric acidity and a smooth, creamy body.

beans.name: Rwanda: Kinini Spring Harvest
beans.desc: A clean, crisp coffee from the Northern Province of Rwanda, grown on small farms and gardens on steep hillsides. Syrupy blackcurrant notes backed with tropical fruit and a floral aftertaste.

beans.name: Brazil Santos
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, caramel, nuts; also caramelised, cocoa, dark chocolate, molasses, nutty
beans.desc: A smooth, sweet Brazilian Arabica with notes of milk chocolate, caramel and nuts, from a natural process coffee grown at 900 to 1100m. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Colombian Dark
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, caramel, soft maple syrup; also apple, lemon, orange, sweet
beans.desc: A bold, full-bodied washed Colombian coffee from Racafe, with notes of dark chocolate, caramel and soft maple syrup. Grown above 1100m from Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties, SCA score 85. Roasted medium to dark.

beans.name: Colombian Excelso
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, caramel, cinnamon; also apple, lemon, orange, sweet
beans.desc: A citric, lively washed Colombian coffee from Racafe, with creamy notes of milk chocolate, caramel and cinnamon. Grown above 1100m from Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties, SCA score 85. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Ethiopian Djimmah
beans.listedNotes: Dark cocoa, walnut, red wine; also berry, fermented, winey
beans.desc: A rich, earthy natural Ethiopian heirloom coffee with notes of dark cocoa, walnut and red wine. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.listedNotes: Jasmine, stone fruits, slight floral finish; also caramelised, lemon, sweet
beans.desc: A lively, delicate washed Ethiopian coffee from the Daye Bensa washing station, with notes of jasmine and stone fruits and a slight floral finish. Grown at 1700 to 2200m from heirloom varieties, SCA score 85. Roasted light.

beans.name: Traditional French
beans.desc: A dark, robust 100% Indian Robusta, naturally processed and grown at 900m. Intense flavours with smoky undertones and notes of cocoa, herbs and tobacco, with high caffeine content. Fairtrade and organic.

beans.name: Guatemalan
beans.listedNotes: Sweet honey, berries, caramel; also cherry, chocolate
beans.desc: A bright, velvety fully washed Guatemalan coffee with creamy notes of sweet honey, berries and caramel. Grown at 1400m from Caturra, and certified Fairtrade, organic and Rainforest Alliance. Roasted medium.

beans.name: Kenyan Blue Mountain
beans.listedNotes: Berries, slight tea-like finish; also blackberry, caramelised, cherry, chocolate, citrus fruit
beans.desc: A bright, citric, bold and punchy fully washed Kenya AA with velvety notes of berries and a slight tea-like finish, grown at 1850m on volcanic, iron-rich soils. Bourbon and Kent varieties, SCA score 85. Roasted light.

beans.name: Monsoon Malabar
beans.listedNotes: Nuts, dark chocolate, spicy kick; also caramelised, cocoa, nutty
beans.desc: A bold, robust monsooned Indian Arabica with earthy notes of nuts and dark chocolate and a spicy kick. Grown at 950m from Kent, roasted medium.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, vanilla; also caramelised, chocolate
beans.desc: A smooth, sweet decaffeinated Brazilian coffee, decaffeinated by the Swiss Water Process to 99.9% caffeine free, with notes of dark chocolate and vanilla. Grown at 900 to 1100m from Bourbon and Catuai, roasted light to medium.

beans.name: The Festive Stag Christmas Blend
beans.listedNotes: Rich dark chocolate, sweet dried fruit, warming spice
beans.desc: A limited edition Christmas blend with rich dark chocolate, sweet dried fruit and warming spice: a little festive cheer in every cup, for cosy winter mornings.

beans.name: The Highlander
beans.desc: A bright, balanced washed Arabica blend of South American and African coffees, with notes of citrus fruits, milk chocolate and honey. Roasted medium.

beans.name: Ballater Blend
beans.desc: A bright, sweet Arabica blend of American and African coffees, naturally processed and washed, with smooth notes of milk chocolate, stone fruits and nuts. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Balmoral Blend
beans.desc: A rich, smooth South American Arabica blend, naturally processed and washed, with creamy notes of caramel, milk chocolate and berries. Roasted medium.

beans.name: Ben Macdui Blend
beans.desc: A rich, bold South American blend, naturally processed and washed, with notes of dark chocolate, nuts and caramel. Includes some Robusta. Roasted medium to dark.

beans.name: Braveheart Blend
beans.desc: A dark, robust Indian blend of monsooned Kent Arabica and Robusta, with smoky undertones and a high caffeine content. Roasted dark.

beans.name: Cairngorm Blend
beans.desc: A lively, delicate Arabica blend of American and African coffees, naturally processed and washed, with notes of cherries, jasmine and bright citrus fruits. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Dark Lochnagar Blend
beans.listedNotes: Smoky notes of dark chocolate and berries
beans.desc: A dark, bold South American Arabica blend, naturally processed and washed, with smoky notes of dark chocolate and berries. Roasted dark.

beans.name: Lochnagar Blend
beans.desc: A rich, full-bodied South American Arabica blend, naturally processed and washed, with smooth notes of dark chocolate and berries. Roasted medium to dark.

beans.name: Royal Stag Blend
beans.desc: A rich, complex South American blend of Arabica and Robusta, naturally processed and washed, with smooth notes of chocolate and red apples. Roasted medium.

beans.name: The Byron
beans.desc: A Brazilian single estate coffee from Alta Mogiana, natural processed and roasted medium dark for classic all-round use, great for espresso and flat whites. Notes of chocolate, apple, hazelnut and dried fruit. Named after Lord Byron, the rebellious son of Nottinghamshire.

beans.name: Street Tuff
beans.desc: A dark roasted blend of speciality Arabica with Vietnamese Robusta to maximise the caffeine and ramp up the flavour. So dark, strong and tough you will want a double shot. Coming soon.

beans.name: Unknown Treasures Espresso Blend
beans.producer: Ichamama Mill (Othaya Farmers Cooperative), Kenya; Asobombo (El Bombo), Pitalito, Huila, Colombia
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, creamy nutty body, cassis finish
beans.source: The Little Coffee Roastery product page
beans.desc: The roastery's flagship espresso blend: big chocolatey aromas with a creamy, nutty body and a classic cassis finish. Wonderful as an espresso, with enough lift to stand out in milky drinks. The current edition combines a fully washed Kenyan from the Ichamama Mill with El Bombo Colombian from Huila.

beans.name: Barnaby Wakes Espresso
beans.listedNotes: Floral and berry highlights, deep caramel body, stone fruit sweetness
beans.source: The Little Coffee Roastery product page
beans.desc: An espresso blend combining wonderful floral and berry highlights with a deep caramel body and stone fruit sweetness. Primarily an espresso, but works well with longer infusion times for cafetieres and drip methods. The current edition has Ethiopian Yirgacheffe heirlooms and a Colombian Caturra from Neiva.

beans.name: Single Origin No. 2 Ethiopian Yirgacheffe
beans.producer: Worka Nenke washing station, Yirgacheffe (about 2,950 smallholders)
beans.source: The Little Coffee Roastery product page
beans.desc: A garden coffee from smallholder farmers around the Worka Nenke washing station in Ethiopia, grown from Jarc, an Ethiopian heirloom sub-variety, at 1,983m. In the cup: peach, honey and bergamot.

beans.name: Single Origin Decaffeinated (Indian Catuai)
beans.source: The Little Coffee Roastery product page
beans.desc: An Indian Catuai decaf from the Ratnagiri district, decaffeinated by the CO2 method, which extracts the caffeine while keeping an excellent flavour profile. No organic solvents are used.

beans.name: Single Origin No. 3 Costa Rica Natural
beans.producer: Finca Santa Elena, Los Santos (Tarrazu); 46ha farm on the Caraigres mountain
beans.source: The Little Coffee Roastery product page
beans.desc: A naturally processed Costa Rican microlot from Finca Santa Elena in Tarrazu, grown at 1,650m on the slopes of the Caraigres mountain. Excellent soil and climate, plus slow drying of the beans on the patios, give a wonderful depth of flavour. Caturra and Catuai varieties.

beans.name: Bankilal - Fully Washed
beans.producer: Tenejapa, Altos de Chiapas; community lot from 16 smallholders (Tzeltal communities), via Ensambles Cafés Mexicanos
beans.listedNotes: Chocolatey, sweet toffee, ripe juicy oranges
beans.desc: A community lot from five high-altitude Tzeltal indigenous communities in Tenejapa, Altos de Chiapas, Mexico, produced by 16 smallholder farmers (6 women, 10 men) at 1,300 to 1,500m under native shade alongside traditional milpa crops. Fully washed heirloom trees. A rich, inviting cup balancing chocolatey, sweet toffee notes with a fruity hint of ripe juicy oranges.

beans.name: Genova - Fully Washed
beans.producer: Colon Genova; Maria Argote farm (2 hectares), Argote Specialty Coffee collective
beans.listedNotes: Sweet deep fruit, rich chocolatey backbone
beans.desc: A fully washed Colombian lot from Colon Genova, grown and meticulously cared for by 78-year-old Maria Argote on her two-hectare farm of 5,000 trees, part of the Argote Specialty Coffee collective and a direct trade project. A cup packed with sweet, deep fruit and a rich, chocolatey backbone.

beans.name: Gitwe - Fully Washed
beans.producer: Gitwe hill, Kayanza province (Long Miles Coffee), edge of Kibira National Park
beans.desc: A fully washed community lot from the Gitwe hill in Kayanza province, Burundi, on the edge of Kibira National Park. Grown by smallholder families alongside subsistence crops and produced by Long Miles Coffee, a farmer-driven model founded in 2011, with rigorous quality control at its washing stations.

beans.name: Lion’s Roar - Honey Process Robusta
beans.producer: Stephan Katongole farm, 200km south of Kampala (coffeeyouknow)
beans.listedNotes: Clean, earthy, chocolaty with hints of fruit; full bodied and spicy
beans.desc: A fan-favourite fine Robusta from Stephan Katongole's farm in Uganda, bought direct trade and honey processed on raised beds. A very clean, earthy and chocolaty cup with hints of fruit: a full-bodied, spicy espresso with the chocolate, depth and spicy earthiness of a traditional Italian espresso, without the bitterness.

beans.name: Frailesca DECAF - Washed Mt. Water Decaf
beans.producer: Frailesca region, Sierra Madre, Chiapas; community lot from 24 communities (via Ensambles Cafes Mexicanos)
beans.desc: A washed community lot harvested by 24 diverse communities across the Sierra Madre mountains in Chiapas, Mexico, gateway to the El Triunfo Biosphere Reserve. Grown in high-altitude edible forests, giving a vibrant cup. Decaffeinated by a chemical-free mountain water process: the green beans are immersed in water in a high pressure filtration system that gradually removes the caffeine.

beans.name: Bookkisa - Natural
beans.producer: Bookkisa sub-kebele, Guji Zone; Dambi Uddo drying station (Sookoo Coffee, Ture Waji)
beans.desc: A clean, vibrant natural process coffee from the Bookkisa hamlet in the Guji Zone of Southern Ethiopia, produced by Ture Waji of Sookoo Coffee, who works directly with about 100 smallholders, and dried on raised beds at the Dambi Uddo station. Notes of oranges, jasmine flowers and creme brulee.

beans.name: Brazilian Santos
beans.listedNotes: Dark cocoa, roasted almonds, creamy finish
beans.desc: A natural process Brazil Santos from Santos, Sao Paulo, grown at 900 to 1,100m from Bourbon and Catuai. Luscious sweetness of cocoa and toasted almonds with a full, velvety body, low acidity and a creamy finish. Medium/dark roast, SCA 80. Good for espresso, cappuccino or French press.

beans.name: Ethiopian Sidamo
beans.listedNotes: Lemon, wild berries, sugar cane; aromas of jasmine and bergamot
beans.desc: A hand-roasted, medium single origin Ethiopian Sidamo from the Daye Densa producer, grown at 1,600 to 2,100m. SCA 85, washed, heirloom varieties. Vibrant lemon zest, wild berry sweetness and delicate floral notes with jasmine and bergamot aromas, a silky body and refined acidity. Best black, as a pour-over or Aeropress.

beans.name: Brazil Santos Decaf (Swiss Water Processed)
beans.listedNotes: Caramelised sweetness, roasted peanuts, dark chocolate
beans.desc: A speciality-grade Brazilian decaf from Minas Gerais, decaffeinated by the chemical-free Swiss Water Process and dark roasted. Luscious caramel sweetness, roasted peanut notes and a smooth dark chocolate finish, bold but balanced with no bitterness. SCA 82.25, Rainforest Alliance certified.

beans.name: Colombia Inza Racafe
beans.desc: A washed Colombian coffee from Inza in the central Andes of Cauca, near the Tierradentro National Park, produced by smallholders across 16 communities and 35 villages and exported by Racafe. Chocolate notes cross with complex fruit: apple, blackberry and grapefruit, with a juicy, round body and smooth, low acidity. Medium roast, SCA 84.75.

beans.name: Guatemala Todosantarita
beans.producer: Huehuetenango; Todosantarita Cooperative, San Antonio Huista
beans.listedNotes: Peach, milk chocolate, dates, vanilla, orange
beans.desc: A washed Guatemalan coffee from the 131-member Todosantarita cooperative in Huehuetenango, in the Sierra de los Cuchumatanes, founded in 1992 and named after a local festival. Sweet notes of milk chocolate and vanilla with delicate hints of peach, dates and orange, a light body and smooth, low acidity. Medium roast, SCA 83.

beans.name: Sevenstones - Colombia Washed
beans.producer: AMACA women producers' association, El Tambo (Cauca); page bean specifics say Tolima, various smallholder farms
beans.desc: A washed Colombian coffee from AMACA (Asociacion de Mujeres Productoras Agropecuarias del Cauca), a group of women coffee producers in El Tambo, Cauca, formed in 1999 by 80 women and now 140 smallholder members, all women farm owners.

beans.name: Eddystone - Lima Peru Washed
beans.producer: Cajamarca; smallholder farmers working with Lima Coffee
beans.listedNotes: Praline, mellow brown sugar, cooked fruit, jammy honeydew
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian coffee from the highlands of Cajamarca, produced by smallholder farmers working with Lima Coffee. Grown at altitude and carefully processed, it delivers a beautifully balanced cup of praline, mellow brown sugar, cooked fruit and jammy honeydew. Named after the Eddystone Lighthouse off the Cornish and Devon coast.

beans.name: Longships - Colombia Decaf
beans.desc: A natural and sustainable decaf from Huila, Colombia, made with the EA (sugar cane, ethyl acetate) process at Descafecol in nearby Manizales. Keeping decaffeination close to origin cuts transport, uses locally grown sugar cane, and uses less water than most other decaf methods. Expect chocolate, almond, brown sugar and citrus.

beans.name: Godrevy - Papua New Guinea Washed
beans.producer: Ulya, Waghi Valley, Western Highlands; various smallholders plus one 178-hectare private farm
beans.listedNotes: Lemon, milk chocolate, cane sugar (soft, sweet and tart)
beans.desc: The roastery's all time favourite coffee is back: a washed Papua New Guinea coffee from lots tendered by the 178-hectare Ulya plantation and several hundred local smallholder farmers. Daylots are blended by quality and cupped at the Ulya mill in the heart of the Waghi Valley, in the Western Highlands.

beans.name: Sennen - Cristal Mexico Washed
beans.producer: Cristal programme: aggregated smallholder lots from Veracruz, Oaxaca and Chiapas
beans.desc: A washed Mexican coffee from the Cristal programme, an aggregated lot from smallholder producers across Veracruz, Oaxaca and Chiapas. Grown at 1,000-1,800 MASL and made up mainly of Bourbon, Typica and Mundo Novo, it shows toffee sweetness, fresh citrus and a bright, tart acidity with a smooth, approachable finish.

beans.name: Runnel Stone - Guatemala Washed
beans.listedNotes: Fresh citrus zest, nutty, cooked cascara
beans.desc: A washed coffee from Huehuetenango in western Guatemala, on the border with Mexico. The region is known for some of the best coffees in Latin America thanks to its climate, altitude, water and traditional varieties, from chocolatey volume lots to fruit-forward microlots.

beans.name: together - House Espresso
beans.desc: A medium-dark espresso blend made for bean-to-cup and home espresso machines. The roast brings out natural sweetness alongside deeper flavours, giving an intense cup that still shows fruit, with a lingering strawberry aftertaste.

beans.name: Indonesia - Iwan Patra Natural
beans.producer: Atu Lintang, Takengon, Sumatra; Iwan Patra (Iwannitosa Putra)
beans.listedNotes: Dried cranberry, tropical fruits, dark chocolate
beans.desc: A natural-process Sumatran coffee from Iwan Patra, a farmer and processor in Atu Lintang, Takengon, who also buys cherries from local smallholders and is strict about cherry selection. Cherries are floated for density separation and dried on a patio under a specialised canopy for 15 to 25 days, giving dried cranberry, tropical fruit and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Worka Chelbesa Natural
beans.producer: Worka Chelbesa, Gedeb, Gedeo (Yirgacheffe Grade 1); producer Negusse Debela
beans.desc: A natural Yirgacheffe Grade 1 from the Kebele community of Worka Chelbesa in Gedeb, the southernmost part of Gedeo. Producer Negusse Debela opened his first site here in 2017 and a second washing station in nearby Danche in 2019, running experimental lots to push quality. Passion fruit, violets and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Boledu Aricha Natural
beans.producer: Yirgacheffe; Aricha washing station, Boledu Coffee
beans.desc: A natural, sun-dried Aricha Grade 1 microlot from Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, from the Aricha washing station supplied to exporter Boledu, which buys directly and funds farmer training. Raspberry sweetness, creamy vanilla and cacao.

beans.name: Guatemala - Blue Ayarza Washed
beans.producer: Lake Ayarza, Santa Rosa; Ayarza cherry mill, smallholders; featured producer Francisco Najera
beans.desc: A washed lot from smallholders around Lake Ayarza in Santa Rosa, processed at the Ayarza cherry mill, which keeps quality consistent across lots. Featured producer Francisco Najera grows in El Naranjo, Jutiapa and runs a nursery selling coffee saplings to other farmers. Red apple, chocolate and blueberry.

beans.name: Timor-Leste - Rotutu Natural
beans.desc: A natural-process coffee from Rotutu in Timor-Leste, roasted medium. Bright lemon and tropical fruit with a jammy sweetness.

beans.name: Mexican Mountain Water Decaf - Quetzal
beans.producer: Chiapas, Frailesca and Sierra Mariscal; 24 high-altitude communities
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate, molasses, spices, orange acidity, creamy body
beans.desc: A single-origin decaf from Chiapas, Mexico, sourced from 24 high-altitude communities across Frailesca and Sierra Mariscal. Chemical-free decaffeination preserves notes of chocolate, molasses and spice with an orange acidity and creamy body.

beans.name: Wilton Benitez Castillo - Colombia Yeast Fermentation
beans.desc: A limited-edition coffee and Lars & Margo's first yeast fermentation lot, produced by Wilton Benitez, who applies fermentation know-how from wine, beer and cheese, using tailored microorganisms and a hot and cold water technique to seal in flavour. Gummy bears, guava and lemon.

beans.name: Brazil - Eagle Monte Carmelo (Cafe Delas)
beans.producer: Monte Carmelo; women farmers via Cafe Delas
beans.desc: A smooth, sweet natural Brazilian coffee for everyday brews and espresso, from Cafe Delas, which sources 100% from women farmers and reinvests part of each sale in programmes for gender equality. Hazelnut, milk chocolate and fruity caramel.

beans.name: Nicaragua - Ojo de Agua
beans.producer: Ojo de Agua farm, Mozonte, Nueva Segovia; Katherin and family
beans.processFull: Washed, raised-bed dried for two weeks
beans.listedNotes: Lemon, orange, caramel, chocolate, roasted almond
beans.desc: A washed Nicaraguan coffee from Ojo de Agua, a family farm of about 10 acres run by Katherin in Mozonte, Nueva Segovia, one of the highest parts of the country. Shaded by guava, lemon, orange, avocado and oak, the cherries are picked and processed by hand and dried on raised beds for two weeks. Lemon, orange, caramel, chocolate and roasted almond with a clean finish.

beans.name: Peru - El Paraiso
beans.producer: El Paraiso, Huabal, Jaen, Cajamarca; several producers via Falcon Speciality
beans.desc: A washed Peruvian coffee from producers in and around El Paraiso, a village in Huabal district, Jaen province, Cajamarca. The producers pick and process their own coffee: cherries rest 24 hours before depulping, ferment for 36 hours and dry for 10 to 15 days. Satsuma, lime, shortbread and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Brazil - Toca da Onca
beans.producer: Toca da Onca, Mantiqueira de Minas; Luciana Flores Martins Swan
beans.listedNotes: Caramel, almond, strawberry, molasses, citric acidity, liquorice body
beans.desc: A natural Brazilian coffee from Toca da Onca, a family-run farm in Mantiqueira de Minas founded over 40 years ago, using regenerative and sustainable farming. It won first place in the 2022 Coopervass Natural category. Caramel, almond, strawberry and molasses with citric acidity and a liquorice body.

beans.name: Ethiopia - G1 Bochesa
beans.producer: Bochesa washing station, Arbegona, East Sidama
beans.listedNotes: Blueberry muffin, strawberry, lime, caramel, bergamot, dark chocolate
beans.desc: A natural Sidama coffee from the G1 Bochesa washing station in Arbegona, set up in 2022 at around 2,000-2,100 m. Ripe cherry is sorted and dried on raised beds for 25 to 35 days, then rested about 20 days before export. Blueberry muffin, strawberry, lime, caramel, bergamot and dark chocolate, gentle and balanced.

beans.name: Colombia - ACC Attia El Silencio
beans.producer: El Silencio, Piendamo, Cauca; Robinson (ACC cooperative, 77 members)
beans.desc: A natural Castillo from El Silencio, an 8-hectare farm in Piendamo, Cauca, run by Robinson and sold through the 77-member ACC cooperative. Very ripe cherries are floated, rested, given a 24-hour humid oxidation in sealed bags and finished on a parabolic dryer. Pineapple, plum, cacao, tamarind and nutmeg.
