beans.name: Colombia Decaf - Atunkaa
beans.listedNotes: Orange, apple, milk chocolate, almond, caramel
beans.desc: A sugar cane decaf from Atunkaa, a family farm in Jardin, Antioquia, in Colombia's Western Andes, where altitude and volcanic soil slow ripening and there are two harvests a year. Orange, apple, milk chocolate, almond and caramel.

beans.name: Blend 26AW - Costa Rica, Peru, Brazil
beans.desc: An espresso blend of coffees from Costa Rica, Peru and Brazil, the 26AW seasonal recipe. Bright red apple and grapefruit sit alongside hazelnut and honey sweetness.

beans.name: Decaf - Colombia Castillo Caturra Washed
beans.desc: A sugarcane-process washed decaf from Colombia, roasted for espresso. Orange and caramel sweetness with almond and milk chocolate.

beans.name: 076 Volcan Azul Gesha - Costa Rica Yellow Honey
beans.producer: Volcan Azul, Poas Volcano, West Valley; family farm (five generations)
beans.desc: A new-harvest yellow honey Gesha from Volcan Azul, a family farm on the Poas Volcano in Costa Rica's West Valley, run by Alejo's family for five generations. Nectarine, chamomile and nectar.

beans.name: 073 Miguel Bohorquez - Colombia Pink Bourbon Washed
beans.producer: El Triunfo farm, Paloquemado, Garzon, Huila; Miguel Bohorquez (Coocentral cooperative)
beans.desc: A washed Pink Bourbon from Miguel Bohorquez's El Triunfo farm in Garzon, Central Huila, sold through the Coocentral cooperative. The trees are named for their pinky-orange cherries and the farm has its own mill and dryer. Fruit punch, honey and chamomile.

beans.name: 072 AA Riakiberu - Kenya Washed
beans.producer: Riakiberu washing station, Kamacharia Cooperative, Murang'a; about 1,300 smallholders
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan AA from the Riakiberu washing station, run by the Kamacharia Cooperative on the slopes of the Aberdare Range in Murang'a, with about 1,300 smallholder farmers delivering cherry. Ripe red fruits, lemonade and raspberry.

beans.name: 071 Gitega Hills - Rwanda Washed
beans.producer: Gitega Hills washing station near Miko, southern highlands; founded by Bernard Uwitije
beans.listedNotes: Mandarin, jasmine tea, red cherry, caramel
beans.desc: A fully washed Bourbon from the Gitega Hills washing station in Rwanda's southern highlands near Nyungwe Forest. It buys cherry from about 1,040 smallholders and employs 150 people, 90% of them women. Mandarin, jasmine tea, red cherry and caramel.

beans.name: 070 Las Brisas - Colombia Washed
beans.producer: Las Brisas farm, Southern Huila; Brayan Smith
beans.processFull: Washed, aerobic fermentation 24-36h, raised-bed dried ~20 days
beans.listedNotes: Orange cream, cream soda, white flowers
beans.desc: A bright, floral washed Bourbon Aji from Las Brisas farm in southern Huila, managed by Brayan Smith. Cherries are hand-picked, depulped the same day, fermented aerobically for 24 to 36 hours and dried on raised beds for about 20 days. Orange cream, cream soda and white flowers.

beans.name: 069 Santa Monica - Colombia Chiroso Natural EF2
beans.producer: Santa Monica farm, Quindio; Jairo Arcila (Cofinet family)
beans.listedNotes: Strawberry, passion fruit, Kyoho grape, violet
beans.desc: A Chiroso natural from Santa Monica farm in Quindio, run by Jairo Arcila. Cherries get 24 hours of aerobic then 50 hours of anaerobic fermentation in sealed GrainPro bags below 22C, then dry on raised beds for about 18 days. Strawberry, passion fruit, Kyoho grape and violet.

beans.name: 059 Pepe Jijon Florcita - Ecuador Sydra Washed
beans.producer: Finca Soledad, Intag Valley; Pepe Jijon
beans.desc: A filter coffee from Finca Soledad, a small biodynamic and organic farm in Ecuador's Intag Valley. Four hectares of coffee sit within 120 hectares of cloud forest, and the farm is also a community project employing local single mothers. Red apple, strawberry, sugarcane and Kirin.

beans.name: 054 Pepe Jijon TyOxy - Ecuador Washed
beans.producer: Finca Soledad, Intag Valley, Imbabura; Pepe Jijon
beans.desc: A limited-production washed filter coffee from Finca Soledad in the Intag Valley, made with Pepe Jijon's TyOxidator process: ripe cherries ferment in open air, are pulped, then sealed in tanks for 48 hours before 20 days of drying. Pear, honey and jasmine tea.

beans.name: 066 Natalia Moreria Brito - Brazil Yellow Catuai Natural
beans.producer: Natalia Moreria Brito (producer not confirmed on page)
beans.desc: A natural Yellow Catuai from Brazil, listed under the name Natalia Moreria Brito. Raspberry, marmalade, caramel and milk chocolate.

beans.name: 064 James Cubilos - Colombia Pink Bourbon Washed
beans.producer: El Triangulo farm, Santa Maria, El Placer, Huila; Jamer Alberto Cubillos Romero (exporter Cuatro Vientos)
beans.desc: A washed Pink Bourbon from El Triangulo, a 2-hectare farm with about 9,000 trees in Santa Maria, Huila, run by Jamer Alberto Cubillos Romero and exported by Cuatro Vientos. Pink lemonade, honey and black tea.

beans.name: 063 Burtukaana Goro Bedesa - Ethiopia Heirloom Natural
beans.producer: Goro Bedessa drying station, West Guji (Hambela Wamena); 149 smallholders
beans.desc: A natural from 149 smallholders around the Goro Bedessa drying station in West Guji. The importer's name Burtukaana means orange in Oromiffa, for its round, citric stone-fruit profile with good structure. Peach, star fruit and white tea.

beans.name: 062 Edilberto Coronado - Colombia Tabi Washed
beans.producer: Bellavista farm, Santa Maria, Huila; Edilberto Coronado (exporter Cuatro Vientos)
beans.desc: A washed Tabi from Bellavista, a 3-hectare farm in Santa Maria, Huila, run by Edilberto Coronado for over 30 years, with about 13,000 coffee trees among fruit trees and vegetables. Apricot, caramel and almond.

beans.name: 061 Diima Bensa Odako - Ethiopia Heirloom Natural
beans.producer: Bombe, Bensa; Tariku Kare Banata (556 smallholders)
beans.desc: A fruit-forward natural filter coffee from Bombe in Bensa, collected from 556 smallholders by Tariku Kare. Diima means red in Oromiffa. Strawberry, banana and rock sugar.

beans.name: 056 PB Wamuguma - Kenya Washed
beans.producer: Wamuguma washing station, Ritho Farmers Cooperative, Kiambu (Gatundu)
beans.listedNotes: Red grapes, roses, iced black tea
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan filter coffee from the Wamuguma washing station of the Ritho Farmers Cooperative, sorted to peaberry only. Red grapes, roses and iced black tea.

beans.name: 032 San Sebastian - Colombia Castillo Washed
beans.desc: A balanced, reliable washed Castillo filter coffee from Colombia, part of LIFT's year-round Core Collection, made with careful farm management, selective picking and wet-milling. Plum, stone fruit and brown sugar.

beans.name: Cooperage Brazil
beans.listedNotes: Creamy milk chocolate, toasted hazelnut, sweet caramel, subtle dried fruit
beans.desc: A smooth, sweet and very easy-drinking Brazilian coffee from family-owned farms in Cerrado Mineiro, roasted medium-dark in small batches in Cornwall. Full body, very low acidity and a soft, lingering finish, with creamy milk chocolate, toasted hazelnut, sweet caramel and subtle dried fruit.

beans.name: Kamcha House Blend
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, sweet caramel, toasted nuts, hint of warm spice
beans.desc: Limak's signature everyday house blend of Brazilian arabica and Ugandan robusta, roasted medium in small batches in Cornwall and balanced enough for espresso, cafetiere or filter. Medium-full body, low acidity and a clean, sweet finish, with milk chocolate, caramel and toasted nuts.

beans.name: Colombian Peaberry
beans.listedNotes: Milk chocolate, sweet caramel, juicy red berries, soft citrus
beans.desc: A single-origin peaberry from Huila and Cauca in Colombia, roasted medium-dark in small batches in Cornwall. Peaberries are the single round beans found in 5 to 10% of cherries, which concentrates flavour. Medium-full body and balanced acidity with milk chocolate, caramel, juicy red berries, soft citrus and a long, sweet, nutty finish.

beans.name: Yoshi Honduras
beans.listedNotes: Golden honey, red apple, stone fruit, milk chocolate
beans.desc: Named after the founder's cat, a sweet and approachable Honduran coffee from the highlands of Copan and Santa Barbara, roasted medium in small batches in Cornwall to keep the fruit and honey. Medium body and gentle acidity with golden honey, red apple, ripe stone fruit and soft milk chocolate.

beans.name: Bandido Colombian Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark milk chocolate, sweet caramel, toasted pecans, hint of red fruit
beans.desc: A signature 100% Arabica blend of Colombian coffees from Huila, Narino and Caldas, roasted medium-dark in small batches in Cornwall for those who love a deeper, more intense cup. Full body and medium-low acidity with dark milk chocolate, sweet caramel, toasted pecans and a hint of red fruit.

beans.name: Nela Uganda Robusta
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, toasted walnut, molasses, warm spice
beans.desc: A high-grown robusta from the slopes of Central Uganda, strong and bold but smooth, without a harsh bite. Higher-altitude growing adds sweetness and complexity, and it has about twice the caffeine of arabica. Very full body, low acidity and a heavy finish with dark chocolate, toasted walnut, molasses and warm spice.

beans.name: Zibby CO2 Decaf
beans.listedNotes: Creamy milk chocolate, sweet caramel, soft nuts
beans.desc: A 100% Arabica decaf roasted in St Austell, decaffeinated with the natural CO2 process to under 0.1% caffeine. Medium body and low acidity, with creamy milk chocolate, sweet caramel, soft nuts and a clean finish.

beans.name: Colombia Sidra
beans.listedNotes: Red berries, stone fruit, jasmine, honey, citrus zest
beans.desc: A rare, high-grown Sidra hybrid from Huila, Colombia, where slow ripening at altitude builds sweetness and floral depth. Roasted light-medium in small batches in Cornwall, it has medium-full body and bright, sparkling acidity with red berries, stone fruit, jasmine, honey and citrus zest.

beans.name: Tico Costa Rica
beans.listedNotes: Bright orange and citrus, toasted almond, sweet caramel, hint of vanilla
beans.desc: A clean, bright and well-balanced fully washed Arabica from Tarrazu, Costa Rica, roasted medium-light in small batches in Cornwall to keep its lively character. Medium body and crisp acidity with bright orange and citrus, toasted almond, sweet caramel and a hint of vanilla.

beans.name: Limini Blend
beans.desc: A full-bodied espresso blend of coffees from Brazil, El Salvador and India with a naturally sweet caramel flavour and muted acidity. Suited to strong espresso, milk drinks and frappes.

beans.name: Limini Blend Dark Roast
beans.desc: A stronger, richer-bodied dark roast of the Limini Blend, roasted dark without tasting burnt, with caramel and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Kata
beans.desc: A medium-bodied two-bean blend of Guatemalan and Cerrado Brazilian coffee with soft acidity and a maple-like sweetness. Suited to silky espresso, easy-drinking milk drinks and strong filter coffee. Pecan, toffee and milk chocolate.

beans.name: Rimini Blend
beans.listedNotes: Rich dark chocolate, nougat in milk drinks
beans.desc: A full-bodied, complex dark-roast espresso blend with very low, smooth acidity. Rich dark chocolate, with a nougat note in milk drinks. Suited to rich espresso, milk drinks and very strong filter coffee.

beans.name: Liscio
beans.desc: A sweet, complex blend of Brazilian, Costa Rican and Indonesian coffees with a velvety body and berry and stone-fruit aromas. Berry, vanilla and milk chocolate. Suited to complex espresso, fruity milk drinks and lively filter coffee.

beans.name: Blue Mountain Blend
beans.desc: An easy-drinking, smooth blend of Brazilian and Salvadoran coffees intended to echo Jamaica Blue Mountain. Honey and mellow plums. Suited to sweet espresso, easy milk drinks and light filter coffee.

beans.name: Brazil Fazenda Pinhal
beans.desc: A natural Mundo Novo from Fazenda Pinhal in Sul de Minas, Brazil, grown at around 1,000 m. Chocolate, hazelnut and caramel with low acidity.

beans.name: Colombia Medellin
beans.desc: A fully washed supremo-grade coffee from Medellin, Colombia, made from Caturra, Typica and Bourbon. Milk chocolate, nutty and sweet.

beans.name: Costa Rica Tarrazu San Rafael
beans.desc: A washed Strictly Hard Bean coffee from Tarrazu, Costa Rica, roasted medium. Smooth, with dark chocolate and plums.

beans.name: El Salvador Santa Ana
beans.desc: A washed Pacamara and Bourbon from Potrero Grande Arriba in Santa Ana, El Salvador, fermented for 8 hours and dried on clay patios at 1,500 m. Sweet plums and chocolate.

beans.name: Ethiopia Limu
beans.producer: Limu, Oromia, south-west Ethiopia; six farms
beans.desc: A fruity, sweet and winey Ethiopian coffee from six farms in Limu, Oromia, grown at around 1,600 m from heirloom varieties.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
beans.desc: A fully washed heirloom from Negele Gurbitu in Yirgacheffe, grown at 1,700 to 2,000 m and roasted light. Earl Grey, whisky and floral notes.

beans.name: Guatemala Antigua
beans.desc: A coffee from the volcanic valleys around Antigua, Guatemala, grown at 1,650 m from Caturra, Bourbon and Typica. Blackberries and sweet chocolate.

beans.name: India Monsoon Malabar
beans.desc: A bold, full-bodied monsooned AA Arabica from Malabar, India, roasted medium-dark. Dark chocolate with a smoky finish and low acidity. New to the range.

beans.name: Indonesia Sumatra Lake Toba
beans.desc: A wet-hulled (Giling Basah) Catimor and Typica from near Lake Toba, Sumatra. Bold, spicy and tobacco-like with low acidity.

beans.name: Kenya AA
beans.producer: Slopes of Mount Kenya and the Aberdare Range
beans.processFull: Fully washed, sun dried up to 21 days
beans.desc: A fully washed Kenyan AA from the slopes of Mount Kenya and the Aberdare Range, sun dried for up to 21 days. Blackcurrant, vanilla and chocolate. New to the range.

beans.name: Rwanda Inzovu
beans.desc: A fully washed Bourbon and Typica from Rwanda, collected from 40 washing stations and 35,000 farmers. Fruity and mild, with cranberries.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Brazil
beans.desc: A Brazilian decaf made with the 100% chemical-free Swiss Water method, roasted medium-dark for espresso machines. Smooth and bold with dark chocolate. Good for lattes, cappuccinos and flat whites, and as strong filter coffee.

beans.name: Mountain Water Decaf - Mexico
beans.producer: Northern Chiapas; smallholders delivering to San Cristobal de las Casas and Yajalon
beans.desc: A Mexican decaf from smallholders in northern Chiapas, decaffeinated with water from Mexico's highest mountain and 99.9% caffeine free. Roasted medium, with milk chocolate, mellow and nutty notes. Good for sweet lattes and medium-strength filter coffee.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Worka Chelbessa Natural
beans.producer: Worka Chelbessa, southern Gedeo; Neguesse Debela
beans.desc: A natural heirloom from Worka Chelbessa in southern Gedeo, Ethiopia, where producer Neguesse Debela opened a first site in 2017 and a second washing station in Danche in 2019. Prized for its juicy body, bright citrus and delicate floral sweetness, with blueberry, passionfruit, blackberry and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Colombia - Sun Kissed Natural
beans.producer: Gaitania, Planadas, south Tolima; Azahar Coffee Company and partner farmers
beans.listedNotes: Sherry, dark rum, raisin, fruity finish
beans.desc: A special natural lot from Azahar Coffee Company and partner farmers in Gaitania, Planadas, south Tolima, most of whom continue a family coffee-growing tradition. Cherries ferment for 38 hours and dry for eight days on raised African beds under canopy. Sherry, dark rum and raisin with a fruity finish.

beans.name: Peru - Cajamarca
beans.desc: A Grade 1 washed coffee from various producers in Cajamarca, northern Peru, with varieties chosen for a specific profile and every lot screened. A well-balanced cup with a fruity, classic espresso finish: cranberry, bitter orange and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Brazil - D'Barbosa Natural
beans.listedNotes: Red grape, strawberry, chocolate, red apple finish
beans.desc: A natural fermented Red Catuai from D'Barbosa Coffee, a Cerrado family farm begun in 1980 and run by Danilo Barbosa, Brazilian Cup of Excellence champions in 2021. Red grape, strawberry and chocolate with a red apple finish.

beans.name: Alma Road - House Blend
beans.desc: The roastery's original house blend, first roasted in 2015 and a local cafe staple, made from Peru, Brazil and Ethiopia coffees. Balanced and approachable, designed to work both black and with milk.

beans.name: Brazil - Finca Pinhal
beans.desc: A natural Catuai and Caturra from Finca Pinhal, a family-run Brazilian farm the roaster visited in 2024. Roasted slightly darker for a smooth, full-bodied, rounded cup with the classic character of Brazilian coffee and no bitterness.

beans.name: Duck's Coffee Blend
beans.desc: A blend created for the sister brand Duck's Hot Subs, roasted to be versatile and consistent. A smooth, balanced cup with enough depth to stand up to milk while staying refined on its own.

beans.name: Decaf - Colombia Jardin
beans.desc: A sugar cane decaf single origin from Jardin, Antioquia, in Colombia's Western Andes, from generational family farming. The decaf process keeps the region's microclimate character, with natural sweetness and an elegant acidity.

beans.name: High View - Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Originally a wholesale espresso blend, named after the Scaynes Hill site where the roastery is based. Smooth, reliable and full-bodied, built to taste consistent across espresso styles, from a Brazilian farm and a washed Ugandan coffee.

beans.name: Guatemala - La Bolsa
beans.desc: A washed Bourbon and Caturra from La Bolsa, a long-established farm in Huehuetenango, Guatemala. A clean, structured cup with vibrant but balanced flavour and a bright, refined profile.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Beshasha
beans.desc: A traditional washed lot of local heirloom varieties from Beshasha in the Jimma region of western Ethiopia, with clarity, floral aromatics and a delicate structure.

beans.name: Colombia - Wayuu
beans.desc: A washed Colombian single origin, smooth and sweet with a clean, approachable cup, and a fresh direction for the roastery after changing supplier.

beans.name: Session Blend - Guatemala and Colombia Half-Caf
beans.processFull: Guatemala washed; Colombia sugar cane decaf
beans.desc: A half-caf blend of washed Guatemala La Bolsa and sugar cane decaf Colombia Atunkaa, made for enjoying coffee at any time of day. Smooth, composed and clean-finishing, with clarity, sweetness and structure.

beans.name: Crawley Town FC - Red Devils Blend
beans.desc: A blend made with Crawley Town FC from three coffee-growing regions: Brazil, Guatemala and Ethiopia. £1 from every bag sold goes to the Crawley Town Community Foundation.

beans.name: Costa Rica - Las Lajas
beans.producer: Sabanilla de Alajuela; Oscar Chacon Solano and Francisca Cubillo
beans.desc: A Black Diamond process coffee from Las Lajas, a family-owned farm and ecological mill in Sabanilla de Alajuela run by third-generation producers Oscar Chacon Solano and Francisca Cubillo. Pulped with the mucilage intact, fermented anaerobically for 100 hours and dried on raised beds for 15 to 20 days.

beans.name: El Salvador - El Borbollon
beans.desc: A washed blend of lots from 19 RFA-certified farms in the Apaneca-Ilamatepec range, including the slopes of the Santa Ana Volcano, selected by the Alvarez family and head cupper Luis Rodriguez. Fermented overnight, patio dried for 8 to 10 days, then rested and hand sorted at the mill.

beans.name: Maratona Blend
beans.desc: An equal-parts blend of Brazil El Fumo and Honduras El Dulce, pairing hazelnut with a subtle sweetness and finishing with chocolate and caramel.

beans.name: Black Gold Blend
beans.desc: The roastery's first blend: hard-hitting Colombian with the subtle smoothness of high-altitude Guatemalan. Well balanced and full-bodied, with blueberry and chocolate.

beans.name: Colombia Laguna
beans.producer: Northern Cauca (Cafe del Norte), incl. Suarez
beans.desc: The one with the kick: a lively, washed Colombian from the Cafe del Norte area of northern Cauca, grown by about 17,000 families across eight municipalities, 99% on under 5 hectares. Bright citric acidity, recommended for flat whites. SCA 84.5.

beans.name: Colombia Laguna Oscuro (Dark Roast)
beans.desc: A darker-roasted version of Colombia Laguna for those who want a bolder cup. Washed, 84.5 SCA, with citrus, blueberry and lime.

beans.name: Brazil El Fumo
beans.desc: A smoky, nutty washed Brazilian, roasted slowly at a low temperature and suited to both filter and espresso. SCA 82.5.

beans.name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Selasa
beans.desc: A high-grade, balanced washed Yirgacheffe, one of the roastery's favourites, good in milk drinks like flat whites and cortados and on its own as espresso or americano. SCA 83.25.

beans.name: Swiss Water Decaf - Brazil
beans.desc: A Brazilian decaf from Minas Gerais made with the Swiss Water Process, which uses only heat and water, grown under Rainforest Alliance practices. Medium-dark roast, SCA 82.75.

beans.name: Cold Brew Blend
beans.desc: Ground coffee made for cold brewing: steep with cold water in the fridge for 12 to 24 hours for a sweet, non-acidic cup suited to iced drinks.

beans.name: Nicaragua Blueberry Candy
beans.desc: A Great Taste Award 2024 winner from La Bastilla Coffee Estate in Nicaragua, with oodles of blueberries in every sip and gentle florals that suit pour over. Hand-picked very ripe and dried in two stages at a low, steady temperature. SCA 85.5.

beans.name: Honduras El Dulce
beans.producer: Cocafelol cooperative; Finca Las Toreras (Edgar Dubon)
beans.desc: A sweet, high-grade washed Honduran with a natural caramel flavour, good for people who usually add sugar. From the Cocafelol cooperative, including shade-grown Finca Las Toreras (Edgar Dubon). SCA 83.5.

beans.name: Rwanda Kinini
beans.producer: Rulindo, Northern Province; Kinini Mountain Coffee
beans.desc: A bright, fruity natural from Kinini Mountain Coffee in Rulindo, Northern Province, processed at the Kinini washing station with 633+ farmers across 252 hectares. A roaster favourite that gives espresso a fruity strawberry-syrup edge. SCA 86.5.

beans.name: Colombia Danilo Perez La Cabana 120
beans.producer: El Agrado, Huila; La Cabana (Perez family)
beans.desc: A natural from La Cabana, a family farm in El Agrado, Huila, where Danilo Perez runs the experimental lots. Ripe cherries are floated and hand-sorted, fermented anaerobically for 120 hours in sealed barrels turned daily, then silo dried for eight days. Silky body with red fruit, cocoa and port-like depth.

beans.name: Kenya Ruera Estate
beans.desc: A sweet, juicy natural from Ruera Estate, about 190 hectares of red volcanic soil in Kiambu County. Hand-picked ripe cherries are floated, fermented in airtight wraps on raised beds, then dried thinly for about four weeks.

beans.name: St Mocha Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, berries, brown sugar, dark fruits
beans.desc: The roastery's signature blend of washed coffees from Kenya, Guatemala and Colombia, roasted fresh in Balmaha on East Loch Lomond. Silky smooth with rich, chocolatey depth and a bright hint of blackberry sweetness.

beans.name: Brazil - Fazenda Pantano
beans.producer: Fazenda Pantano, Cerrado Mineiro; Jorge Fernando Naimeg (via Ally Coffee)
beans.listedNotes: Rich dark chocolate, caramel sweetness, cooked fruit acidity
beans.desc: A natural Yellow Catuai from Fazenda Pantano, a mountainous farm in Brazil's Cerrado Mineiro, roasted fresh in Balmaha. A rich, caramel-sweet cup with nutty notes and a cooked-fruit acidity to balance.

beans.name: Speciality Decaf - Colombia Mustafa Estate
beans.producer: Finca Mustafa Estate; Ana Mustafa (La Real Expedicion Botanica collective)
beans.desc: A washed sugarcane (EA) decaf Castillo from the Mustafa Estate in Colombia, run by Ana Mustafa and bought direct through the La Real Expedicion Botanica farmer collective. Roasted fresh in Balmaha, with cocoa, honey and sweet fruit.

beans.name: Colombia - Las Mercedes Washed
beans.producer: Finca Las Mercedes, southwest Antioquia; Guerra family
beans.desc: A washed coffee from Finca Las Mercedes in southwest Antioquia, farmed by the Guerra family for 150 years, with about 236 of its 386 hectares kept as native forest and watershed preserve. For drinkers who want more fruit in the morning cup: smooth, with brown sugar and orange peel.

beans.name: Guatemala - Hunbatz Community Lot
beans.desc: A Guatemalan community lot from Hunbatz, roasted fresh in Balmaha. Bright, with dark chocolate and red apple.

beans.name: Costa Rica - Aquiares Estate
beans.desc: A Costa Rican coffee from Aquiares Estate, roasted fresh in Balmaha, with spiced notes of cinnamon and cloves and a candied orange sweetness.

beans.name: Instant Coffee - Timor-Leste
beans.desc: A premium washed, freeze-dried instant coffee from Timor-Leste, one of the world's youngest coffee-producing regions, which the roastery sources from to help fund social projects and sustainability in local communities. Each sachet makes one 250ml cup, with sticky toffee and rum and raisin notes.

beans.name: Market Yard Espresso Blend
beans.desc: Named after Deptford Market Yard, where Lomond began, this espresso blend has been roasted for over 12 years in small batches at the all-female roastery. Cocoa, hazelnut, caramel and blackcurrant.

beans.name: Royal Greenwich Espresso Blend
beans.desc: A rich, full-bodied espresso blend with a hint of fruitiness, to enjoy black or with milk, made from Guatemalan, Colombian and Kenyan coffees (the Kenyan adds citrus) and roasted in small batches at the all-female roastery.

beans.name: El Buho Sugarcane Decaf - Colombia
beans.desc: A single-origin Colombian decaf from Tolima and Huila, made with the ethyl acetate (sugarcane) method using high-mountain spring water. Subtle fruitiness, a nutty body and a smooth, lightly sweet finish, with golden syrup, nuts and lemon.

beans.name: Brazil - Fazenda Paraiso
beans.desc: A pulped natural from Fazenda Paraiso in Brazil, roasted in small batches at the all-female roastery. Full body, natural sweetness and balanced acidity, with dark chocolate, cherry and raisin. SCA 84.

beans.name: Kenya - Thunguri AA
beans.desc: A fully washed Kenyan AA from the southern slopes of Mt Kenya, hand-picked red ripe, wet milled the same day, fermented, washed and sun dried. Recommended for filter, with blackcurrant, forest fruits and lemon. SCA 87.

beans.name: Guatemala - Huehue
beans.desc: A washed coffee from the Huehuetenango highlands of western Guatemala, smooth and chocolatey with balanced sweetness, good for espresso or pour over. SCA 83.75.

beans.name: Honduras - Copan
beans.desc: A strictly high-grown washed coffee from the Cafescor co-operative in Honduras, smooth and well rounded with a fruity body and chocolate undertones. SCA 82.25.

beans.name: Colombia - La Reforma (14-Day Fermented)
beans.producer: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta; Huber Quintana
beans.desc: A vibrant, juicy 14-day fermented coffee from Huber Quintana, a third-generation farmer in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, with bright tropical notes and a delicate berry finish. SCA about 85.75.

beans.name: Colombia - El Porvenir
beans.producer: El Porvenir farm, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta; Isaid Guerrero Torres
beans.desc: A natural from El Porvenir farm, grown by third-generation farmer Isaid Guerrero Torres in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. Rich and indulgent, with high sweetness and a velvety body, like rum and raisin ice cream. SCA 86.

beans.name: Ethiopia - Aricha Wubanchi
beans.desc: A high-altitude fully washed Yirgacheffe heirloom from about 1,700 smallholders, processed at the Aricha Wubanchi washing station at 2,213 m. Best served black and excellent as cold brew, with lemonade, pomegranate and floral notes and apricot behind. SCA 86.

beans.name: Colombia - Toad Bella Vista (13-Day Fermented)
beans.producer: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta; Rubin Pianeta
beans.desc: A 13-day fermented coffee from third-generation farmer Rubin Pianeta in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, roasted in small batches in Camberwell. Smooth and fruity, with molasses, sweet spices, marzipan and liquorice. SCA 85.5.

beans.name: London Calling Coffee Blend
beans.listedNotes: Chocolate biscuit, butter, marzipan, butterscotch, hazelnut, apricot
beans.desc: A 100% Arabica blend of Brazil Mogiana, Colombia Huila and Honduras. It opens with chocolate biscuit, butter and smooth marzipan, then moves to a rich butterscotch and hazelnut finish, with a syrupy body and a golden crema.

beans.name: London Calling Decaff
beans.listedNotes: Rich walnut, dark cocoa, creamy mouthfeel
beans.desc: A decaf of Brazilian and Vietnamese Arabica and Robusta, roasted as beans in 227g bags. Rich walnut and dark cocoa with a creamy mouthfeel.

beans.name: Colombian Alma (Swiss Water Decaf)
beans.origin: Peru (per page details; name says Colombian)
beans.source: Lone Wolf Mountain Coffee product page
beans.desc: A Swiss Water Process decaf: all the flavour and none of the buzz, for late-night drinkers and caffeine-sensitive coffee lovers. A smooth, satisfying medium roast with milk chocolate, caramel and almond that lets you unwind without the caffeine crash.

beans.name: Brazilian Bacano
beans.source: Lone Wolf Mountain Coffee product page
beans.desc: A versatile everyday Brazilian medium roast grown at about 1,100 m on Mundo Novo, Catuai and Acaia varieties. A silky body with chocolate and nut notes and a strong crema, good morning or afternoon.

beans.name: Homestay Blend
beans.brew: Espresso, French press, drip filter, baking and cocktails
beans.source: Lone Wolf Mountain Coffee product page
beans.desc: A medium-strength, full-bodied blend of beans from across the Americas, made for everyday morning and afternoon coffee as well as coffee cocktails, desserts and baking. Chocolate, caramel and nutty notes.

beans.name: Mexican A Huevo Decaf
beans.source: Lone Wolf Mountain Coffee product page
beans.desc: A smooth, balanced medium-roast Swiss Water decaf from Mexico for all-day drinking without caffeine. Nutty and citrusy on the nose, with rich chocolate and bright lemon.

beans.name: Bariso - Ethiopia
beans.desc: An anaerobic natural heirloom from Belaneh Bariso in the Bombe area of Sidama, slowly dried on raised beds. Juicy, with tropical fruit and berry notes, honeyed sweetness and lively acidity. Roasted as an omni-roast, the same profile for filter or espresso, so you adjust brew ratios instead.

beans.name: Martinez Gesha - Colombia
beans.desc: A washed Gesha from producer Jose Martinez, who focuses on careful cultivation and selective picking rather than complex processing. A poised cup with a silky body and long finish: jasmine, white peach and bergamot, with honey and soft citrus.

beans.name: Copey II - Costa Rica
beans.desc: A Black Honey Gesha from Finca Copey, bought by the Solis Cordero family to build a farm where coffee, forest and agriculture support each other. Leaving fruit on the seed during drying adds sweetness and texture while keeping the Gesha's elegance: jasmine, ripe tropical fruit, candied citrus and honey, with a silky finish.

beans.name: Kihuyo - Kenya
beans.producer: Kihuyo Factory, Othaya Farmers Cooperative, Nyeri
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from the Kihuyo Factory of the Othaya Farmers Cooperative in Nyeri, where smallholders combine their harvests. Blackcurrant, grapefruit and panela sweetness with lively acidity and a long, juicy finish.

beans.name: Sanchez - Colombia
beans.desc: A washed Pink Bourbon from Demetrio Sanchez, who focuses on healthy trees, careful picking and slow cherry maturation. Pink Bourbon may share ancestry with Ethiopian landraces, which could explain its floral character and bright acidity: mandarin, raspberry, blossom and soft panela sweetness.

beans.name: Mutambu - Burundi
beans.desc: A washed Red Bourbon from Mutambu Hill, where smallholder families deliver cherry to a local washing station (partner Migoti Coffee), on cool slopes above Lake Tanganyika. Slow ripening gives concentrated sweetness and bright acidity: crisp citrus, red berries and black tea with a silky body.

beans.name: Rojas - Colombia
beans.producer: Chorro Alto, Huila; Luz Angela Rojas
beans.desc: An anaerobic natural Chiroso from Luz Angela Rojas at Chorro Alto in Huila, fermented for 48 hours under 25C and gently dried at 38C. Floral and tropical, with mango, melon, peach and jasmine and a juicy, honeyed sweetness.

beans.name: Peng Editions #16 - White Honey Geisha
beans.producer: Finca El Placer, Quindio; Sebastian Ramirez
beans.desc: A luxury white honey Geisha from Sebastian Ramirez at Finca El Placer in Quindio, anaerobically fermented for 48 hours then slowly shade dried with a thin layer of mucilage. Sweet, vivid and astonishingly clean, with jasmine, lavender, white grape, citrus and a honeyed mouthfeel. Cup score 90.
beans.priceBasis: 200g per spec table (100g per description) (one-time purchase)

beans.name: Peng Editions #15 - Sidra Bourbon
beans.producer: Quebraditas Coffee Farm, Oporapa, Huila; Edinson Argote
beans.listedNotes: Turkish delight, rose water, lime, berry
beans.desc: A washed Sidra from Quebraditas Coffee Farm in Oporapa, Huila, managed by Edinson Argote and family. Floated, thermal-shock washed and fermented for 36 hours with hybrid yeast, then rinsed cold and dried for 76 hours. Turkish delight, rose water, lime and berry. Cup score 90.

beans.name: Peng Editions #13 - Colombia Decaf
beans.desc: A natural sugarcane decaf Castillo from Cofinet, the Colombian producer founded by Carlos and Felipe, a shade under the roastery's 90-point criteria but allowed in as a decaf. Raspberry, Turkish delight and strawberry ganache.

beans.name: Mira - Colombia
beans.producer: El Jaragual farm, Antioquia; Jorge Mira
beans.desc: A washed Caturra from Jorge Mira at the 150-hectare El Jaragual farm in Antioquia, where forestry and coffee are combined. Yeast-inoculated, fermented for 48 hours, thermal-shock washed and dried for 76 hours. Tropical fruit, elderflower, vanilla and cinnamon. Cup score 89.

beans.name: Decaffeinated
beans.desc: A seasonal speciality-grade Arabica decaf, decaffeinated with the sparkling water process and roasted to order slightly darker than usual for extra body while keeping the natural fruit flavours. A strong seller that rarely disappoints.

beans.name: Good Times Blend
beans.desc: A heavy, rich three-bean blend of Brazilian, Indonesian and Central American coffees, poured in many coffee shops across the UK. An easy-drinking crowd-pleaser.

beans.name: Blue Monday Blend
beans.desc: The roastery's first coffee and still its bestseller, a classic, reliable medium roast with subtle fruity flavours and rich chocolate notes.

beans.name: Chime Blend
beans.desc: A luxurious blend heavy on El Salvador, with a creamy, richly textured mouthfeel and good body, and milk chocolate creaminess. More James Bond than James Brown.

beans.name: Weekender - Roasters Blend
beans.desc: The team's go-to morning blend, built on a Sumatran foundation that gives weight and power.

beans.name: Mad World Blend
beans.listedNotes: Dark chocolate, blackberry, prune, orange liquorice
beans.desc: An expert blend with a mix of flavours and a dreamy orange liquorice finish: dark chocolate, blackberry and prune.

beans.name: Honduras - Carlos
beans.producer: Corquin, Copan; Carlos Alfredo Estevez (El Supte)
beans.desc: A washed coffee from Carlos Alfredo Estevez, a second-generation farmer and trained agronomist at El Supte in Corquin, Copan, who advises his neighbours on nutrition, fermentation and drying. Cherries are floated and dried on beds for 20 to 30 days.

beans.name: El Salvador - Finca Bosque Lya
beans.producer: Finca Bosque Lya; Gustavo Vides Valdes
beans.desc: From Finca Bosque Lya, a just-under-100-hectare estate founded by Gustavo Vides Valdes, nearly a third of it natural rainforest, and a Cup of Excellence first-prize winner. Mostly Bourbon with experimental Pacamara, Caturra and Typica. Red berries, tea rose and a chocolate finish.

beans.name: Sumatra - Bener Meriah
beans.listedNotes: Red fruits, cloves, dark chocolate, tamarind
beans.desc: A full-bodied coffee from richly fertile volcanic land at high altitude in Bener Meriah, Sumatra, fermented for 12 hours and sun dried. Smartly integrated red fruits, cloves, dark chocolate and tamarind; recommended as a V60 pour over.

beans.name: Ethiopia Haru
beans.processFull: Natural, raised-bed dried up to 21 days
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A shade-grown natural from various smallholders in Yirgacheffe, handpicked and processed together at the Haru washing station, then dried on raised beds for up to 21 days. Roasted light-medium for filter brewing. Blueberry, pear and vanilla.

beans.name: Kenya Kapcheseny
beans.producer: Slopes of Mt Elgon; Kapcheseny Farmers' Cooperative
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Kenyan from the Kapcheseny Farmers' Cooperative, founded in 2024 by about 62 farmers each tending around 400 trees on the slopes of Mt Elgon in deep red volcanic soil. Deeply fruity and complex, good through any filter or espresso and recommended for flat whites. Blackberry, jam and port.

beans.name: The Fermentation Project - Guatemala
beans.producer: Finca San Miguel Urias, Antigua Valley; Hector and Lilian Leal
beans.processFull: Experimental: four process options (demucilaged, wild, lactobacillus, yeast)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Part of James Hoffmann's Fermentation Project: one Guatemalan coffee from Finca San Miguel Urias in the Antigua Valley (Hector and Lilian Leal), processed four different ways at the El Jaguar washing station: mechanically demucilaged, wild fermented, lactobacillus inoculated and yeast inoculated. Each 48 hours submerged. Roasted light to medium.

beans.name: Bloomsbury Blend
beans.producer: Sao Paulo region (Brazil); southern Rwenzori Mountains near Kisinga (Uganda)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A best-selling espresso blend of natural Brazilian Mundo Novo and washed Ugandan coffee, good black or with milk, and featured in The Times and Sunday Times Top 50 Foods and Drinks. Chocolate, nuts and citrus.

beans.name: Guatemala - The Lioness (La Leona)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: La Leona, grown by a producer collective in the San Marcos region on volcanic soils for clean, elegant notes. Roasted slightly fuller to bring out hazelnut, brown sugar and toffee sweetness.

beans.name: Mexico Zaju
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A limited restock from a single sack found in the roastery, from Finca Guadelupe Zaju, which Eduardo (Teddy) Estave took over in 2004 and has restored. Roasted longer for a richer, darker profile, best as espresso, moka pot or cafetiere. Dark molasses and allspice.

beans.name: Noel - Christmas Blend
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A medium-roasted blend of Brazilian Sao Lucas with a Colombian coffee fermented with cherry fruit. Rich and chocolatey with a subtle sweet cherry note and a creamy finish, like Black Forest gateau. Best as espresso, moka pot or cafetiere.

beans.name: 1839 Blend
beans.producer: Fazenda Sao Lucas and select Brazilian lots
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: The first coffee Lost Barn launched, named after the storm that blew a barn off the roastery's land in 1839. A best seller for espresso or cafetiere: smooth and balanced with cocoa and caramel. Beans from Fazenda Sao Lucas plus select Brazilian varietals.

beans.name: Brazil Bom Jesus
beans.producer: Fazenda Bom Jesus, Cristais Paulistas, Alta Mogiana
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A smooth, syrupy natural Catuai from Fazenda Bom Jesus in Cristais Paulistas, Alta Mogiana, grown by Gabriel and Flavia Lancha Oliveira, founding members of the Alta Mogiana Speciality Coffee Association. Rainforest Alliance and UTZ certified, with 140 hectares of natural reserve. Walnuts and maple syrup.

beans.name: Colombia Cherry Co-Ferment (Limited Edition)
beans.listedNotes: Sweet cherry, caramelised red fruits, floral
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Fresh cherries are added during a 48-hour anaerobic fermentation, then the coffee is de-pulped, washed and dried. From Jairo Arcila, a third-generation Quindio grower who bought Finca La Esmeralda in 1987. Sweet cherry with caramelised red fruits and subtle florals.

beans.name: Colombia Papayo (Limited Edition)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A limited-edition Papayo, a varietal that arose as a natural mutation and whose elongated beans resemble a papaya. Cherries get 45 hours of aerobic fermentation and 10 to 15 days of drying. Roasted lighter for filter. Pineapple and papaya.

beans.name: Colombia Peach Co-Ferment (Limited Edition)
beans.processFull: Co-fermented with peaches (48h dry anaerobic), washed
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: Peaches are added during 48 hours of dry anaerobic fermentation, then the cherries are pulped, washed and dried, passing the fruit's flavour to the coffee. From Quindio grower Jairo Arcila. Summery, sweet and fragrant, best black.

beans.name: Colombia Villa Betulia (Limited Edition)
beans.producer: Finca Villa Betulia; Luis Anibal Calderon
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A natural Yirgacheffe-type varietal, more typically found in Ethiopia, grown at Finca Villa Betulia by second-generation farmer Luis Anibal Calderon. Roasted lighter for filter. Red fruits, floral and honey, a treat while stocks last.

beans.name: Costa Rica La Chumeca (Limited Edition)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A well-rounded, balanced, fruit-forward coffee from La Chumeca, a farm committed to regenerative agriculture that makes only natural coffees with varying fermentation styles. Anaerobically fermented in an oxygen-free tank with yeast extract before drying. Papaya, plum and vanilla.

beans.name: India Ratnagiri (Limited Edition)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A single estate Catuai from Ratnagiri, founded in 1920 and run by Ashok Patre, processed with the hybrid Hydro Honey method: partly dried, rehydrated, de-pulped, then dried 31 days with most mucilage intact. A lighter roast with strong sweetness: honey puffs and sweet milk.

beans.name: Irish Whiskey Barrel Aged Coffee - Brazil
beans.producer: Fazenda Bom Jesus, Cristais Paulistas, Alta Mogiana
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A collaboration with Thomond Gate Whiskey: natural Brazilian beans from Fazenda Bom Jesus aged for two months in French oak barrels that previously held port and then whiskey. Vanilla, toffee and whiskey.

beans.name: Brazil Decaffeinated
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: An organically certified Brazilian decaf made with the chemical-free Swiss Water method. Rich and sweet with chocolate, creamy and nutty.

beans.name: Lost Session Blend
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A blend of speciality-grade single origins from Brazil and Colombia, made for drinking cup after cup in one sitting. Toasted nuts and chocolate.

beans.name: Rescue Blend (Limited Edition, supports NEWSAR)
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A blend of two of the roastery's best-selling single origins from Brazil and Sumatra, an all-rounder for cafetiere, moka pot or espresso. All profits go to NEWSAR (North East Wales Search and Rescue). Biscuit and dark chocolate.

beans.name: Brazil Peaberry
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A natural Brazilian peaberry, about 5% of the harvest separated from the main crop, from some of Brazil's highest plantations. Smooth and nutty with a subtle acidity.

beans.name: Brazil Sao Lucas
beans.producer: Fazenda Sao Lucas; Lucas Lancha de Oliveira
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A natural Mundo Novo from Fazenda Sao Lucas, grown by sixth-generation farmer Lucas Lancha de Oliveira. Smooth and nutty, best as espresso or cafetiere, with peanuts and caramel.

beans.name: Uganda Buzira (formerly Kisinga)
beans.producer: Southern Rwenzori Mountains; Kisinga washing station
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Ugandan from the southern Rwenzori Mountains, hand-picked from surrounding farms, sun dried on raised beds and processed at the Kisinga washing station. The roastery buys through a social enterprise that funds community and environmental projects. Bold and juicy with peach, apricot and tart cherry.

beans.name: Colombia La Leona
beans.source: Lost Barn Coffee Roasters product page
beans.desc: A washed Caturra from Luz Helena Salazar. Cherries are picked at strict ripeness, floated, hand-sorted, fermented underwater for 30 hours, then pulped, washed and dried in controlled conditions. Medium roasted for maximum sweetness, good for espresso drinks, with berries, stone fruit and toffee.

pods.name: Ambush Forest Pods
pods.desc: Ambush is a mix of top-grade Ethiopian beans with fruity and lavender flavours, popular brewed as V60 and refined into a fruity, sweet blend for any time of day. Each box holds ten compostable pods.

pods.name: Italiano Vero Pods
pods.desc: A popular authentic Italian-style espresso with intense melted chocolate and toasted nut flavours, for a strong straight shot or silky milk drink. Each box holds ten biodegradable pods.

pods.name: Decaf Coffee Pods (Swiss Water)

pods.name: Home Compostable Espresso Capsules
pods.desc: Nespresso-compatible pods in plant-based, renewable materials certified for home and industrial composting, with an oxygen barrier for freshness. An aromatic cup with caramel and chocolate from Brazilian and Peruvian beans.

pods.name: Home Compostable Decaffeinated Capsules

pods.name: BS1 Espresso Capsules

guides.why: Clean and clear: brings out florals, fruit and acidity.
steps: Rinse the paper filter with hot water and tip the water away.
Add the coffee and gently level the bed.
Pour about 40 g of water to wet all the grounds. Wait 30–40 seconds while it bubbles (the bloom).
Pour slowly in small circles up to 150 g by 1:15.
Keep pouring to 250 g by about 1:45, then give the dripper a gentle swirl.
Let it drain. Aim to finish between 3:00 and 3:30. If it runs faster, grind finer; if slower, grind coarser.

guides.why: Forgiving and versatile: works for nearly any coffee.
steps: Rinse the filter in the cap and set the AeroPress on your mug.
Add the coffee, then pour all 220 g of water.
Stir three times, put the plunger in loosely to stop dripping, and wait until 2:00.
Swirl gently, then press down slowly for about 30 seconds.
For a stronger cup, use 18 g of coffee. For a softer, less bitter cup, use water a few degrees cooler.

guides.why: Rich and full-bodied: suits chocolate, nutty and caramel notes.
steps: Add the coffee to the press and pour all 500 g of water.
Leave it for 4 minutes without stirring.
Break the crust on top with a spoon and scoop off the foam.
Wait another 4–5 minutes so the fine particles sink.
Press the plunger only to the surface of the coffee, then pour gently. Leave the last bit in the pot.

guides.why: Concentrated and sweet: ideal for milk drinks and chocolatey coffees.
steps: Weigh 18 g of coffee into the basket and level it.
Tamp firmly and evenly.
Lock in and start the shot straight away.
Stop at 36 g in the cup (a 1:2 ratio). Aim for 25–30 seconds.
Sour or thin? Grind finer. Bitter or harsh? Grind coarser. Light roasts often taste better at 1:2.5.

guides.why: Strong and bold: a stovetop take on espresso-style coffee.
steps: Fill the base with just-boiled water up to the valve.
Fill the basket with coffee and level it without pressing down.
Screw it together using a tea towel, as the base will be hot.
Heat on a medium-low flame with the lid open.
When the coffee turns pale and starts to sputter, take it off the heat and run the base under cold water to stop it.

guides.why: Very clean and tea-like, thanks to its thick filter. Great for sharing.
steps: Place the filter with the thick, three-layer side towards the spout and rinse it well.
Add the coffee and pour 60 g of water to bloom. Wait 45 seconds.
Pour in slow circles to 300 g.
Once it drops a little, pour to 500 g.
Aim to finish at 4:00–4:30. Remove the filter and give the coffee a swirl.

podTips.Nespresso Original: Ristretto (25 ml) for intensity 9+, espresso (40 ml) for most, lungo (110 ml) for light, fruity capsules.
podTips.Nespresso Vertuo: The machine reads the barcode and sets the cup size, so just pop it in.
podTips.Dolce Gusto: Use the strength lever: fewer bars for brighter capsules, more for darker ones.
podTips.Tassimo: The machine reads the barcode. Descale regularly, as it strongly affects taste.
